records.title: Host genotype-microbiota-metabolome interactions modulate semen quality in Holstein bulls.
records.abstract: Semen quality is critical for reproductive performance in dairy cattle; however, its microbial, metabolic, and genetic bases remain poorly understood. We integrated rumen microbiota, metabolome, and genome-wide variation from 55 Holstein bulls stratified into relative semen quality high (RSQH) and relative semen quality low (RSQL) groups based on semen quality records to investigate host-microbiome-metabolome interactions associated with fertility. The rumen microbiota was dominated by Bacteroidota, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria, while Fibrobacter (phylum Fibrobacterota) was enriched in RSQH bulls and positively associated with sperm motility and density. The metabolome distinguished the two groups with 64 discriminatory metabolites, including elevated N-acetyl-L-phenylalanine and prostaglandin H2 in RSQH and sebacic acid in RSQL. Machine learning models were used to prioritize microbial and metabolic features, identifying candidate markers that may contribute to differences in semen quality. Fibrobacter, thromboxane B2, and N1-[4-(cyanomethyl)phenyl]-4-chlorobenzamide emerged as candidate indicators of semen quality, supported by machine learning, high heritability, and genome-wide association study signals. Overall, 511 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were jointly associated with Fibrobacter and these metabolites, including six significantly linked to sperm motility based on GWAS analysis. These SNPs were grouped into two contrasting types, with C1-type variants showing decreasing trends and C2-type variants showing increasing trends in semen quality-related traits. Structural equation modeling revealed that C2-type variants were positively associated with semen traits through microbial and metabolite enrichment, whereas C1-type variants were negatively associated with them. These findings highlight coordinated host genetic, microbial, and metabolic contributions to semen quality in Holstein bulls and provide candidate biomarkers for fertility-related research and breeding.ImportanceImproving bull fertility is important for reproductive efficiency in dairy production, but the biological factors underlying semen quality remain incompletely understood. This study shows that variation in semen quality in Holstein bulls is associated with coordinated differences in rumen microbiota, metabolites, and host genetic variation. In particular, Fibrobacter, thromboxane B2, and N1-[4-(cyanomethyl)phenyl]-4-chlorobenzamide emerged as promising indicators of semen quality. These findings provide a basis for future fertility biomarker research and may support the development of genetics- and microbiota-informed strategies for bull selection and reproductive management.
records.authors: Ju Z, Jiang Q, Li Y, Zhang Y, Xiao Y, Zhang Y, Wang X, Wei X, Gao Y, Yang C, Liu W, Wang J, Huang J.

records.title: Genetic Characterization of Avian Influenza H14 Viruses in Guangdong, China: Evidence of Intercontinental Transmission and Reassortment in the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.
records.abstract: AbstractH14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. This study investigated the ecological origins and zoonotic potential of H14 viruses in southern China. Active surveillance was conducted in Guangdong (2022-2025). The isolates underwent full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Receptor binding specificity for avian- and human-type receptors was evaluated using a solid-phase assay. In vitro replication was assessed in avian, mammalian, and human cell lines. In vivo pathogenicity was evaluated in mice. In this study, four H14 AIVs (one H14N6, two H14N7, and one H14N8) were isolated. We identified a novel H14 transmission network involving Mareca penelope and multiple shorebird species (Tringa, Himantopus), suggesting a multihost dispersal mechanism. Phylogenetically, the Guangdong isolates formed a distinct subclade within the Eurasian lineage, closely related to strains from Russia and Cambodia. Importantly, the three isolates (SZ3742/H14N6, ZJ3523/H14N7, and SZ3536/H14N8) exhibited dual receptor-binding specificity, recognising both avian-type (α-2,3) and human-type (α-2,6) sialic acids. Replication in human A549 cells was strain-dependent: SZ3742/H14N6 reached a peak titre comparable to that in DF-1 cells but lower than that in MDCK cells, whereas ZJ3523/H14N7 and SZ3536/H14N8 reached lower peak titres than in both reference cell lines. All three tested isolates replicated transiently at low titers in mouse lungs with limited viral pathogenicity, despite reduced fitness in human A549 cells. Molecular characterization revealed key mammalian adaptation markers and a typical HA cleavage site motif (PDKQTR↓GLF). This study provides the first evidence of H14 AIV circulation in Guangdong Province, China. The virus demonstrates a broad host range in migratory birds and possesses genetic markers associated with mammalian adaptation, highlighting the need for increased surveillance in the East Asian‒Australasian Flyway.
records.authors: Liu J, Li Y, Huang R, Yao Q, Yang Q, Shen X, Ge Y, Gao Y.

records.title: Host species identity drives temporally stable octocoral microbiomes in Florida.
records.abstract: Octocorals are foundational components of Caribbean reef ecosystems, yet their bacterial microbiomes remain poorly characterized compared to scleractinian corals. We present an extensive 16S rRNA gene survey of western Atlantic octocoral microbiomes, characterizing 180 samples from four co-occurring South Florida species over three years: the encrusting species Briareum asbestinum and Erythropodium caribaeorum, and the branching species Eunicea flexuosa and Muricea muricata. Host species identity was the strongest predictor of microbiome composition, explaining 14.4% of bacterial community variation, while temporal and spatial factors contributed less than 2% each. Core microbiome analysis at three prevalence thresholds (80, 90 and 100%) revealed host-specific bacterial associations. All four species harbored largely host-specific Endozoicomonas ASVs as dominant core members, with encrusting species maintaining larger and more taxonomically diverse cores than branching species. Phylogenetic reconstruction placed the dominant Endozoicomonas ASVs among described Endozoicomonas species, three lineages related to E. euniceicola, which was described from Florida octocorals, while the dominant Mycoplasma ASVs were highly divergent from described type strains, suggesting undescribed octocoral-associated lineages. Differential abundance analysis identified only a few significant temporally or spatially variable ASVs, reinforcing overall community stability. These findings demonstrate strong host control over microbial associations and provide a phylogenetic framework for understanding octocoral-bacteria symbioses in the western Atlantic.
records.authors: Liberman R, Gómez-Corrales M, Lopez JV.

records.title: Biosensor-guided genome-wide CRISPR screens enable  cis  ,  cis  -muconic acid overproduction in yeast
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Classical pathway metabolic engineering relies on enhancing strain productivity through the introduction of rationally identified genetic perturbations, which while useful, are time-consuming and miss unintuitive targets. Genome-wide CRISPR screens offer an alternative by efficiently sampling genomes, enabling the engineering of novel phenotypes, and are further enhanced when combined with high-throughput strain interrogation methods. Here, using  Saccharomyces cerevisiae , we engineered small molecule biosensors into population enrichment tools using zeocin resistance and fluorescence as signal outputs. We then introduced the multi-functional genome-wide CRISPR (MAGIC) library that targets every gene for activation, interference, or deletion, thus creating biosensor-aided MAGIC, or senMAGIC. As a case study, we utilized senMAGIC to identify single genetic determinants that improve productivity of the nylon precursors protocatechuic and  cis ,  cis -muconic acids (PCA and ccM). These were then randomly assembled as triple gRNA-tRNA arrays for multiplexed gene perturbations to identify combinatorial effects. Top gRNA hits were then confirmed using direct genomic integrations in senMAGIC-free production strains, resulting in identifying known as well as novel targets that increase PCA and ccM titres. Our results demonstrate senMAGIC as a robust automation-friendly whole-genome evolution tool and highlight limitations of the method, providing a roadmap for future multifunctional CRISPR screens to optimize host metabolism for efficient bioprocesses.
records.authors: Nasr MA, Knoops A, Thornbury M, Davies M, Kwan DH, Martin VJ.

records.abstract: An oil-degrading enrichment culture was inoculated from Marine Oil Snow (MOS) collected during an oil-spill experiment at the Churchill Marine Observatory in winter 2024. The complete metagenome-assembled genome for  Paraperlucidibaca sp. CMO1 was reconstructed, exhibiting the genetic potential to degrade hydrocarbons, including alkanes and aromatic compounds, as well as the ability to produce surfactants.

records.title: Resurrecting host–microbiome interactions: combining resurrection ecology and microbiome transplants to test temporal local adaptation
records.abstract: Host-associated microbiomes can influence fitness, respond rapidly to environmental change, and potentially contribute to host adaptation. Yet, determining whether host–microbiome associations evolve adaptively over ecological timescales remains challenging because historical host genotypes and their associated microbial communities are rarely available for experimental comparison. Resurrection ecology offers a means of recovering historical host genotypes from dormant propagules, while microbiome transplantation provides an experimental approach for testing the effects of microbial communities on host performance. Combining these approaches could enable direct tests of temporal local adaptation in host–microbiome associations. Freshwater Daphnia provide a promising model because their dormant eggs can persist in lake sediments, allowing historical host genotypes to be resurrected. However, the microbiota associated with dormant eggs may originate from multiple sources, including ancestral hosts, lake water, and surrounding sediment, complicating the recovery of historically associated microbial communities. We outline a framework combining sediment archives, host resurrection, microbiome characterisation, and reciprocal transplantation experiments to test whether historical and contemporary hosts perform better with microbiomes from their respective time periods. We discuss the conceptual predictions, methodological challenges, and experimental controls required to distinguish temporal local adaptation from microbial environmental effects, host-genotype specificity, and changes in community composition. This framework could extend resurrection ecology beyond host evolution to experimentally investigate the historical evolution of host–microbiome interactions.
records.authors: Paplauskas S, Frisch D.

records.title: Transpolar Drift and Atlantic inflow shape microbial biogeography and metabolic processes across the central Arctic Ocean
records.abstract: Abstract  The Arctic Ocean is changing rapidly. Sea-ice loss, advancing Atlantification and terrigenous inputs create contrasting ecoregions, yet their underlying microbial processes remain unresolved. Here, we combine high-resolution oceanographic observations and multi-omics data from the North Pole to the Svalbard shelf to determine how the shift from terrigenous influence to Atlantic-dominated waters shapes microbial biogeography, community assembly and metabolic processes. We demonstrate distinct, lifestyle-specific differences in microbial communities across four hydrographic regimes, with particle-attached communities showing a predominantly stochastic distribution while free-living communities were more regime-dependent. In the terrigenous-influenced Amundsen Basin, particle-attached microbial communities drive degradation of recalcitrant terrigenous organic matter with enrichment in denitrification, suggesting potential net nitrogen loss. Moving into Atlantic-dominated waters in the Nansen Basin during late summer, free-living communities increasingly rely on mixotrophic scavenging, trace gas oxidation and marine organic matter cycling as waters become progressively more nutrient-depleted. Surface-driven photoheterotrophy prevails in the warmest, ice-free waters. Comparative genomics across the Arctic Ocean further demonstrates highly connected yet regionally adapted microbial communities governed by these distinct hydrographic regimes. These results offer a mechanistic view of how microbial metabolic processes may restructure as the region becomes seasonally ice-free, Atlantification intensifies, and terrigenous inputs increase, thereby reshaping biogeochemical cycling across the Arctic Ocean.

records.title: Reconstruction of contact signals from repeated elements with Hicberg.
records.abstract: Throughout evolution, genomes have acquired various repetitive elements, such as transposons, ribosomal DNA, duplicated genes, and tandem repeats. These sequences pose significant challenges to current high-throughput sequencing pipelines, which generate short reads that cannot be unambiguously mapped to reference genomes. We present an innovative algorithm, Hicberg, designed to leverage reads typically discarded by standard pipelines. Hicberg employs statistical inference coupled with probability distribution computation to accurately infer missing 3D contacts of repetitive elements within a genome from paired omic data, such as Hi-C data. Our results demonstrate that Hicberg provides new insights into the potential impact of repetitive elements on the spatial organization of genomes. Notably, we observed the positioning of molecular motors that create chromosomal loops associated with certain transposons in yeast. These findings underscore the importance of an integrative approach to better understand genomic complexity and pave the way for deeper explorations of repeated elements.
records.authors: Gradit S, Ortion S, Larrous P, Delouis M, Koszul R, Cournac A.

records.title: SwinePan for pig graph-based pangenome and multiomics data mining.
records.abstract: Pigs are one of the most important livestock species worldwide. Although multiple high-quality reference genomes exist, reliance on a single linear reference limits the detection of structural variants (SVs) and the characterization of population-specific genetic diversity. To address this limitation, we developed SwinePan, a comprehensive and integrated multiomic database for pigs built on a graph-based pangenome framework. SwinePan incorporates a variome derived from the graph-based pangenome, covering 2598 individuals across 35 breeds, including 185,759 SVs, 117 million SNPs, and 6.8 million indels. The database also integrates transcriptomic data from liver, loin muscle, abdominal fat, and backfat, along with more than 150,000 phenotypic records. The online toolkit deployed in SwinePan enables genome-wide association studies (GWAS), expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) mapping, and colocalization, whereas interactive modules visualize population structure and multiomic associations, streamlining candidate gene and variant exploration. Additionally, two proof-of-concept analyses demonstrate how SwinePan pinpoints trait-associated loci and deciphers their potential regulatory mechanisms.
records.authors: Lin M, Liu L, Cai G, Huang S, Qiu Y, Yao Z, Deng S, Wang S, Liu Y, Ruan D, Zhou F, Wu J, Zhang Z, Zheng E, Yang J, Wu Z.

records.title: Iron-associated functional differentiation between granules and flocs enhances resilience and phosphorus recovery in a CEPT-PDA treating low-strength wastewater.
records.abstract: Carbon fluctuations destabilize microbial ecosystems by disrupting metabolic interactions, yet how community heterogeneity drives resilience remains unclear. Using a CEPT-PDA system, we show that iron associates functional differentiation between granules and flocs under alternating COD disturbances. High‑COD shocks allowed recovery within 5-7 days, whereas low‑COD starvation required 12-15 days. Iron accelerated recovery, achieving NH4+‑N (99.1%), PO43-‑P (70.0%), and TN (99.2%) average removal rate. Mechanistically, iron promoted niche differentiation: granules sustained anammox (Candidatus. Brocadia, 33.3%), while flocs supported denitrification (Thauera, 50.1%). Metagenomics revealed distinct Fe utilization: granules enhanced Fe(II) transport, flocs enriched Fe(III) uptake, iron-sulfur cluster assembly, and denitrification-related pathways. Iron also sequestered P as ferric phosphate and vivianite. Thus, iron acts as an ecological regulator that reorganizes microbial resource use and spatial functional differentiation, enhancing resilience to carbon fluctuations while enabling nutrient removal and recovery.
records.authors: Sun X, Tang M, Gu P, Cao S, Du R, Peng Y.

records.title: BAHD acyltransferase ApAT2 catalyzes the acetylation of protostane-type tetracyclic triterpenes in Alisma plantago-aquatica.
records.abstract: Alisma plantago-aquatica L. is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb used to treat urinary disorders. Acylated protostane-type tetracyclic triterpenes such as alisol B 23-acetate and alisol C 23-acetate are its major bioactive components and have been reported to exhibit improved antiviral activities. However, the content of these compounds is relatively low in plants, and the enzyme that catalyzes this acetylation process has not yet been identified. In this study, we constructed a transcriptome dataset for A. plantago-aquatica. Using co-expression analysis and enzyme activity screening, we successfully identified a benzyl alcohol O-acetyltransferase, anthocyanin O-hydroxycinnamoyltransferase, anthranilate N-hydroxycinnamoyl/benzoyltransferase, deacetylvindoline 4-O-acetyltransferase (BAHD), ApAT2. This enzyme catalyzes the acetylation of alisol B and alisol C but does not exhibit any catalytic activity toward alisol A. Molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis confirmed that the M412 residue of ApAT2 played a critical role in its substrate specificity. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that the active pocket of ApAT2 possibly diverged via lineage-specific evolution, conferring specificity for protostane-type tetracyclic triterpenes. Furthermore, we established a semi-biosynthetic platform in Escherichia coli expressing ApAT2 to produce alisol B 23-acetate from alisol B. In conclusion, we identified the BAHD enzyme responsible for the acetylation of protostane-type tetracyclic triterpenes, thus providing new systems to produce these valuable compounds. We also identified a new molecular basis for the recognition and modification of diverse substrates by the BAHD family during plant evolution.

records.title: Identification and functional characterization of pineapple AcGPX5 in oxidative stress response.
records.abstract: Pineapple (Ananas comosus), a globally significant crop, stands as the world's third most important tropical fruit. Throughout its extensive domestication history, mitotic recombination has contributed to the formation of terminal homozygosity regions on chromosomes. However, the functional genomic landscape and biological significance of these regions remain largely unexplored. In this study, we systematically investigated these regions. Functional enrichment analyses revealed that genes residing within these regions are predominantly associated with critical biochemical processes, including ADP binding, oxidoreductase activity, response to oxidative stress, and the catabolic metabolism of macromolecules. Utilizing transcriptomic profiling across fruit developmental stages, we classified these genes into five distinct clusters, each exhibiting unique expression patterns. Notably, genes within these clusters showed significant transcriptional dynamics during fruit ripening, suggesting a coordinated regulatory role in this process. Among these genes, AcGPX5, a cluster 1 gene, was identified as a strong candidate because of its markedly high expression levels during fruit development. To elucidate its functional role, we characterized AcGPX5 in terms of sequence architecture, predicted protein structure, and subcellular localization. Additionally, we conducted preliminary functional validation through enzyme activity assays and transgenic experiments. The enzyme activity assays confirmed that recombinant AcGPX5 possesses thioredoxin-dependent glutathione peroxidase activity, while multiple transgenic assays demonstrated that AcGPX5 plays an essential role in plant oxidative stress resistance. Collectively, this study identifies a set of ripening-related candidate genes embedded in chromosome terminal homozygosity regions and functionally characterizes AcGPX5 as a representative member. These findings advance our understanding of pineapple genome evolution and domestication and provide an experimental basis for exploiting these unique genetic resources in crop improvement.
records.authors: Guo LN, Liu BQ, Liu YY, Nie L, Liu XX, Li X, Fu BL, Chen LY.

records.title: In silico characterization of copy number variation (CNVS) in Renibacterium salmoninarum genomes from farmed salmonids.
records.abstract: Renibacterium salmoninarum is a highly clonal intracellular pathogen responsible for bacterial kidney disease (BKD) in salmonids. Although previous studies have demonstrated limited genomic diversity within this species, the contribution of copy number variations (CNVs) to its genomic variability remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed CNVs in 41 Chilean R. salmoninarum isolates recovered from Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) and Coho salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch) hosts using short-read sequencing data mapped against the genome of the type strain ATCC 33209. CNVs were detected throughout the chromosome and comprised both duplications and deletions. While the overall CNV burden was not significantly associated with lineage, geographic origin, or year of isolation, CNV profiles differed significantly between host genera. Specifically, duplications were more frequent among isolates recovered from Oncorhynchus spp., whereas deletions occurred more frequently in isolates derived from S. salar. Functional annotation identified host-associated genomic differentiation in CNV patterns, including variation affecting the dCTP deaminase gene, which plays a key role in nucleotide metabolism. Collectively, these findings reveal that CNVs constitute an additional source of genomic variation in R. salmoninarum and highlight patterns of host-associated genomic differentiation whose biological significance remains to be determined.
records.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
records.authors: Sandoval A, Avendaño-Herrera R, Gallardo-Escárate C, Valenzuela-Miranda D.

records.title: Computational identification of EBNA1-binding candidates using machine learning-based virtual screening and molecular docking.
records.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is associated with several malignancies and multiple sclerosis, and Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) plays an essential role in viral genome replication and episome maintenance. The experimentally characterized KVD-associated pocket within the EBNA1 DNA-binding domain provides a structurally defined site for computational ligand prioritization. This study aimed to identify and prioritize predicted EBNA1-binding candidates using an integrated machine-learning and structure-based virtual screening framework. A PubChem EBNA1 bioactivity dataset comprising 304,124 records was curated to obtain 4,584 unique compounds. Molecular representation combined 1,024-bit Morgan fingerprints with 11 RDKit molecular descriptors. Random Forest, SVM-RBF, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost models were evaluated using scaffold-based independent testing. The optimized XGBoost model was applied to a non-overlapping DrugBank library of 12,287 compounds. Compounds with predicted activity probabilities ≥0.5 were subjected to Lipinski-based filtering, followed by molecular docking against the KVD-associated binding pocket of EBNA1 (PDB ID: 6NPM). Docking validation was performed by independent KVD redocking at exhaustiveness values of 8, 16, and 32. Post-docking candidates were further evaluated using PAINS, aggregation, frequent-hitter/promiscuity, assay-interference, redox-associated structural-alert, and ADMET assessments. XGBoost demonstrated the highest test-set ROC-AUC (0.835), PR-AUC (0.408), and best Brier score (0.067), and was selected for virtual screening. Screening identified 116 compounds above the probability threshold, of which 40 satisfied Lipinski criteria and were docked. Thirty-two compounds achieved docking scores ≤ -7.0 kcal/mol. Sequential liability assessment and integrated prioritization identified 10 computationally prioritized EBNA1-binding candidates with favorable combined machine-learning, docking, and structural-filter profiles. The integrated computational framework enabled systematic prioritization of structurally diverse predicted EBNA1-binding candidates for further experimental investigation. The identified candidates represent computationally prioritized molecules for subsequent biochemical and functional evaluation of EBNA1 binding and activity and should not be interpreted as experimentally validated antiviral or disease-modifying agents.Graphical abstractVirtual screening for drug discovery using trained ML model for EBNA1 protein, Molecular Docking, and ADMET analysis.
records.authors: Pauskar AP, Natarajan E.

records.title: Local hydrology and seasonality outweigh the influence of Phragmites australis on coastal bacterial communities across two Baltic Sea bays.
records.abstract: BackgroundAquatic macrophytes shape microbial habitats in shallow coastal systems, yet the relative influence of plant-driven effects versus local hydrology and seasonal environmental variation remains poorly resolved. We investigated how Phragmites australis influences sediment, water, and phyllosphere bacterial communities in two shallow Baltic Sea bays, Haapsalu and Pärnu, that are approximately 83 km from each other.ResultsBacterial communities clustered strongly by substrate (sediment, water, and phyllosphere). Sediments exhibited higher 𝛼-diversity and stronger site specificity than water or phyllosphere habitats, with bulk sediments harboring greater richness than Phragmites-associated sediments. Seasonal 𝛼-diversity peaked in summer-autumn and reached minima in spring across sediments, whereas water communities showed weaker seasonality. β-diversity analyses revealed that sediments maintained lower seasonal turnover (i.e., more temporally stable) and site-specific communities compared to water and phyllosphere habitats, which showed rapid compositional shifts and higher seasonal dissimilarity. Pärnu Bay, which experiences stronger riverine influence, exhibits larger temporal shifts in both 𝛼- and β-diversity than Haapsalu Bay. Taxonomic differences between bays included the dominance of Cyanobium in Haapsalu Bay and Synechococcus in Pärnu Bay, most likely driven by site-specific hydrology and nutrient regimes. After accounting for environmental gradients, P. australis had only modest, context-dependent effects on the bacterial community composition.ConclusionsLocal hydrology and seasonal variation, particularly riverine inputs and salinity dynamics, exert stronger control over coastal bacterial community composition in top-layer sediment and water than the presence of P. australis. While sediments act as relatively stable, site-specific reservoirs, water, and phyllosphere communities were more labile and seasonally dynamic. These findings underscore the importance of site-specific assessments in shallow coastal studies and caution against generalizing results across bays.
records.authors: Ercoli F, Tammert H, Kisand V, Blank K, Kivistik C, Herlemann DPR.

records.title: Integrative transcriptomic and gut microbiota analysis reveals thermal stress-induced physiological regulation in the narrow-clawed crayfish Pontastacus leptodactylus.
records.abstract: This study systematically investigated the effects of acute temperature stress on transcriptional levels and gut microbiota in the narrow clawed crayfish (Pontastacus leptodactylus). GO enrichment analysis showed that upregulated genes were significantly enriched in biological process terms (chitin-based cuticle development, vacuolar acidification, and lysosomal lumen acidification), the cellular component term sarcomere, and molecular function terms (structural constituent of cuticle and proton channel activity). In contrast, downregulated genes were primarily associated with normal growth and development, exoskeleton mineralisation, and enzymatic degradation processes, such as molting cycle, chitin breakdown, and skeletal mineralisation, indicating suppression of routine physiological activities under stress conditions. KEGG pathway analysis further showed that upregulated genes were significantly enriched in apoptosis, gap junctions, mTOR signaling, and Toll like receptor pathways, reflecting activation of cellular defense and immune regulatory networks. In contrast, downregulated genes were mainly enriched in oxidative phosphorylation and thermogenesis, suggesting impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism. RT-qPCR validation of 14 representative DEGs strongly agreed with transcriptomic data, confirming the results' reliability. Meanwhile, alpha-diversity analysis of the gut microbiota revealed numerically higher Chao1 and observed species richness estimates but lower Simpson and Shannon diversity indices under acute temperature stress, although none of these differences reached statistical significance (all P > 0.05). At the genus level, acute temperature stress substantially increased the relative abundances of Hafnia-Obesumbacterium, Enterobacter, and Raoultella, while dominant genera such as Prevotella and Agathobacter declined significantly, as confirmed by LEfSe analysis. Functional prediction results indicated a significant increase in proportions of biofilm formation, stress tolerance, and potentially pathogenic bacterial phenotypes in the stressed group, along with notable reductions in the relative abundances of multiple KEGG orthologs and COG functional categories, suggesting a reduction in predicted gut microbial functional potential. Overall, acute temperature increased profoundly reshaped the transcriptional expression profile and intestinal microecological structure of the narrow-clawed crayfish, providing essential molecular and microbiological insights into its adaptive mechanisms to acute high temperature.
records.authors: Li Y, Tay YJ, Han M, Yao Z, Li B, Lv M, Li Y, Gao P, Cheng Z, Lai Q.

records.title: Genome-wide selection signatures in Turkish Awassi sheep: uncovering the genetic basis of production traits and adaptation.
records.abstract: The Awassi sheep is one of the leading fat-tailed breeds of the Fertile Crescent, known for its high milk yield and resilience in arid and semi-arid environments. Despite its socio-economic importance, a high-resolution genomic characterization of selection signatures in Turkish Awassi populations remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the genomic diversity, demographic history, and selection signatures of Turkish Awassi sheep using double-digest restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing (ddRADseq). Genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) discovery was performed on 40 unrelated Awassi sheep. Genetic diversity parameters, historical effective population size ( Ne ), and linkage disequilibrium (LD) decay were assessed. Selection signatures were identified using both runs of homozygosity (ROH) islands and Tajima's D analyses, followed by functional annotation of candidate genes. A total of 397 315 high-quality SNPs were identified. The average minor allele frequency (MAF) was 0.333, and the ROH-based inbreeding coefficient ( FROH ) was low (0.025), indicating high genetic integrity. The historical Ne showed a consistent decline, reaching 147 in the most recent generations. Selection signature analysis identified 21 and 48 protein-coding genes by means of ROH and Tajima's D , respectively. The key candidate genes were associated with milk yield and lactation (AKR1C3, AKR1D1, OXT, AVP, ZNF131), meat production and growth (PBX1, KBTBD8, HOXA cluster, ADGB), fat-tail formation (HOXA cluster, HMGCS1, STARD4), and environmental adaptation (ABCB1, TSLP, IL6). Our findings reveal that the Turkish Awassi genome is a rich genetic reservoir shaped by combined natural and artificial selection. The selection signatures identified in this study provide fundamental genomic targets for future breeding strategies to enhance productivity without compromising environmental resilience. These findings support the use of Turkish Awassi as a genetic resource for breeding programs in arid and semi-arid production systems.

records.title: A gut symbiotic bacterium enhances baculovirus resistance in Spodoptera frugiperda by maintaining peritrophic matrix integrity.
records.abstract: BackgroundSpodoptera frugiperda is a major agricultural pest worldwide, whereas Spodoptera frugiperda multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus (SfMNPV) serves as an important microbial control agent against this pest. Resident gut bacteria are increasingly recognized as important modulators of insect-pathogen interactions; however, whether and how they influence SfMNPV infection in S. frugiperda remains unclear. We therefore investigated how gut bacteria modulate host resistance to SfMNPV.ResultsAntibiotic-mediated depletion of gut bacteria increased larval susceptibility to SfMNPV. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that gut bacterial depletion downregulated midgut genes associated with immune defense, digestive functions and peritrophic matrix (PM) maintenance. Among seven culturable midgut bacterial isolates, reinoculation with Glutamicibacter soli significantly enhanced larval resistance to SfMNPV. Pre-feeding with either the G. soli culture supernatant or cell lysis precipitate also increased larval resistance and partially reversed transcriptional changes caused by gut bacterial depletion before viral challenge, including the downregulation of peritrophin-1. RNAi-mediated silencing of peritrophin-1 disrupted PM structure, increased PM permeability, and enhanced larval susceptibility to SfMNPV. Consistently, G. soli reinoculation restored PM integrity impaired by gut bacterial depletion.ConclusionThese findings identify maintenance of PM integrity as an important mechanism contributing to gut symbiotic bacterium-mediated resistance to SfMNPV. The study advances our understanding of how gut bacteria influence baculovirus infection in insect hosts and provides potential microbial and molecular targets for improving baculovirus-based pest management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
records.authors: Guo L, Jin W, Kang Q, Tong Y, Shi H, Zhang J, Li X, Wang H, Qin Q, Meng Q, Zhang H.

records.title: A RecBCD-like enzyme regulates expression of bacterial defense operons in response to DNA damage
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Bacteria must quickly respond to stress signals including bacteriophage (phage) infection, invasion by mobile genetic elements, and other threats. DNA damage is a stress-signaling nexus in bacteria, initiating global responses such as the SOS response and triggering expression of specific defense and immune pathways through DNA damage-sensing transcriptional regulators. Here we identify a three-protein pathway termed Cerberus that senses dsDNA ends that become available during DNA damage or inhibition of the key DNA repair complex RecBCD, and controls expression of an associated defense/immune operon. The central player in Cerberus is a large peptidase-helicase-nuclease fusion protein, CerC, that is architecturally similar to the RecBC complex itself. Upon DNA damage or RecBCD inhibition, CerC binds and unwinds free DNA ends to allosterically activate its fused HExxH metallopeptidase domain. CerC specifically cleaves the adjacently encoded anti-sigma factor CerB to release its cognate sigma factor CerA, allowing CerA to mediate transcription of a defense/immune operon encoded nearby. Cerberus therefore represents a pathway that has co-opted a key DNA repair machine for DNA damage sensing, and linked that activity to transcriptional control through anti-sigma factor cleavage.

records.title: Molecular and Structural Characterisation of the MERS-Coronavirus Polymerase
records.abstract: MERS-CoV (Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus) belongs to the  Betacoronavirus genus, which also includes SARS-CoV-2, the causative agent of the COVID-19 pandemic. MERS-CoV is the pathogen responsible for Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS), a respiratory disease with a 36.5% case fatality rate. Given the capacity of coronaviruses for genetic recombination and mutation, MERS-CoV remains a pathogen of significant pandemic potential, with viral evolution potentially facilitating enhanced adaptation and transmission in humans. There are no approved treatments for MERS-CoV infection. The MERS-CoV replication-transcription complex (RTC), a multimeric protein complex key to genome amplification, has no cellular analogues and a highly conserved sequence, making it a useful target for antiviral compounds; however, structural and biochemical characterisation of the MERS-CoV RTC is limited. Here, we characterise the minimal MERS-CoV RTC using in vitro and single-molecule assays and show that it is susceptible to the RNA-dependent-RNA-polymerase inhibitor suramin. We present a structure of the minimal MERS-CoV RTC in complex with an RNA duplex, which shows strong structural similarity to the SARS-CoV-2 RTC. We use cross-subunit swapping experiments to show that the MERS-CoV NSP12 core can efficiently utilise SARS-CoV-2 cofactors NSP7 and NSP8, whereas SARS-CoV-2 NSP12 exhibits reduced in vitro activity with the MERS-CoV NSP8. This asymmetric cross-species compatibility highlights both the evolutionary conservation and virus-specific adaptation of coronavirus polymerase-cofactor interactions. Together, these findings provide a structural and mechanistic framework for understanding MERS-CoV RNA synthesis and establish its conserved RTC as a potential target for the development of broadly acting coronavirus antivirals.  Significance Statement  Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) causes severe respiratory disease and represents a significant pandemic threat because of the capacity of coronaviruses to mutate and recombine. Despite this risk, there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for MERS, and no structure of the essential replication-transcription complex (RTC) has been available. Here, we define the biochemical properties of the MERS-CoV RTC and determine its structure bound to RNA, revealing conserved and virus-specific features of coronavirus replication. We further demonstrate inhibition of the polymerase by suramin. By establishing a structural and functional framework for MERS-CoV genome replication, this work addresses a key gap in our preparedness for MERS-CoV and supports the development of antivirals that could be effective against multiple coronaviruses.
records.authors: Cunnison RF, Philip SS, Deng A, Groves D, Spence AM, Coleman CM, Keown J, Robb NC.

records.title: DNA Analyser: An Interactive Web Server for Integrated Prediction of Local Non-B DNA Structures in Genomic Sequences.
records.abstract: BackgroundLocal non-B DNA structures and R-loops are associated with genome regulation and stability. CpX islands and p53 response elements provide complementary sequence annotations. Exploring these features often requires separate tools and repeated sequence submission.Main findingsDNA Analyser web server integrates G4Hunter, G4Killer, R-loop Tracker, Z-DNA Hunter, pretrained Z-DNABERT models running on CPUs, CpX Hunter and a p53-binding predictor. Palindrome analyser is linked as a separate companion server. Inputs include plain-text or FASTA upload, pasted sequences, multiple-sequence workflows and NCBI retrieval. Outputs include analysis settings, sortable regions, interactive graphics and module-specific exports. Guest and registered users have access to the same analytical functions.Biological relevanceA shared sequence workspace supports examination of structural propensity, nucleotide composition and potential regulatory elements. Predictions identify candidates for further investigation; they do not demonstrate structure formation or biological function in vivo.SignificanceIntegrated access reduces repeated sequence handling and helps researchers explore complementary features of the same genomic region. DNA Analyser is freely accessible through HTTPS without identity registration at https://bioinformatics.ibp.cz/#/.

records.title: New insights on the dual role of viruses favoring microbial survival and pollutant degradation in the rhizosphere.
records.abstract: The rhizosphere is widely recognized as a crucial environment for microbial community assembly and pollutant degradation, with numerous mechanisms already elucidated. However, the role of viruses in these processes remains largely unexplored. Viruses can carry auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), which shape microbial functions through horizontal gene transfer and may play an important role in the rhizosphere. This study investigated microbial and viral community structures, as well as degradation gene profiles, in rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere soils at a PCBs-contaminated site. More microbial functional pathways were negatively correlated with PCBs concentrations in rhizosphere soils, a pattern consistent with potentially greater functional sensitivity to pollutant-associated stress. Meanwhile, viral AMGs associated with antioxidant defense and DNA repair appeared to help microbes resist PCBs toxicity. Notably, viruses also carried potential PCBs degradation genes associated with both aerobic and anaerobic degradation pathways. More putative transfer events involving these degradation-related genes were observed among microbes in rhizosphere soils than in non-rhizosphere soils, suggesting that viruses may play an important role in PCB degradation. The normalized abundance of degradation genes was significantly correlated with that of antioxidant and DNA repair genes, but not with PCBs concentrations. This association is consistent with a possible ecological link between toxicity resistance and degradation potential. This study provides new insights into the role of rhizosphere viruses in organic pollutant degradation and informs the development of strategies to enhance microbial bioremediation efforts.
records.authors: Wang Y, Yan W, Song M, Jiang L, Xie Y, Jin LN, Wang S, Luo C.

records.title: An integrative GWAS, Transcriptomic, and domestication analysis Uncovers Multi-Layered genetic architecture of kernel rate in maize testcross hybrids.
records.abstract: IntroductionImproving yield efficiency in maize (Zea mays L.) is increasingly important under high-density production systems, where gains from total biomass accumulation are approaching physiological limits. Kernel Rate (KR), or shelling percentage, captures reproductive biomass partitioning within the ear but remains less well characterized genetically than absolute yield components.ObjectiveHere, we evaluated KR together with ear weight (EW), cob weight (CW), and kernel weight (KW) in two testcross populations generated with Mo17 and Zheng58 and assessed across six year-by-location environments. KR was highly heritable, showed only weak correlations with EW, and was consistently negatively correlated with CW, supporting its use as an index of relative kernel-to-cob biomass allocation.MethodsTo investigate the genetic basis of this variation, we applied an integrative analytical framework combining testcross-based genome-wide association studies (GWAS), comparative parental-line transcriptomic comparisons associated with extreme F1 testcross performance, and population genomic signals from domestication scans. Rather than identifying a single set of causal genes, this approach revealed limited overlap among data layers, indicating that yield efficiency is shaped by multiple, context-dependent genetic contributions.ResultsGWAS identified multiple trait-associated loci with limited overlap across environments and tester backgrounds; two CW associations also met FDR_BH ConclusionThese results support a multi-layered and context-dependent genetic basis of biomass partitioning in maize testcross hybrids. The integrative framework provides biologically informed candidate priorities for functional validation and breeding across additional testers and environments.
records.authors: Xiong X, Duan H, Ding D, Tang J, Zhang X.

records.title: Design, Synthesis, in silico Studies, and Biological Evaluation of N<sup>4</sup>-Acetyl/Benzoyl Piperazinyl Ciprofloxacin-Amino Acid Conjugates as Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Agents.
records.abstract: This study reports a second-stage optimization of our previously reported ciprofloxacin derivatives through molecular hybridization, with structural modifications aimed at improving antimicrobial potency and activity against resistant strains. Their structures and identities were confirmed by spectroscopic techniques, elemental analysis, and HPLC. In vitro antimicrobial activity showed enhanced potency across a panel of bacterial strains. The derivatives demonstrated promising activity against both wild-type and resistant strains, while the most active derivatives also exhibited promising antimycobacterial activity. The most active compounds were selected for further in vitro and live-cell mode-of-action studies. Several compounds showed biofilm-inhibiting activity against Staphylococcus aureus at sub-MIC. Phenotypic mode-of-action studies indicated topoisomerase inhibition in both Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis. Enzyme inhibition studies revealed potent activity against DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Additionally, the best anti-Helicobacter pylori candidates showed promising urease inhibition. Selected derivatives showed bactericidal activity with minimal resistance development compared with ciprofloxacin. The cytotoxicity study indicated low in vitro cytotoxicity under the tested conditions. Molecular modeling supported favorable binding and inhibitory potential, while QSAR linked physicochemical properties to biological activity, providing mechanistic insights and guiding compound optimization toward improved efficacy and development. Overall, the synthesized ciprofloxacin hybrids showed promising antimicrobial activity and potential to combat bacterial resistance.

records.title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship.
records.abstract: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

records.title: rmf, a conserved ribosome hibernation marker of convergent dormancy in experimentally evolved Escherichia coli.
records.abstract: Bacteria adapt to remarkably diverse chemical stresses, yet how far independent adaptive trajectories converge, and on what, remains poorly defined. We reanalyzed transcriptomes from 188 Escherichia coli lineages evolved under 47 different chemical stresses, 4 M9 controls, and 4 ancestral replicates. We used multiple public data sets to test whether divergent lineages converge on a shared physiological endpoint. Lineages evolved under chemically diverse stresses converged on a shared transcriptional axis, with their expression change positively correlated across chemicals (r = 0.157; P = 0.001). This axis corresponds to a slow-growth, RpoS-governed stationary-phase and ribosome hibernation program, aligning strongly with an RpoS/stationary-phase index (r = 0.97) and inversely with a ribosomal index (r = -0.65). The ribosome modulation factor rmf, which forms translationally silent 100S ribosome dimers, rose along the PC1 axis (r = 0.65) and co-expressed specifically with the 100S hibernation factors hpf, yfiA, and sra. In contrast, its associations with persister toxin-antitoxin, multidrug efflux, and oxidative stress genes were weak or inconsistent. Cross-species analysis supported purifying selection on ribosome modulation factor, and a genome-wide analysis placed rmf within the lowest-diversity 4% of core genes, consistent with convergence through regulation rather than coding change. Neither the axis nor rmf expression tracked the resistance level of the lineages, identifying the program as a conserved state of adaptation rather than a resistance mechanism. These findings recast a canonical stress response program as the convergent endpoint of adaptive evolution and identify rmf as a conserved readout of that state.IMPORTANCEBacteria survive antibiotics not only by becoming resistant but also by entering a dormant, slow-growing state that tolerates drugs, and how predictably different populations reach such a state has been unclear. By reanalyzing Escherichia coli populations experimentally evolved under dozens of chemically distinct stresses, we show that each population acquired largely stress-specific mutations, yet their gene expression profiles converged on a shared dormancy program centered on ribosome hibernation. A single gene, rmf, whose product switches ribosomes off, reliably marked how deeply a population had entered this state, was reproducible across many independent data sets, and was almost invariant across hundreds of E. coli genomes. Because this convergence arose through gene regulation rather than mutation and did not correspond to resistance, rmf offers a simple readout of a dormant state associated with tolerance, a distinction useful for understanding and countering how bacteria survive antibiotics.

records.title: Quantifying microbial fitness in high-throughput experiments.
records.abstract: Few concepts are as central to evolution as is fitness, and yet the quantification of fitness is often ambiguous. In particular, high-throughput experiments to measure mutant fitness in microbes are increasingly common, but vary widely in their definitions of fitness, which makes their results difficult to compare. What are the consequences of these different fitness statistics, and is there a best way to quantify fitness in a given context? Here, we systematize the set of possible fitness statistics according to the following three choices: (1) the encoding of relative abundance (e.g., transforming by a log or logit function), (2) the time scale over which to measure the change in relative abundance, and (3) the choice of a reference subpopulation for calculating relative fitness in bulk competition experiments, such as those using DNA-barcoded mutants. We show that these different choices can lead to significantly different interpretations of mutant fitness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, affecting the magnitude of fitness effects, the apparent presence of epistasis, and even the fitness ranking across mutants. This can confound predictions for evolutionary dynamics and gene functions. Altogether, our results demonstrate the importance of consistent fitness definitions for reproducible results across experiments.
records.authors: Fink JW, Manhart M.

records.title: Accuracy of plasma cell-free DNA PCR versus mNGS for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease.
records.abstract: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) detection in plasma is a novel testing modality for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease (IMD) in immunocompromised patients. The accuracy of PCR compared to metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for diagnosis of IMD remains unknown. Plasma samples from patients with proven and probable IMD and no IMD were tested with mold PCR and shotgun mNGS. Mold PCR detected Aspergillus species, Mucorales agents, Fusarium species, Scedosporium species, and Lomentospora prolificans. The sensitivity and specificity of mold PCR and mNGS were measured. Ninety-four patients with proven (48) and probable (48) IMD due to Aspergillus species (64), Mucorales agents (13), Scedosporium species and Lomentospora prolificans (13), and Fusarium species (6), and 62 patients with no IMD were included in this study. 99.4% (155) of the patients were immunosuppressed. The overall sensitivity and specificity were 62.5% (60/96; 95% CI 52.0-72.2) and 99.8% (535/536; 95% CI 99.0-100), respectively, for mold PCR and 43.8% (42/96; 95% CI 33.6-54.3; P P = 1.0), respectively, for mNGS. The proportion of mold PCR-positive mNGS-negative results was 16.0% (4/25) in focal cases compared with 25.0% (11/44; P = 0.384) and 18.5% (5/27; P = 0.810) in multifocal and disseminated cases, respectively. The median PCR cycle threshold was 40.6 (IQR, 37.5-41.5) in PCR-positive mNGS-negative cases compared with 37.3 (IQR, 34.5-39.3; P = 0.004) in PCR-positive mNGS-positive cases. Plasma cfDNA PCR is more sensitive than mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD in immunocompromised patients. Lower sensitivity of mNGS was associated with lower mold cfDNA burden.ImportanceInvasive mold disease (IMD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised patients. Early diagnosis and initiation of tailored antifungal therapy are critical for optimizing outcomes in patients with IMD. Detection of circulating fungal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in the acellular fraction of blood is a novel testing modality that is increasingly used for early and non-invasive diagnosis of IMD. This study represents the first head-to-head accuracy study to compare the sensitivity and specificity of PCR with mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD. The study showed that the overall mold PCR was significantly more sensitive compared with mNGS, while both assays demonstrated very high specificity. Similar trends were observed in a smaller subgroup of patients with invasive aspergillosis, mucormycosis, and scedosporiosis. The findings have implications for assay selection when seeking to non-invasively diagnose IMD in immunocompromised patients.
records.authors: Pusz-Bochenska K, Murugesan K, Senchyna F, Lalljie A, Budvytiene I, Banaei N.

records.title: Short-tailed Salmonella Phage SWJM-03: Isolation, Characterization, and Application in Controlling Contamination on Lettuce.
records.abstract: AimsSalmonella enterica, a major cause of foodborne outbreaks associated with ready-to-eat leafy greens, like lettuce, poses urgent challenges to food safety. In this study, a lytic phage, SWJM-03, was isolated and evaluated for its potential as a biocontrol agent against Salmonella contamination in lettuce.Methods and resultsPhage SWJM-03 was isolated from sewage using multidrug-resistant Salmonella Typhimurium 2112 as the host, and its biological characteristics, genomic features, antibiofilm activity, and biocontrol efficacy on lettuce were evaluated. Phage SWJM-03 is classified within the genus Berlinvirus, class Caudoviricetes. The phage exhibited a short-tailed morphology and demonstrated rapid adsorption (92.7% within 20 min), a short latent period of 5 min, and a burst size of 97 PFU/cell. SWJM-03 showed high stability across a wide pH range (3-12) and retained high activity within a temperature range of 30-60°C relevant to food processing conditions. Notably, SWJM-03 also exhibited great storage stability, with minimal titer reduction after 4 weeks at 4°C, supporting its practical applicability. Genomic analysis (39 474 bp dsDNA, 48.97% G + C, GenBank Accession no.: OQ818670) confirmed the absence of virulence-associated genes. SWJM-03 significantly reduced biofilm biomass of S. Typhimurium by 56.8%, and demonstrated promising biocontrol potential. Importantly, in a simulated lettuce contamination system under refrigeration (4°C), SWJM-03 achieved up to 4.00 log₁₀ CFU/cm² reduction within 3 days, reducing bacterial counts below detectable levels (ConclusionsPhage SWJM-03 is a rapid-acting and environmentally stable lytic bacteriophage with strong antibacterial activity under refrigeration conditions, highlighting its potential as a promising biocontrol agent for controlling Salmonella contamination in fresh produce.
records.authors: Zhang L, Huang N, Pan H, Shu M, Li J, Zhong C, Wu GP.

records.title: The Genetic Legacy of Thermal Processing in Pasteurized Foods: Persistence of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes, Potential for Horizontal Gene Transfer, and a Proposed Genetic Legacy Index.
records.abstract: Thermal processing inactivates foodborne bacteria but does not necessarily destroy their DNA, membrane vesicles, or bacteriophage particles. Such residues persist in pasteurized milk and heat-treated meat and are ingested by consumers. Whether this material can transfer antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) to gut bacteria remains untested: the only direct human evidence of foodborne resistance-gene transfer involved live bacteria, not material released from heat-killed cells. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the post-thermal fate of extracellular DNA, membrane vesicles, and bacteriophages, grading that evidence explicitly from detection of a target sequence, through structural integrity, to demonstrated transfer under realistic conditions. Persistence of ARG sequences after pasteurization is well documented, whereas functional transfer from foodborne dead-cell material has not been demonstrated in vivo. A Genetic Legacy Index (GLI) is proposed as a conceptual measurement framework-not a validated index-combining extracellular DNA abundance, ARG load, and ARG-mobile genetic element linkage, with an illustrative formula, normalization strategy, and validation agenda. Current finished-product microbiological criteria are predominantly culture-based and do not establish limits for extracellular or dead-cell genetic material, although integrated antimicrobial resistance surveillance increasingly includes molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. The GLI is therefore proposed as a research and surveillance tool rather than a product-release criterion: a first step toward evaluating an unquantified exposure pathway within One Health surveillance of the food chain.
records.authors: Song S, Yan L.

records.title: Born in the wild: the ecological roles of key Enterobacteriaceae virulence factors.
records.abstract: Many Enterobacteriaceae family pathogens are not truly human adapted but are instead opportunists able to thrive in various different niches. Survival in environments outside human hosts provides a means for transmission and also represents an important selective pressure shaping the evolution of these bacterial species. Pathogens such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae benefit from highly diverse genomes and horizontally acquired virulence or host fitness factors that collectively determine infection type and severity. These same "virulence" factors can also drive environmental survival. Here we will review current knowledge of the environmental roles of canonical host fitness factors of opportunistic pathogens, including capsule, siderophores, curli, and type VI secretion systems. These systems are primarily known for their roles in protection, nutrient acquisition, and intermicrobial competition within the host but can also make dramatic contributions to environmental survival. Investigating these roles can give us new perspectives on how these factors may function within the host and help us to understand the evolutionary forces shaping bacterial pathogens.
records.authors: Nunez C, Howells GA, Short FL.

records.title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase.
records.abstract: Intermolecular Diels-Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels-Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic "dark matter". Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.
records.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
records.authors: Meng LH, Wang LY, Ying Z, Li XM, Li X, Yan LH, Wang BG.

records.title: SEARCHLIGHT: A Modular Workflow for High-Resolution Viral Single-cell Genomics.
records.abstract: Single-cell viral genomics is limited by low viral abundance and incomplete genome recovery. We developed SEARCHLIGHT (scRNA-seq-enabled acquisition of mRNA and consensus haplotypes linking individual genotypes and host transcriptomes), a modular workflow that improves recovery of viral cDNA from standard 10× Genomics 5' single-cell libraries, preserving barcodes for cell-level genome reconstruction. The core Basic Protocol uses virus-specific primers during cDNA synthesis to recover viral sequences from single cells. Two optional modules extend the workflow: SEARCHLIGHT + Kinnex, which increases sequencing depth through cDNA concatenation, and SEARCHLIGHT + Twist + Kinnex, which incorporates hybrid capture to enrich viral cDNA before long-read sequencing. Together, these modules expand recovery from moderate to low-abundance infections and support high-resolution analysis of viral diversity across diverse sample types. SEARCHLIGHT provides a flexible framework for balancing sensitivity, throughput, and cost in single-cell viral genomics. Published 2026. This article is a U.S. Government work and is in the public domain in the USA. Current Protocols published by Wiley Periodicals LLC. Basic Protocol: SEARCHLIGHT core workflow (single-cell viral genomics) Alternate Protocol 1: SEARCHLIGHT + Kinnex Alternate Protocol 2: SEARCHLIGHT + Twist + Kinnex.

records.title: Co-dissemination of anti-phage defence systems and multidrug resistance is associated with the seventh-pandemic Vibrio cholerae defensome.
records.abstract: Anti-phage defence systems in Vibrio cholerae are recognized as cargo on mobile genetic elements carrying antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and virulence genes, but a population-scale view of how the V. cholerae defensome partitions between the pandemic O1 clade and the environmental non-O1 reservoir has been missing. We analysed 1,740 RefSeq V. cholerae genomes (773 O1, 967 non-O1) sampled from 1934 to 2022 across 60 countries. Cataloguing defence systems with DefenseFinder, we found that the non-O1 reservoir harboured 283 subtypes and 55 families absent from any O1. This asymmetry persisted after collapsing each core-genome lineage to a single representative, although it partly reflected the greater diversity of non-O1. O1 favoured abortive infection systems (36.8% vs 14.1% in non-O1; P<0.001). Defence and prophage burden were inversely related within O1 (R=-0.15) but weakly positive in non-O1, and a five-decade reconstruction revealed mirror trajectories of rising defence diversity and declining prophage burden in O1, coincident with SXT/R391 integrative conjugative element-borne AMR. A bipartite network identified strong defence-AMR associations (Phi up to 0.80), nominating AbiE, AbiJ, AvcID, Menshen, Retron-I_A and Lamassu-Fam as candidate co-acquired cargo; though much of this is clonal, the strongest associations falling to 0.51 to 0.68 after de-duplication. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection clustering resolved seven defensome lineages, and a Random Forest classifier trained on defence profile predicted multidrug resistance status with cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.96, generalizing across O1 (0.92), non-O1 (0.93), decades (0.88) and regions (AUC=0.92); a five-system signature (AbiE, BREX-I, CBASS-II, AvcID and AbiJ) achieved AUC=0.91. Together, these data show that the pandemic defensome has expanded in step with the AMR-bearing mobilome rather than with prophage burden, with defence and resistance genes co-inherited on seventh pandemic El Tor elements. Their association reflects shared lineage history rather than a causal or mechanistic link, and the defensome serves as a descriptive genomic correlate of multidrug resistance.

records.title: Archaeal histones coordinate conserved DNA sequence motifs to promote CRISPR adaptive immunity.
records.abstract: Archaea and bacteria acquire resistance to viruses by integrating fragments of foreign DNA at the beginning of a CRISPR locus. In the archaeon Pyrococcus furiosus, histones bind the leader to promote specific integration at the first CRISPR repeat. However, it remains unknown whether archaeal CRISPR leaders contain conserved DNA sequence motifs required for integration. Here, we analyze 542 archaeal CRISPR leaders found across Thermococcales and Methanococcales. We identify 36 motifs found up to 500 bps upstream of archaeal CRISPR loci. Scrambling or truncating novel motifs or histone binding sites found 100-400 bps upstream of the P. furiosus CRISPR modestly decreases integration efficiency. However, mutation of motif T2, which overlaps with the proximal histone site and is adjacent to the CRISPR, ablates both histone-mediated and histone-independent integration. Mutations tiled across T2 reveal that a pyrimidine at position -3 of the leader is required for histone-independent integration, and basepairs -4 to -19 are required for histone-mediated integration. T2 is found in most Thermococcales, and a similar sequence is found in most Methanococcales leaders, suggesting this motif may be a broadly conserved element that facilitates CRISPR adaptive immunity across taxonomic orders. These data shed light on the sequence requirements for histone-mediated DNA integration.
records.authors: Patel P, Treat AR, Gonzalez R, Rajaraman S, Cruga BN, Chinea EB, Onwuka A, Nguyen C, Terns MP, Santiago-Frangos A.

records.title: Long Noncoding RNA LINC00941 Links Oncogenic KRAS Signaling to Aggressiveness, DNA Repair, and Chemoresistance in Pancreatic Cancer.
records.abstract: Oncogenic KRAS mutations are the primary drivers of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but the noncoding landscape downstream of KRAS remains to be fully elucidated. Here, by integrating PDAC RNA sequencing and exome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), we identified 49 long intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) differentially expressed according to KRAS mutation status. Among these, LINC00941 emerged as a primary candidate, as its expression is regulated by KRAS in both loss- and gain-of-function models and is significantly upregulated in PDAC tumors. Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing and clinical datasets (TCGA/ICGC) revealed that LINC00941 is significantly enriched in PDAC malignant epithelial cells and correlates with poor PDAC patient prognosis. Functional assays demonstrated that LINC00941 knockdown impairs PDAC cell migration and invasion. Notably, LINC00941-depleted cells exhibit delayed DNA repair following irradiation, as shown by the slower resolution of radiation-induced DNA strand breaks, and increased sensitivity to gemcitabine-induced apoptosis. Transcriptomic and RT-qPCR analyses associated the loss of LINC00941 with a significant reduction in key DNA repair and survival-related genes, including BACH1, TOP2A, and BIRC5. These findings suggest that LINC00941 is required to maintain genomic stability and promote survival under therapeutic stress in KRAS-driven cells. In conclusion, our study identifies a novel KRAS/LINC00941 axis that supports a pro-survival and chemoresistant phenotype in PDAC, positioning LINC00941 as a mediator of the DNA damage response and a potential therapeutic target in PDAC.

records.title: How far can you borrow? Divergence limits of cross-species Gene Ontology enrichment in non-model organisms.
records.abstract: Functional interpretation of omics data from non-model species almost always relies on borrowing Gene Ontology (GO) annotations from a model organism-often a distant one (Arabidopsis for plants, zebrafish or human for fish)-and running enrichment analysis on inferred orthologs. How far this practice can be pushed before the enrichment result degrades has never been quantified at the level practitioners use. We present the first systematic benchmark of the divergence-tolerance of cross-species GO-transfer enrichment, across six focal species spanning three eukaryotic kingdoms, each with 15-22 reference species tiling a continuous phylogenetic gradient. Set-level fidelity-measured as redundancy-robust Wang semantic similarity between transferred and experimental-truth enriched term sets-declines monotonically with distance, collapsing to chance at the clade boundary in some panels (fish, rice) while remaining well above it in others (insect, fungi, mammal) (half-collapse identity, ID50, ~40%-59%). At fixed distance, a richer reference raises recall but lowers precision, quantifying a long-recognized but unresolved trade-off. Conserved processes transfer reliably to distant references whereas taxon-specific processes do not, a pattern consistent across all six focal species tested. Whole-genome duplication degrades transfer only when ohnolog retention is high, showing up as sensitivity to the orthology method rather than a steeper decline. An independent, GO-free measure of expression conservation supports the curves in vertebrates. We condense these results into a focal-species × distance reliability guide and a step-by-step decision protocol that let researchers judge, before analysis, whether borrowed-GO enrichment can be trusted for their species and question.
records.authors: Lee SG, Park C.

records.title: A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.
records.abstract: Accurate detection of Z-DNA-forming regions is limited by the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in sequence-based methods. We present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0-a fast and interpretable protocol that extends Z-DNA Hunter through a dual-scan strategy combined with a fuzzy expert layer. A permissive scan (model 2, minimum length 6 bp, threshold 30%) captures a broad candidate set, while a stringent scan (model 2, minimum length 10 bp, threshold 60%) provides high-confidence support. These outputs are integrated using fuzzy inference incorporating sequence signal, cross-scan support, genomic context, and bias penalties. On the audited 385-locus Shin analysis, the protocol achieves balanced accuracy 0.883 (recall 0.862, specificity 0.904), comparable with the published Z-DNABERT operating point, while alternative modes increase specificity to 0.973. The paired scans are combined by a transparent, configurable prioritization layer with an adjustable recall-specificity trade-off. The local workflow requires only a FASTA (Fast-All sequence alignment format), sequence and transcription start site annotation. The tool is freely available at https://github.com/mifo123/zdna-fuzzy-hunter.
records.authors: Petrovič M, Trenz O, Kledus F, Brázda V, Šťastný J.

records.title: Mining of Small Open Reading Frame-Encoded Peptides from Chlamydomonas nivalis without Its Reference Genome.
records.abstract: Small open reading frame (sORF)-encoded peptides (SEPs) participate in diverse biological processes, yet their identification in nonmodel organisms is limited by the lack of high-quality reference genomes. Here, we developed an integrative proteogenomic pipeline to discover SEPs in Chlamydomonas nivalis by combining sORFs predicted from its transcriptome with those derived from the genomes of the related species, Chloromonas eustigma and Volvox carteri. Using this strategy, we identified 978 endogenous SEPs supported by transcript evidence and 1 999 candidate SEPs supported by cross-species proteogenomic evidence. SEPs predicted from transcriptomic and related-species genomic data showed broadly similar physicochemical and evolutionary features. Importantly, incorporation of related-species genomic data substantially increased identification coverage, with over 95% of SEPs identified through these databases absent from the transcriptome-derived data set. Functional analysis identified several cold-responsive candidates, including an Lhca6-homologous SEP and several intrinsically disordered region-rich SEPs. Heterologous expression of selected candidates in C. reinhardtii further showed that two SEPs enhanced cold tolerance. These results demonstrate the value of integrating transcriptomic and related-species genomic resources for SEP discovery and provide functional evidence for SEP involvement in cold adaptation.
records.authors: Yao S, Peng Z, Liu G, Huang K, Wan C.

records.title: IsoPairFinder: A Computational Workflow for Prioritizing LC-MS Feature Pairs Representing Candidate Microbial Pathway Intermediates from Stable Isotope Tracing Metabolomics.
records.abstract: Functional annotation of microbial genes lags behind the pace of genome sequencing, leaving major gaps in our understanding of microbial metabolism. Combining genetic perturbation with untargeted stable isotope tracing metabolomics provides a powerful strategy for identifying pathway intermediates and elucidating microbial metabolic pathways. To streamline this workflow, we developed IsoPairFinder, a computational tool that prioritizes pathway-intermediate feature pairs by analyzing paired unlabeled (12C) and 13C-labeled metabolomics datasets from genetically perturbed microbes. By consolidating redundant liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) features and pairing features across unlabeled and labeled samples, IsoPairFinder reduces candidate lists to plausible isotope-paired intermediates for downstream validation. We demonstrate the utility of IsoPairFinder in a case study of uric acid catabolism in Clostridium sporogenes, where it filters redundant features and prioritizes LC-MS feature pairs representing gene-associated pathway intermediates. IsoPairFinder is available as an open-source R package and as a web-based workflow within GNPS2. By integrating differential analysis and isotope-pair detection into a single workflow, IsoPairFinder enables microbiologists to connect metabolomic features with microbial gene function more efficiently, thereby accelerating microbial pathway discovery.

records.title: The Potential Role of Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis and Functional Reprogramming in Colorectal Liver Metastasis via the Gut-Liver Axis.
records.abstract: BackgroundColorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) is a leading cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet current surveillance often misses occult micrometastases, underscoring an urgent need for early non-invasive biomarkers and mechanistic insights.AimsThis study aimed to investigate gut microbiota dysbiosis and functional alterations associated with CRLM and explore potential non-invasive biomarkers.Methods and resultsFecal metagenomic sequencing was performed in 60 participants, comprising healthy controls, patients with non-metastatic CRC, and patients with synchronous CRLM (n = 20 per group). Microbial composition, functional pathways, co-occurrence networks, and clinical associations were systematically analyzed, and a random forest model was constructed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers. Results showed that gut microbiota dysbiosis intensified as CRC progressed toward CRLM, characterized by the depletion of commensal flora and significant enrichment of specific genera, such as Eikenella and Porphyromonas. Functionally, the gut microbiome displayed stage-specific remodeling, shifting from infection- and virulence-related pathways in CRC to functions associated with microbial secondary metabolism and stress adaptation in CRLM. Furthermore, SPIEC-EASI-based network analysis revealed a sparser and more compartmentalized microbial ecological structure in CRLM, with [Clostridium] symbiosum, Campylobacter concisus, and Coprococcus eutactus emerging as module hubs. A random forest model integrating nine core taxa and one virulence factor (VF0160 FeoAB) achieved an overall 97.5% classification accuracy in discriminating CRLM from non-metastatic CRC, indicating the potential of fecal metagenomic biomarkers for future risk stratification. However, prospective validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical translational utility.ConclusionCollectively, our findings suggest that gut microbiota dysbiosis and functional reprogramming are strongly associated with CRLM progression, potentially through remodeling the hepatic pre-metastatic niche via the gut-liver axis.
