records.title: Do Leaf Temperatures Determine Endophyte Composition and Richness in Florida Native Plant Species?
records.abstract: Microbiomes play crucial roles in ecosystems, largely through their interactions with plants. Fungal endophytes occur in nearly all plant tissues and can influence host physiology, stress tolerance, and productivity. Although previous studies have examined how air temperature shapes foliar endophyte communities, endophytes may respond more strongly to leaf temperatures, which are often decoupled from ambient air temperatures. Consequently, changes in leaf temperature (e.g., due to global warming) may alter endophyte diversity and composition. In this study, we experimentally tested whether elevated leaf temperatures affect fungal endophyte richness and community composition in six native subtropical plant species from South Florida. Using in situ localized heating of individual branches, we increased leaf temperatures by 1°C-3°C over a 2-week period. Leaf thermal profiles were monitored with thermal imaging, and pre- and post-treatment leaf samples were collected from warmed and control branches for fungal DNA extraction, ITS sequencing, and community analysis. Our results show that fungal leaf endophyte richness and composition were strongly determined by host plant identity, but were unaffected by warming. Linear mixed-effects models and paired t-tests showed no significant changes in ESV richness with heating across all hosts. Similarly, distance-based redundancy analysis and PERMANOVA tests revealed no significant shifts in fungal community composition due to increased leaf temperatures. However, a random forest classification model identified a subset of fungal ESV that were predictive of temperature treatment. While overall endophyte communities were stable, specific taxa may be thermally responsive. Foliar fungal endophyte communities in subtropical woody plants may be resistant to short-term warming. Such stability could buffer host plants against microbial disruption during temperature extremes, though it may also limit adaptive microbial turnover. This study advances understanding of plant-microbe thermal dynamics and underscores the need for further research on the functional resistance of endophyte communities under climate change.
records.authors: Tserej O, Hernandez DJ, Rawstern AH, Kiesewetter KN, Almeida BK, Afkhami ME, Feeley KJ.

records.title: Are entirely virus-free CAR T cells as good as lentiviral transduced universal cells?
records.abstract: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cells are commonly generated using gamma-retroviral or lentiviral vectors given their efficiency and stable integration, but vector supply constraints have created bottlenecks to wider access. Using a combination of lentiviral transduction and genome editing, 'universal' donor CAR-T cells devoid of endogenous TCRαβ and suitable for multiple recipients are also under investigation as 'off-the-shelf' therapies. In addition, nuclease mediated insertion by homology-directed repair (HDR) of CAR genes delivered by Adeno Associated Virus into the TRAC locus has been reported to mediate superior tumour clearance. We investigated alternative entirely virus-free procedures to insert synthetic DNA encoding CAR genes at either TRAC or CD3ζ loci in direct comparison to lentiviral generated universal 41BB-CD3ζ-CAR T cells. While non-viral manufacture was successful and in vitro cytotoxic function was comparable, in vivo inhibition of human leukemia in xenograft murine models was not superior to lentiviral products. Non-viral approaches offer attractive prospects for sophisticated editing and precise CAR insertion and may offer valuable therapeutic options, but careful preclinical evaluation and well-designed clinical trials benchmarked against existing lentiviral approaches are recommended.
records.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

records.title: Deuterium at environmentally relevant concentrations modulates metabolite production and protein synthesis in Chlorella sp.
records.abstract: Natural aquatic ecosystems exhibit substantial fluctuations in water deuterium concentrations. However, the physiological and molecular responses of microalgae to deuterium concentrations within the range of environmental baselines remain poorly characterized. In this study, Chlorella sp. was cultured for 8 days in deuterium-depleted water (DDW, 75 ppm), natural deuterium control water (150 ppm), and moderately deuterium-enriched water (DEW, 195 ppm). Chlorophyll fluorescence assays showed that DDW improved photosynthetic efficiency and promoted algal biomass accumulation, with the effect evident by day 8. By contrast, DEW initially stimulated photosynthetic activity but later caused severe inhibition of Photosystem II (PSII). Untargeted metabolomics revealed 374 differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) in response to DDW exposure, alongside widespread upregulation of lipid and energy metabolism pathways. Under DEW exposure, the number of DAMs was substantially lower, with only 114 identified, and amino acid and nucleotide metabolism was suppressed. Quantitative proteomics indicated that DDW induced mild remodeling of proteins involved in cytoskeletal organization and cell division, whereas DEW triggered extensive changes in the proteome associated with DNA damage repair. Isotope quantification of culture media showed bidirectional net hydrogen-deuterium (H-D) exchange between microalgae and the surrounding water: algae released deuterium into DDW media and assimilated deuterium under DEW conditions. Linoleic acid metabolism was consistently suppressed under both DDW and DEW treatments compared with the control. These findings indicate that environmentally relevant deuterium fluctuations can modulate microalgal photosynthesis, metabolism, and proteostasis, thereby providing a basis for interpreting hydrogen isotope biogeochemical cycling in freshwater ecosystems. Whether such effects can be exploited for industrial metabolite production remains to be established.
records.authors: Liu J, Shen S, Han J, Fan H, Chen J, Feng G, Hu C, Liu J.

records.title: Cryo-EM structure of a near-planar 13-mer ring formed by recombinant human parainfluenza virus type 2 nucleoprotein.
records.abstract: Human parainfluenza virus type 2 (HPIV2) is an orthorubulavirus respiratory pathogen whose genome is encapsidated by the viral nucleoprotein (N), for which high-resolution experimental structural information has been lacking. Here, we report a cryo-electron microscopy structure of recombinant HPIV2 N assembled with co-purified RNA in a closed, near-planar 13-protomer ring, reconstructed with C13 symmetry at a nominal, sampling-limited resolution of 2.91 Å. Tilted cryo-EM data collection was used to mitigate strong preferred orientation, and C13-symmetric refinement of 430,693 particles yielded this reconstruction. An independent C1 reconstruction supported the closed ring-like architecture without imposed rotational symmetry. The structure contains a conserved RNA-binding groove. Because the recombinant protein co-purified with heterogeneous host-derived RNA and the groove-associated density was not sequence-resolved, a template-derived poly-uridine strand was positioned as a conservative representation of a plausible RNA path and six-nucleotide-per-protomer register rather than as a native RNA assignment. Contact-map and ILV/LIV hydrophobic-cluster analyses identified recurrent intra-protomer and inter-protomer packing features, including N-arm-to-neighbouring-core and C-terminal-side contacts. In single 300 ns RNA-bound and RNA-free molecular-dynamics trajectories, the overall ring architecture and compactness were maintained, while local flexibility differences were observed near the RNA-binding groove. Comparative structural analysis places the recombinant HPIV2 N 13-mer observed here among near-planar paramyxovirus N assemblies, alongside PIV5 and the near-planar mumps N form, and distinguishes it from more strongly pitched nucleocapsid assemblies. These results define the oligomeric architecture of recombinant HPIV2 N and provide a structural reference for RNA binding, inter-protomer organisation and future structure-guided engineering of the scaffold.
records.authors: Matić Z, Sarim KM, Degtjarik O, Vujaklija D, Kazazić S.

records.title: Microenvironment of Bone and Joint Infection: Examining the Microenvironment.
records.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of arthroplasty, and conventional diagnostic methods for PJI remain limited by suboptimal sensitivity, long turnaround times, high cost, and patient inconvenience, particularly in biofilm-associated and culture-negative infections. Emerging data suggest that the infected joint microenvironment contains host- and pathogen-derived molecular signatures with substantial diagnostic potential. This review evaluates current evidence on microenvironment-related biomarkers in PJI, including host extracellular vesicles, host cell-free nucleic acids (microRNA/cell-free DNA), non-host-derived biomarkers, and sequencing-based pathogen detection techniques. Host-derived biomarkers show favorable discriminatory capability by characterizing inflammatory and immune responses, and metagenomic and sequencing-based technologies improve pathogen identification. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, widespread clinical implementation remains limited due to a lack of standardization, cost, and limited prospective validation. Future prospective multicenter studies should integrate conventional microbiological methods with molecular and microenvironment-based approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy.
records.authors: Abbaszadeh A, Damirchi MH, Soleimani M, Ortega-Yago A, Javad Mortazavi SM, Citak M, Parvizi J.

records.title: Predicting key viral mutations from within-host deep sequencing data.
records.abstract: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 evolution drives continuous epidemic waves, harming vaccine protection and exerting heavy burden to population health. Predicting virus evolution holds the key for current and future medical countermeasures against infectious diseases by allowing well-matching vaccines and timely epidemic response. However, due to its high genetic diversity, fast transmissibility and evolutionary rate, accurate and timely prediction of SARS-CoV-2 evolution remains a challenge. To address this, we developed a computational framework, Beth-2, to predict key mutations of SARS-CoV-2 through analyzing within-host viral genome deep sequencing data. We leveraged the early fitness signals of variants exhibited within-host and their fitness pattern between-host to infer the emerging mutations with fitness potential. In retrospective data validation, 98.6% of the key SARS-CoV-2 mutations on receptor binding domain could be detected by our model with a median lead time of 9 mo before they reached predominance at population level. Among the 26 prospectively predicted mutations, 69% of them exhibited significantly enhanced transmissibility and five showed significant immune escape from plasma of subjects who received COVID-19 mRNA vaccine collected 6 mo after the prediction time. The mutations predicted by Beth-2 that are functionally enhanced include F456L, the defining mutation of multiple current circulating lineages, including KP.3, NB.1.8.1, and XFG. The model captures mutations of high fitness potential under the natural immune environment of host and is applicable to other pathogens. The framework can be implemented along with the existing genome surveillance network and offers an efficient and effective instrument for vaccine preparation and epidemic response.

records.title: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation.
records.abstract: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively. In vitro assessment revealed divergent probiotic adaptive traits between the two strains, particularly in gastrointestinal stress tolerance. Genomic analysis revealed the presence of genes encoding the functionally related effector proteins P9 and Amuc_1100. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, supplementing with Muc_T9 and Mas_DA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and alleviated colonic inflammation and histological damage. Notably, divergent expression patterns of key genes involved in lipid metabolism and adipose tissue remodeling suggest potential differences in host metabolic regulatory modes. Furthermore, both strains restored gut microbial diversity and increased the relative abundance of putative short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing bacteria. Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.
records.authors: Dai J, Li Z, Zheng C, Li Y, Li X, Ni W, Hu S.

records.title: Stepwise assembly and mechanical stability of nsP3 Helical Scaffolds in Chikungunya Virus
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4. In this study, we focused on nsP3, which comprises three distinct domains: the alphavirus unique domain (AUD), the long and intrinsically disordered hypervariable domain (HVD), and the enzymatic macrodomain (MD). Notably, nsP3 assembles into helicoidal macrostructures, termed helical scaffolds (HSs), which are components of the CHIKV replication complex and are involved in the formation of macromolecular traps in the cytoplasm of the infected cell called Alphagranules (AGs). HSs form tubular helical scaffolds assembled through the AUD, with the MD and HVD flexibly deployed to the scaffold exterior. Despite their functional importance, the mechanisms governing HS formation remain poorly understood. Using High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy (HS-AFM) and Electron Microscopy (EM) we achieved new findings on the structure, mechanics and assembly of these macrostructures. Our results show the nsP3 monomers follow intermediate steps before completing the assembly into full helical scaffolds, with each nsP3 domain contributing differently to this process. The macrodomain (MD) provides mechanical stability, yet it fractures under tens of piconewtons of force. This rigidity acts as a mechanical regulator that constrains the position of the HVD, which in turn mediates interactions with host factors and neighboring HSs. Through this interplay, nsP3 achieves both structural cohesion and functional adaptability, promoting the higher-order organization of HSs into honeycomb-like networks.
records.authors: Martín-González N, Karpov A, Reguera J, Casuso I.

records.title: Transcriptome reallocation during infection reshapes synonymous codon demand in  Botrytis cinerea
records.abstract: While genomic codon usage is fixed within an individual isolate, the synonymous codons represented in its RNA pool can change when transcription shifts among genes. We tested whether this transcript-level phenotype accompanies infection by reanalyzing 39 libraries from three public  Botrytis cinerea RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) time series in S. lycopersicum,  Arabidopsis thaliana , and  Physcomitrium patens . Gene counts were corrected for coding length, combined with fixed gene-specific codon inventories, and analyzed as centered log ratios within synonymous amino-acid families. Sampling time accounted for 95–98% of fungal codon-demand variation in each series. The association persisted after effective-length correction, unique-only competitive mapping, host-homology exclusion, depth equalization, protein-family weighting, and removal of translation-associated genes. Change vectors over the interpolated, time-aligned 16–24-h interval were positively aligned among studies, whereas later trajectories diverged. Matched reassignments of complete expression trajectories showed more full-series organization than expected in  S. lycopersicum and  Arabidopsis , but not in  P. patens . Codon-preference-weighted abundance and expression breadth also changed through infection, although their directions were not universal. Across systems, large non-translation contributors repeatedly carried ATP-synthase/respiratory and extracellular annotations, although their timing and companion functions differed. Infection-associated transcriptional reallocation therefore repeatedly restructures the synonymous composition of the inferred fungal transcript pool. This establishes a dynamic allocation phenotype and a basis for testing consequences for RNA stability and translation during host–pathogen interactions.
records.authors: Dowell JA, Pradhan L, Madrigal M.

records.title: QRAFT: Scaling coalescent-based species tree inference to one million taxa
records.abstract: Species tree inference from multi-locus data under the multispecies coalescent has not kept pace with phylogenomic datasets that now span hundreds of thousands of species. We present QRAFT, a statistically consistent method for estimating species trees by maximizing quartet support on phylogenomic datasets at unprecedented scales. For  n taxa and  k gene trees, QRAFT achieves near-linear running time of  O (  kn log  2 n ) when its recursion is balanced, which is within a polylogarithmic factor of the  O (  kn ) time required simply to read the input. It also achieves asymptotically optimal  O (  kn ) memory, so its memory requirements grow only linearly with the input size. QRAFT infers a million-taxon species tree from 1,000 genes in just three hours using only 298 GB of RAM, 64 CPU threads, and no GPUs. We estimate that the same analysis with ASTRAL-MP, a scalable parallel implementation of the widely used method ASTRAL, would take about 36 years (> 100, 000 times longer) and require prohibitive amounts of memory, far beyond practical computational limits. QRAFT maintains accuracy comparable to, and in many cases better than, leading species tree estimation methods. Notably, QRAFT reconstructed a microbial tree of life comprising 199,330 genomes in just a few hours using modest CPU resources. Thus, QRAFT brings highly accurate statistically consistent coalescent-based species tree inference to the unprecedented million-taxon regime and enables phylogenomic analyses towards the scale of the tree of life. QRAFT is publicly available at  https://github.com/risenfromashes/qraft .
records.authors: Rahman A, Saha A, Bayzid MS.

records.title: Creation of genomic chimeras via megabase scale genome expansion
records.abstract: An organism’s physiology is controlled by its genomic content. Building genomic chimeras would enable melding of the diverse functions and properties of life. However, prior arts in genome synthesis are limited to reconstituting pre-existing functions within a singular genome rather than combining diverse genomic functions across multiple distinct genomes. Existing methods are also prohibitively expensive, labor intensive, and time consuming, and thus fundamentally not scalable for creating large synthetic chimeric genomes. To address all these limitations, we invented Additive Conjugative-CAST Engineering (ACE) combining conjugation with CRISPR-associated transposition (CAST) to deliver and integrate up to half a genome per step from a donor cell into a precisely defined position in the recipient’s genome. We have demonstrated ACE’s capability to integrate at least a 2-megabase donor genomic segment in a single step and at least 3 megabase in two consecutive steps. Importantly, we confirmed ACE’s generality through the creation of multiple genomic chimeras across species, genus, and at least order barriers. With ACE, we further demonstrate such chimeric organisms, or what we call genome expanded organisms (GEOs), can be stably forged from at least three starting bacterial strains, and can be stably maintained to express all their acquired genomic parts in a single chimera. ACE offers a new paradigm of creating artificial lifeforms to combine desired properties and potentially create novel functions beyond the constraints of nature. ACE also offers a unique perspective to probe unexplored plasticity in genome architecture and expression patterns of novel, massively expanded genomes.
records.authors: Sanfiorenzo C, Zhang RJ, Wythes G, Wang M, Huang J, Hur J, Lipschitz M, Zhou J, Swift R, Gerber B, Wang K.

records.title: Genomic epidemiology reconstructs the pre-detection transmission and establishment of chikungunya virus in Guangdong, China
records.abstract: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Réunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.

records.title: Multiomics Analysis of Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma Reveals the Immunological Microenvironment Associated with MTAP Loss and Immunotherapy Outcomes.
records.abstract: PurposeNivolumab plus ipilimumab is a standard first-line therapy for unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), yet biomarkers predicting immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy remain undefined. We aimed to identify genomic and tumor immune microenvironmental features associated with ICI response in MPM.Experimental designWe analyzed two independent MPM cohorts. The discovery cohort included patients at the National Cancer Center Hospital (2012-2022) with frozen tumor tissues available for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and RNA sequencing. Genomic alterations, transcriptomic profiles, immune cell composition, and T-cell receptor repertoire were analyzed, and key findings were validated in a nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) cohort.ResultsThe WGS cohort comprised 52 patients. Among ICI-treated patients, overall response rates were 30% in the WGS cohort and 29.4% in the C-CAT cohort. Genomic analyses identified frequent alterations in BAP1 and NF2, across both cohorts. ICI responders showed higher T-cell receptor diversity, increased CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and enrichment of M1 macrophages compared with non-responders. MTAP loss was associated with higher CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and T-cell receptor diversity, and was linked to a higher ICI response rate in the C-CAT cohort. In contrast, BAP1 and NF2 alterations showed no consistent association with immune features or ICI efficacy.ConclusionsAn immune-active tumor microenvironment characterized by high T-cell receptor diversity, CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and M1 macrophage enrichment was associated with favorable ICI responses in MPM. MTAP loss was linked to immune-related features and a higher ICI response, supporting further investigation of MTAP loss as a candidate biomarker.

records.title: Pseudomonas sediminis CRE-TB-54 carries tmexCD3-toprJ3 in a novel chromosomal region.
records.abstract: The emergence of tmexCD-toprJ, coding for a transmissible multidrug resistance efflux pump of the resistance-nodulation-division (RND) family has compromised the usefulness of tigecycline in the treatment of infections caused by multidrug resistant Gram-negative bacteria. Here, we describe the presence of tmexCD3-toprJ3 in a novel chromosomal context in Pseudomonas sediminis CRE-TB-54 isolated from a toilet in a university dormitory in southwestern Nigeria. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole genome sequencing showed that CRE-TB-54 displayed intermediate level resistance to tigecycline and haboured multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including tmexCD3-toprJ3 flanked upstream and downstream by genetic structures not previously reported in association with tmexCD-toprJ. These include insertion sequences IS4 and IS30, and the metal resistance gene czcD upstream, the prophage integrase IntA, the competence associated DNA binding protein gene comEA, and the double stranded DNA repair and homologous recombination gene cluster recBCD downstream. These results provide new insight into the genetic structures surrounding the tmexCD-toprJ cluster and raises concern about toilets as a potential environmental reservoir of bacteria carrying this clinically important gene in a resource-limited setting where tigecycline is not currently used in human or animals.
records.authors: Olufemi Adelowo O, Fashae K, Babajide Taiwo J, Kaster AK, Müller JA.

records.title: Advances and challenges in tissue-based HIV reservoir quantification.
records.abstract: Purpose of reviewPeripheral blood provides an accessible but incomplete representation of the HIV reservoir. This review summarizes recent advances in PCR-based quantification of HIV persistence in human tissues, with particular emphasis on the intact proviral DNA assay (IPDA), the methodological challenges introduced by tissue sampling, and complementary approaches that extend the biological information obtained from IPDA.Recent findingsIPDA and related droplet digital PCR assays are increasingly being applied to human tissues, including lymph nodes, brain, gut, and adipose tissue, often in combination with orthogonal assays to address specific biological questions. Recent studies highlight important considerations in interpreting these measurements, particularly the identity and number of cells used as the denominator, DNA shearing, and spatial representativeness of the sampled tissue. These issues complicate comparisons across tissues and with peripheral blood, particularly when different cell populations or sampling depths are analyzed. Newer multitarget droplet digital PCR assays increase the genomic information used to infer proviral intactness, while complementary approaches provide information on viral genotype, cellular identity, clonality, and functional state.SummaryRecent applications of IPDA to human tissues highlight important considerations in cellular denominator, sampling depth, DNA shearing, and spatial sampling that influence the interpretation of reservoir measurements across anatomical compartments. At the same time, combining IPDA with complementary assays is extending tissue studies beyond quantification toward characterization of the virus, infected cell, clonality, and functional state. Future approaches that preserve the relationship between the virus, its host cell, and its tissue environment will further advance the study of HIV persistence in tissues.
records.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
records.authors: Lee GQ, Simonetti FR.

records.title: Molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii and a Coxiellaceae bacterium in Hyalomma asiaticum and Dermacentor nuttalli ticks collected in Mongolia.
records.abstract: Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of Q fever, is a zoonotic pathogen for which epidemiological data are limited in Mongolia. This study investigated the presence of C. burnetii in ticks collected across Mongolia from forest, pasture, and livestock-associated environments. A total of 7,511 ticks were collected from 42 Soums across 12 provinces and 2 districts of Ulaanbaatar between May and June 2018. Molecular detection of Coxiella-related organisms was performed using 46 DNA samples, comprising 28 individual-tick samples and 18 pooled-tick samples representing 489 ticks, by nested PCR targeting IS1111 and the 16S rRNA gene. Twenty DNA samples (2 individual ticks and 18 pools) were PCR-positive. Sequencing and phylogenetic analysis revealed that 9 Hyalomma asiaticum tick pools contained 16S rRNA sequences of C. burnetii, whereas 11 Dermacentor nuttalli samples (2 individual ticks and 9 pools) contained 16S rRNA sequences of a Coxiellaceae bacterium. Two individual D. nuttalli ticks yielded IS1111 sequences closely related to C. burnetii, whereas the corresponding 16S rRNA sequences clustered with a Coxiellaceae bacterium, highlighting discordance between the 2 molecular targets. The C. burnetii sequences detected in H. asiaticum were closely related to clade A strains reported from the United States, Japan, Greenland, and Korea, whereas sequences detected in D. nuttalli clustered with Coxiella endosymbiont sequences. This study provides molecular evidence for the presence of C. burnetii in H. asiaticum tick pools in Mongolia and demonstrates that Mongolian ticks harbor genetically diverse Coxiella-related bacteria, highlighting the need for further investigation of their epidemiological significance.
records.authors: Kim CM, Kh T, Lp MJ, Lee YM, D G, B N, J B, N T, Yun NR, Kim DM.

records.title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with a severe episode of self-trauma and urinary tract infection.
records.abstract: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales are emerging pathogens of major importance in veterinary medicine. This study describes the clinical, microbiological, and genomic characteristics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with paraparesis and concurrent pyelonephritis, chronic cystitis, and a self-traumatized limb lesion. A 12-year-old mixed-breed female dog underwent repeated antimicrobial therapy during hospitalization. Urine obtained by cystocentesis and wound samples were cultured, and ESBL-producing strains were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequence-based analysis. CTX-M-55-producing E. coli sequence type (ST) 457, phylogroup F, O11:H25, and fimH145, was recovered from urine and wound samples, while the wound sample also yielded a CTX-M-15- and SHV-2-producing K. pneumoniae ST39, KL149:OL2α.2. The two closely related E. coli strains differed by 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms, despite sharing the same ST, resistome, plasmid replicons, and virulence profile. ESBL-positive strains carried multiple virulence genes, with the E. coli strains classified as extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli strains. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae ST39 in an animal in Brazil. The co-occurrence of ESBL-producing E. coli ST457 and K. pneumoniae ST39 in the same dog highlights the potential for companion animals to harbor clinically relevant multidrug-resistant lineages and reinforces the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship in this sector.

records.title: Comprehensive meta-QTL analysis uncovers stable loci for fruit traits, morphological development, anthocyanin regulation, and biotic stress resistance in eggplant.
records.abstract: Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) is a crop of significant nutritional value within the Solanaceae family; however, advancements in breeding for fruit quality, stress resilience, and architectural traits are limited due to the quantitative nature of inheritance for these traits. Meta-QTL (MQTL) analysis provides a powerful approach for integrating QTL information from various studies for identifying stable genomic regions. We integrated 620 initial QTLs derived from 23 independent studies that encompass traits related to morphology, fruit characteristics, anthocyanin content, prickles, and resistance to biotic stress. A high-density consensus genetic framework was constructed, onto which 425 QTLs (68.54%) were successfully projected. Meta-analysis identified 97 stable MQTLs across LG1-LG12, with the mean confidence interval decreasing from 10.29 cM for the initial QTLs to 3.42 cM for the MQTLs, corresponding to an approximately threefold reduction in interval width (66.8% narrowing). Candidate gene mining within 40 prioritized MQTLs resulted in the retrieval of 1,440 gene models, which were subsequently refined to 68 high-confidence candidates. This refinement was based on domain architecture, synteny conservation with tomato and potato, ortholog analysis, and expression profiling. Key genomic hubs were identified across several chromosomes, most notably on Chromosome 6, which acts as a multi-trait super-region housing major loci for anthocyanin pigmentation (MQTL6.4_A), morphological traits (MQTL6.3_M), and prickle development (MQTL6.3_P). Other critical intervals include Chromosome 3 (MQTL3.1_Bs) for biotic stress resistance, and Chromosomes 1 and 4 (MQTL1.1_F, MQTL4.3_F) for fruit quality traits. These hotspots are enriched for coordinated, multi-layered regulatory networks and functional modules, including pattern-recognition receptors (e.g., LRR-RLKs), transcriptional regulators (WRKY, MYB), scaffolding proteins, and specialized metabolic and structural enzymes (such as GDSL esterases, laccases, F-box proteins, and SWEET transporters). The significant conservation of synteny with both tomato and potato, along with functional insights from Arabidopsis orthology, underscores the evolutionary stability and functional importance of these co-adapted candidate gene complexes across the Solanaceae. This study represents the first comprehensive MQTL analysis in eggplant, establishing a robust genomic framework for trait improvement, providing key markers and candidate genes to accelerate marker-assisted selection and genomic breeding aimed at developing climate-resilient, high-quality varieties.

records.title: Genetic disruptions of Hsp90-encoding genes impacted short-term evolutionary trajectories of antifungal resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
records.abstract: Laboratory evolution has been a powerful approach to address questions about evolvability. It has been debated whether the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) buffers or potentiates the effects of variation and, consequently, constrains or accelerates evolution. In this study, we experimentally evolved yeast strains carrying mutant alleles of Hsp90-encoding genes under mild clotrimazole selection. We found that knockout of HSC82, which encodes a constitutively expressed Hsp90 chaperone, led to slower evolution of clotrimazole resistance in the short term. However, all strains generally evolved resistance within seven transfers, regardless of Hsp90 status. Through whole-genome sequencing, we identified genetic changes associated with clotrimazole resistance, including prevalent mitochondrial genome loss, as well as chromosomal duplications and point mutations. HSC82 knockout populations specifically showed convergent chromosomal duplications of chrVIII and chrXV. Taken together, our results demonstrate that disruption of Hsp90 in yeast may not alter the overall outcome of evolution but may shape its evolutionary trajectories at both the phenotypic and genotypic levels.
records.authors: Li XC, Liang M, Han X, Li W, Dou F.

records.title: Integrative transcriptomic and in silico analysis identifies novel long non-coding RNAs associated with BCL6 and SPARC in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
records.abstract: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common and clinically heterogeneous subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, marked by extensive transcriptional dysregulation and variable therapeutic outcomes. While protein-coding alterations are well characterized, the regulatory role of the non-coding transcriptome remains incompletely defined. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) modulate gene expression through cis/trans transcriptional control, RNA-RNA interactions, and RNA-protein scaffolding. However, DLBCL-specific lncRNAs remain largely unexplored. We applied an integrative in silico framework using RNA-seq datasets from the Sequence Read Archive and The Cancer Genome Atlas, incorporating quality control, alignment, quantification, TPM normalization, differential expression, principal component analysis, multi-level filtering, cis-annotation, survival analysis, functional enrichment with STRING network construction, mutation profiling, RNA-RNA interaction prediction (IntaRNA), and RNA-protein interaction analysis (catRAPID) with structural modeling. With this approach we identified three previously uncharacterized lncRNAs, namely lnc-SPARC-2:3, lnc-FXYD2-1:5, and lnc-ADAMTS1-2:1. These consistently overexpressed lncRNAs in DLBCL were validated by semi-quantitative PCR. In silico thermodynamic modeling supported stable RNA-RNA duplex formation with neighboring mRNAs, and protein interaction analyses predicted high-confidence binding to BCL6 protein. These lncRNAs are predicted to participate in lncRNA-mediated attenuation of BCL6 and may disrupt germinal center regulatory programs, impair B-cell lineage commitment and promote microenvironment-dependent signaling, alongside enrichment of ECM proteoglycans indicative of stromal remodeling, accompanied by marked upregulation of SPARC mRNA. Correlation analyses across the SRA and TCGA cohorts supported the IntaRNA-predicted interactions of lnc-ADAMTS1-2:1-ADAMTS5, lnc-FXYD2-1:5-FXYD6, and lnc-SPARC-2:3-ATOX1, revealing consistent positive associations that remained supported after adjustment for cohort and stromal score. Notably, the observed survival trend for lnc-FXYD2-1:5 did not reach statistical significance; nevertheless, it is suggested as a candidate biomarker with potential prognostic relevance that merits further investigation in larger independent cohorts. Collectively, this study provides a systematic computational framework supported by experimental validation for the presence of the shortlisted lncRNAs. However, further experimental validation is required to establish their functional roles, which may support their investigation as potential therapeutic targets in future DLBCL studies.
records.authors: Arun SM, Roy U, Desai S, Choudhary B, Raghavan SC, Devaki NS.

records.title: Intrinsic replication advantage of a Hepatitis B Virus genotype C strain is independent of the basal core promoter A1762T/G1764A mutation.
records.abstract: This study aimed to isolate and characterize individual hepatitis B virus (HBV) strains from a patient co-infected with genotype B and C, and to directly compare their intrinsic replication capacities. HBV DNA was isolated from a chronic hepatitis B patient. Genotypes were determined by genotype-specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and full-length genomes were cloned. Two clones representing subgenotype B2 (c17) and C1 (c21) were selected, sequenced and transfected into HepG2 cells. Viral replication was assessed via Southern blot and quantitative PCR. The role of the common Adenine (A)1762Thymine (T/)Guanine (G)1764A mutation in the C1 clone was investigated by site-directed mutagenesis. As a result, the genotype C1 clone exhibited significantly higher replication capacity than the B2 clone. Counterintuitively, reverting the A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone to wild-type further enhanced its replication, indicating this mutation was not the primary driver of its high replicative fitness. In conclusion, HBV genotype C1 possesses a greater inherent replication capacity than B2, independent of the classic basal core promoter (BCP) mutation, providing a virological explanation for its association with severe disease outcomes in co-infection.
records.authors: Xiao Y, Chen X, Li Z, Lei S, Chen Z, Cai J, Cui X.

records.title: Genital microbial profile of repeat breeding in a Kangal sheep flock: a survey of ewes and rams under natural mating.
records.abstract: Infertility in sheep remains a significant concern in modern livestock production, with non-pregnancy rates during the breeding season increasing considerably in recent decades. The present study was conducted in a Kangal sheep flock with a documented history of reproductive failure, characterised by consecutive estrous cycles without conception. A total of 905 multiparous Kangal ewes (3-6 years old) and 44 Kangal rams (4-6 years old), all with documented fertility records, were enrolled at the beginning of the breeding season. Before mating, all ewes underwent transrectal ultrasonographic examination and evaluation of vaginal discharge. Following this screening, 880 ewes with no ultrasonographic abnormalities and normal vaginal discharge were monitored throughout the breeding season. Of these, 171 ewes that failed to conceive after the first mating underwent a second mating cycle, resulting in 50 additional pregnancies. The remaining 121 non-pregnant ewes underwent a third mating, resulting in 36 additional pregnancies. Blood samples were subsequently collected from the 85 ewes that remained non-pregnant after three consecutive mating attempts. Of these, 21 tested seropositive for Coxiella burnetii and border disease virus (BDV) and were excluded from the study. Vaginal swabs were collected from 25 of the remaining 64 ewes that tested negative for Brucella spp., C. burnetii, and BDV. These animals were classified as repeat breeders or clinically affected animals (Group 2). An equal number of ewes ( n=25 ) that tested negative for these pathogens and conceived after a single mating cycle were assigned to the healthy control group (Group 1). Preputial swabs were also collected from 15 breeding rams to evaluate the potential for venereal transmission. All swab samples were subjected to microbiological culture and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis following DNA extraction. The targeted pathogens included Brucella spp., Mycoplasma spp., Chlamydophila spp., Campylobacter spp., Coxiella burnetii, Salmonella Abortusovis, Trueperella pyogenes, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Although Mycoplasma spp., T. pyogenes, and Campylobacter spp. were detected in swab samples from both groups, the prevalence of Mycoplasma spp. ( padjMycoplasma bovigenitalium ( padj=0.05 ) was significantly higher in Group 2 than in Group 1. The increased detection of these microorganisms in reproductively compromised ewes suggests a potential role in the aetiology of ovine infertility, either through direct pathogenic effects or by contributing to reproductive tract dysbiosis. However, further controlled studies are warranted to establish a definitive causal relationship between these microorganisms and reproductive failure in sheep.
records.authors: Takcı A, Moğulkoç MN, Kıvrak MB, Kalın R, Demirel MA, Sönmez Ünal G.

records.title: Language-guided domain adaptation improves protein sequence representations for antimicrobial resistance analysis
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), particularly antibiotic resistance in bacterial pathogens, complicates infectious disease management. Because bacterial resistance is often mediated by protein functions, including antibiotic inactivation and efflux, protein sequence analysis provides a molecular basis for digital AMR surveillance and therapeutic intervention. We developed BacLLM, a language guided protein representation framework that integrates annotation-derived functional knowledge into protein language model representations for AMR analysis in WHO priority bacterial pathogens. Through sequence enhancement, semantic enrichment of UniProt annotations, and cross modal contrastive learning, BacLLM transfers LLM encoded annotation priors into the sequence encoder. Compared with baselines, BacLLM provided more informative representations for resistance-gene identification and mechanism prediction, captured resistance associated mutational signals at single-residue resolution, and preserved taxonomic relationships not reflected by phenotype based clinical groupings. Moreover, BacLLM recovered resistance associated functional organization within a TolC-centered protein association network, prioritizing proteins with low sequence identity to TolC but predicted structural similarity to TolC. Extending from AMR characterization to therapeutic prioritization, BacLLM also improved strain-level phage host matching for phage therapy candidate prioritization. Together, these findings establish BacLLM as a protein representation framework supporting AMR surveillance, functional characterization, and therapeutic candidate prioritization.
records.authors: Ye R, Li L, Geng Z, Song S.

records.title: Early terminated transcripts and missing proteins reflect artifacts in bacterial proteomes.
records.abstract: The high redundancy of many bacterial proteomes can be used to evaluate proteome quality and identify sequence errors. We have used MMseqs2 clustering with subsequent filtering to identify clusters that contain sequences from at least 50% of the clustered proteomes to build sets of core proteins that include proteins from 95% of the clustered bacteria. These clusters typically capture >80% of proteins in the bacteria. Because these clusters have highly uniform length (the median cluster has >99% of its proteins at the mode length), short (133%) proteins are likely artifacts. Most "outlier" proteins are found in fewer than 10% of clusters, and "high-outlier" clusters are over-represented in a small fraction of proteomes, which often have poor proteome BUSCO fragment scores. Short-outlier proteins are artifacts; at least 80% of short-outlier genomes contain mode-length copies of the protein, which were missed because of frameshifts, termination codons, or initiation codon choice. MMseqs2 clustering with 50% participation provides robust sets of core bacterial proteins and can be used to identify lower-quality proteomes and proteins.
records.authors: Insana G, Martin MJ, Pearson WR.

records.title: Climate-Associated Genetic Variation in Native and Introduced Populations of Eustenopus villosus, a Biological Control Agent for Yellow Starthistle.
records.abstract: Contemporary evolution in biological control systems is rarely studied, though biological agents are repeatedly exposed to novel environmental conditions upon introduction. Their ability to adapt to new conditions could influence management efficacy and reveal important aspects of environmental selection. Using a ddRADseq dataset, we tested for genomic evidence of adaptation to climate in populations of Eustenopus villosus (Boheman, Coleoptera: Curculionidae), the "hairy weevil", which is used in classical biological control for yellow starthistle (Centaurea solstitialis L., Asteraceae) in the western United States. We first estimated population structure in E. villosus across our samples of the native and introduced ranges and then used six complementary genotype-environment association analyses to identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with climate in both native and introduced populations. Additionally, we used historical release records to categorize sampling sites according to their serial founding history and test for impacts of this history on total and putatively adaptive genomic variation in the introductions. We also tested whether candidate loci associated with climate in the native range exhibit similar associations in the introductions, or if new associations have evolved. We identified many candidate loci in both native and introduced populations and found little evidence of a decline in genomic variation, which suggests that serial founding events did not prevent climatic adaptation. Candidate loci differed between native and introduced populations, indicating that local adaptation has occurred in different regions of the genome after introduction of E. villosus. Our findings suggest an important role for novel contemporary adaptation in this biological control system and provide insight into how genetic variation can persist in biological control agents through introduction and serial founding events.
records.authors: Barker BS, Pelosi JA, Sert O, Dlugosch KM.

records.title: Global Population Genomics Links Mobilome Architecture to Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Burden in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
records.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical opportunistic pathogen responsible for severe healthcare-associated infections globally. Understanding its population structure and the interplay between antimicrobial resistance, mobile genetic elements (mobilome), and virulence profiles is essential for combating its spread. This study analyzes 7,341 quality-filtered P. aeruginosa genomes from 84 countries to define the global population structure and characterize the relationships between the mobilome, antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) burden, and virulence profiles. Using a consensus resistome approach alongside specialized bioinformatic tools for mobile genetic elements and virulence factors, we found that the global population exhibits extensive genomic diversity alongside prominent international high-risk clones like ST235 and ST111. Acquired-candidate ARG burden was most strongly associated with integron-related features, whereas insertion sequence metrics showed moderate unadjusted correlations, with no independent association for total IS count after multivariable adjustment. Plasmid-associated metrics showed comparatively weaker associations. While virulence-associated gene content remains largely conserved across the population, type III secretion system effectors exoU and exoS display a largely reciprocal and lineage-specific distribution. Furthermore, carbapenemase genes show distinct geographic and clonal patterns, highlighting a dual dynamic of international high-risk clone dissemination and regional acquisition. These findings are consistent with a major contribution of mobile genetic elements to ARG accumulation in P. aeruginosa, emphasizing the need for continuous genomic surveillance to track and contain emerging strains.
records.authors: Suwannasin S, Kalawong R, Dechathai T, Yaikhan T, Chusri S, Palittapongarnpim P, Surachat K.

records.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
records.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustment for MELD, country, demographics, sex, proton pump inhibitor (PPI), lactulose, and rifaximin use. We enrolled 221 patients (median age 58 y, 57.9% men, median MELD 12). Cognitive performance varied by country despite adjustment for clinical covariates. Lithuania demonstrated greater microbial richness and better cognition despite higher MELD, accompanied by distinct dietary patterns including greater yogurt and tea consumption. In the entire cohort, increasing MELD was associated with reduced microbial richness and depletion of commensals. Worse PHES performance, however, showed a distinct microbiome signature with increased Streptococcus abundance independent of MELD, country, PPI use, and HE therapies. Twenty-two microbial pathways were associated with PHES, mostly related to amino-acid biosynthesis and nitrogen metabolism. Of these, ornithine degradation and heme B biosynthesis II were uniquely enriched with worse PHES and CHE, which mapped onto Enterobacteriaceae. We conclude that across four geographically and culturally disparate countries, cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment was associated with consistent microbial compositional and functional alterations distinct from advancing liver disease. These findings support a consistent gut‒liver‒brain axis signature involving oral-gut translocation and altered nitrogen metabolism.

records.title: Characterization of the organelle genomes of mycoheterotrophic Thismia angustimitra and evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer.
records.abstract: BackgroundOur knowledge about mitochondrial genome evolution in plants is lacking far behind our knowledge of plastome evolution. In heterotrophic plants, it is well-known that plastome degradation and reduced or lost photosynthesis go hand in hand, and there is little if any difference between plastome evolution in mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites. The mitochondrial genome appears less affected by a heterotrophic lifestyle, although exceptions occur. In contrast to plastome evolution, mitochondrial evolution may differ between mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites, in particular with regards to the occurrence of horizontal gene transfer. However, data from mycoheterotrophs are scarce, and complete mitogenomes are only known from three of ten clades.ResultsHere we present data from the complete plastome and mitogenome from Thismia angustimitra, representing a fourth clade of mycoheterotrophs. The 18,215 bp plastome is much reduced and includes only few genes. The mitogenome has a multicircular structure consisting of 22 chromosomes with a total length of 422,400 bp. The gene content and the pattern of RNA editing are normal. The mitogenome includes only few repeats and recombinational activity is limited. A search for foreign DNA did not reveal any fungal sequences, the content of plastid DNA is low, but a large proportion of intergenic DNA shows similarity to distantly related angiosperms. Just a few plastid inserts appear to have originated through intracellular transfer, whereas others most likely stem from horizontal gene transfer. Synteny patterns of the intergenic sequences suggest that horizontal transfer may happen in either direction.ConclusionThe highly reduced plastome of T. angustimitra fits completely the general picture of plastome degradation in heterotrophic plants. Whereas the mitogenome in many aspects appears unaffected by the lifestyle, the recombinational activity is unusually low. Surprisingly, we find evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer, indicating that this phenomenon may be more common among mycoheterotrophic plants than previously thought.

records.title: Microbial biosynthesis of fatty acids for human health: biological evidence, production advances, and commercial challenges.
records.abstract: Several fatty acid (FA) families with established, debated, or emerging health relevance-including long-chain n-3 (EPA, DHA), n-6 (GLA, ARA), branched-chain FA (BCFA), and odd-chain FA (OCFA)-remain scarce in conventional diets, largely absent from plant-based diets, or face supply vulnerabilities driven by climate change and declining marine resources. Bridging the gap between nutritional demand and sustainable supply requires both a clearer understanding of these FA physiological roles and the development of alternative production systems. This narrative review integrates three interconnected dimensions of this challenge. First, current evidence on the physiological functions and health outcomes of these key FA families is critically evaluated, noting that while robust consensus supports the benefits of n-3 and, to a lesser extent, ARA, evidence for most other FA discussed herein remains either limited or controversial. Second, traditional dietary sources of these FA are described alongside advances in non-photosynthetic microbial platforms (yeasts, filamentous fungi, bacteria, and thraustochytrids) as scalable, climate-resilient production alternatives, evaluating both naturally occurring and genetically engineered strains. Third, the key challenges to commercial translation are assessed, including economic feasibility, regulatory frameworks, and consumer acceptance. This review argues that microbial fermentation represents a resource-efficient pathway to secure global access to health-relevant FA under mounting environmental constraints. However, translating this potential into commercial reality demands coordinated progress in strain engineering, bioprocess intensification, regulatory harmonization across jurisdictions, and clinical validation of microbially derived FA.
records.authors: Ventura M, Konzock O, Ledesma-Amaro R, Dulermo T.

records.title: Microbial mechanisms of enhancing carbon and nitrogen conversion by segmented sodium acetate dosing in a modified A<sup>2</sup>/O process.
records.abstract: Low C/N ratios in municipal wastewater often limit nitrogen removal efficiency, necessitating carbon source supplementation to enhance denitrification and reduce effluent total nitrogen (TN) concentrations. This study addresses this challenge by establishing a feast-famine alternating nutritional environment in a modified anaerobic-anoxic-oxic (MAAO) reactor through segmented sodium acetate dosing. This approach was associated with enhanced carbon and nitrogen metabolic pathway conversions. Our results showed that segmented sodium acetate dosing was associated with improved microbial substrate uptake, leading to increased carbon and nitrogen conversion rates of 2.3 percentage points and 11.8 percentage points, respectively. Enhanced interactions between hydrolyzing/fermenting bacteria and denitrifying bacteria fostered synergistic carbon and nitrogen conversion. Furthermore, metagenomic analysis indicated enhanced genetic potential for nitrate transport and denitrification, consistent with the increased denitrification contribution observed in the nitrogen balance. This research illuminates the efficiency of carbon and nitrogen metabolism and microbial community function in MAAO in response to dynamic nutrient environments. It contributes significantly to understanding the potential mechanisms underlying nitrogen transformation in such systems.
records.authors: Wang S, Li W, Zhang G, Guo X, Li D, Yao S, Fang R, Liu P, Huang K.

records.title: Combination antiviral treatment for a patient with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus meningoencephalitis associated with bispecific antibody teclistamab therapy for myeloma.
records.abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans. Although LCMV is a rodent zoonosis with a global distribution, no UK cases in humans have been reported in published literature since the 1950s, and testing is rarely performed. LCMV meningoencephalitis is self-limiting in people who are immunocompetent, but infection in hosts who are immunocompromised causes severe disease. We report a presentation of LCMV meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab. The patient presented with a 5-month history of progressive neurological symptoms, including hearing loss, ataxia, headache, and weight loss. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, markedly elevated protein concentration, and hypoglycorrhachia. Extensive microbiological and autoimmune investigations were negative, and empirical antimicrobial and antituberculosis therapies did not prevent clinical deterioration. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of CSF identified LCMV, and a history of domestic rodent exposure was subsequently identified. Combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir was initiated. Molnupiravir was later substituted for favipiravir, and favipiravir dosing was guided by serum and CSF therapeutic drug monitoring. The patient showed sustained neurological improvement, with clearance of LCMV from CSF and blood within 2 months. Antiviral therapy continued for 6 months. The patient regained functional independence and returned to work, with only mild residual symptoms. In addition to reporting a novel occurrence of LCMV infection in a patient on teclistamab, the case highlights the presence of LCMV in the UK and the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen identification in undiagnosed encephalitis. Finally, the case provides preliminary evidence supporting combination antiviral therapy in persistent LCMV infection.

records.title: Characterization and domain dissection of a PL39 alginate lyase algtm3 from the marine thermophile Rhodothermus profundi.
records.abstract: Alginate lyases are important biocatalysts for the preparation of bioactive alginate oligosaccharides from brown algae. However, the application of currently available alginate lyases is often constrained by insufficient thermostability and catalytic efficiency. In this study, a PL39 family alginate lyase, designated Algtm3, was identified from the thermophilic deep-sea bacterium Rhodothermus profundi (type strain PRI 2902ᵀ = DSM 22212ᵀ = JCM 15944ᵀ) through genome mining, heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli, and systematically characterized. Algtm3 exhibited optimal activity at 70 °C and pH 8.0, and retained more than 90% of its initial activity after incubation at 65 °C for 60 min, indicating excellent thermal stability. Domain truncation analysis revealed that the Chondroitin AC/alginate lyase superfamily domain and the Hepar_II_III catalytic domain are essential for maintaining proper protein folding, soluble production, and catalytic activity. In contrast, deletion of the C-terminal T9SS sorting domain improved enzyme performance in the heterologous expression system, with the truncated variant Algtm3dc exhibiting a 1.98-fold higher activity than the wild-type enzyme. Structural modeling and molecular docking analyses suggested that C-terminal truncation preserved the catalytic core while inducing local changes in the substrate-binding region, which may contribute to enhanced catalytic efficiency. TLC and ESI-MS analyses demonstrated that Algtm3 could degrade sodium alginate, polyM, and polyG, producing alginate oligosaccharides mainly with degrees of polymerization ranging from 1 to 4, and exhibited both endolytic and exolytic degradation characteristics. Collectively, these findings provide insights into the domain organization and structure-function relationship of PL39 family alginate lyases and highlight the potential of Algtm3 as a thermostable biocatalyst for the efficient production of functional alginate oligosaccharides.

records.title: Harnessing phage defense systems to develop a Burkholderia bacterial host.
records.abstract: Heterologous production of metabolites and proteins requires the transfer of foreign DNA into a host. One common barrier to the genetic engineering of bacteria is their plethora of phage defense systems. Targeted deletion of defense system components can improve DNA transfer for downstream applications. We sought to improve the transformation efficiency of Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421, a β-proteobacterial host that has great potential for the high-titer production of bioactive small molecules. We investigated restriction-modification systems and the recently described Kiwa phage defense system. Through deletion of three restriction enzyme genes, transformation efficiency was improved nearly 7-fold. The electroporation protocol was also optimized with respect to temperature, cell density, and buffer composition, which resulted in an additional 40-fold improvement in transformation efficiency, reaching 1 × 106 CFU/µg plasmid DNA. Interestingly, a mimicry by methylation approach, where DNA is pre-methylated using two host DNA methyltransferases, outperformed the transformation efficiency obtained with restriction enzyme deletion mutants nearly 3-fold. Moreover, contrary to previous reports in Escherichia coli, deletion of the Kiwa system did not improve transformation efficiency into Burkholderia sp. FERM BP-3421. Understanding the impact of bacterial innate immune systems on genetic tractability is vital to improving non-model host strains to produce high-value molecules of interest.ImportanceThe ability to transfer DNA into bacteria is key to genetic engineering. However, bacteria have evolved immune defenses to recognize and protect themselves from foreign DNA, thwarting genetic manipulation. Here, we identified putative defense systems in a β-proteobacterial strain of interest and characterized their impact on DNA transfer. The defense systems studied belong to the well-known class of restriction-modification systems and to the recently described Kiwa system. Intriguingly, we observed higher DNA transfer efficiency by avoiding restriction-modification systems via pre-methylation rather than by restriction gene deletion. Future studies should investigate the underlying mechanism for this difference. Moreover, contrary to what was reported for γ-proteobacteria Escherichia coli, we showed that the Kiwa system does not impair DNA transfer into the β-proteobacteria Burkholderia sp. strain. There has been significant interest in the discovery of novel defense systems. Learning more about their complexity is important to enable genetic manipulation of previously intractable strains.
records.authors: Heard SC, Ptacek GM, Kadjo AE, Eustáquio AS.

records.title: An integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq) method for the simultaneous detection of multiple enterovirus types and quantification of infectious Enterovirus B.
records.abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs) are ubiquitous contaminants of surface waters, where they can remain infectious for long periods of time. Most methods used for EV monitoring are unable to distinguish between infectious and non-infectious particles, or between EV types. Because different types exhibit both distinct environmental persistence and health implications, there is a need for type-resolved infectivity measurements. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining short-term cell culture amplification with nanopore sequencing of the VP1 gene. The ICC approach was adapted from a previously described ICC-reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR (ICC-RTqPCR) protocol, while the NanoporeSeq workflow was derived from a clinical EV typing protocol and optimized for environmentally circulating EV types. Using samples containing known concentrations of 10 EV types, the NanoporeSeq method accurately and reproducibly recovered the original proportions of all EV types after correction of biases. When applied to wastewater extracts, the method detected 45 EV types across five species. Furthermore, type-specific calibration curves generated with ICC-NanoporeSeq enabled quantification of the infectious concentrations of six EV types of the Enterovirus B species, allowing a simultaneous and type-resolved assessment of infectivity in mixed samples. Overall, ICC-NanoporeSeq provides a scalable approach for the parallel analysis of multiple EV types. Compared with the predecessor ICC-RTqPCR method, it eliminates the need for multiple type-specific PCR primers, and can therefore be readily expanded to include additional EV types.IMPORTANCECurrent methods used to detect enteroviruses (EVs) in environmental samples generally measure viral genome copies without determining whether viruses remain infectious, limiting their use in public health risk assessment or water quality monitoring. At the same time, available infectivity assays are often labor-intensive and cannot distinguish between different EV types. Here, we developed integrated cell culture-nanopore sequencing (ICC-NanoporeSeq), a method combining cell culture and nanopore sequencing to simultaneously quantify the infectious concentrations of multiple EV types in samples containing mixed EV populations. The method provides an efficient and scalable approach for studying EVs in complex environmental matrices. ICC-NanoporeSeq has potential applications in wastewater-based epidemiology, environmental surveillance, and disinfection studies, where understanding the persistence of different EV types simultaneously is crucial.
records.authors: Astorch-Cardona A, Rouault S, Kohn T.

records.title: PCR-amplified blaKPC-2-triggered Cas12a activation coupled with DNA cube-confined Fc reporter cleavage on a Ti<sub>3</sub>C<sub>2</sub>/CsPbBr<sub>3</sub>@PDA@Au/GCE dual-mode ECL/SERS interface.
records.abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of antibiotic resistance genes is essential for guiding antimicrobial therapy and controlling the spread of carbapenem-resistant pathogens. Herein, we developed a PCR amplicon-activated CRISPR/Cas12a-regulated dual-mode electrochemiluminescence/surface-enhanced Raman scattering biosensor for sensitive detection of the blaKPC-2 resistance gene. A specific blaKPC-2 fragment containing the selected TTTG PAM region was amplified by PCR and used as a double-stranded DNA activator for the crRNA/Cas12a complex. After target recognition, activated Cas12a cleaved the Fc-labeled reporter segments integrated into a DNA cube scaffold assembled on the Ti3C2/CsPbBr3@PDA@Au nanocomposite interface. In the initial state, Fc was positioned close to the Ti3C2/CsPbBr3@PDA@Au-modified GCE surface, resulting in ECL quenching and strong SERS emission. Upon Cas12a-mediated cleavage of the exposed ssDNA reporter segments, Fc-containing fragments were released from the interface, leading to ECL recovery and SERS attenuation. Therefore, the target-induced process enabled an anti-correlated ECL-on/SERS-off signal conversion, and the ratiometric value R = IECL/ISERS was used for quantitative analysis. The concentration-dependent response was empirically fitted over 10-107 copies per µL, whereas the 108 copies per µL group exhibited upper-range response compression. Boundary back-calculation indicated that further quantitative validation is required. Blank-response inverse prediction gave a model-dependent response-equivalent concentration of approximately 1.06 copies per µL; Poisson sampling gave a 95% molecular-sampling threshold of approximately 3.0 copies per µL for a 1.0 µL input. Neither descriptor is an experimentally determined detection or quantification limit. The platform also exhibited good selectivity against other resistance genes and non-target bacterial genomic DNA, together with satisfactory repeatability, reproducibility, stability, and acceptable spike-recovery performance in 10% diluted serum as a model biological matrix, providing preliminary evidence of matrix tolerance rather than clinical validation. This work provides a self-calibrated dual-mode strategy for antibiotic resistance gene detection, while further validation using bacterial lysates, extracted bacterial genomic DNA, and clinical bacterial isolates is required before diagnostic application. qPCR supported linear amplification over 10-107 copies per µL; endpoint responses remained observable through 108 copies per µL, where quantitative resolution was reduced.
records.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
records.authors: Chen Y, Huang J, Wen L, Zhu Q, Liu J, Meng J, Yu L.

records.title: Antibacterial and Virulence-Modulating Activities of Bacillus velezensis JM3 Against Pectobacterium carotovorum subsp. carotovorum PCC21.
records.abstract: Bacterial soft-rot caused by Pectobacterium carotovorum subsp. carotovorum (Pcc) is associated with quorum sensing (QS), motility, and plant cell wall degrading enzymes. In this study, strain JM3, isolated from the rhizosphere of Chinese cabbage, was identified as Bacillus velezensis based on gyrB, 16S rRNA and rpoB phylogenetic analyses. JM3 showed strong antibacterial activity against Pcc strain PCC21 and significantly reduced soft-rot lesions in Chinese cabbage leaf sections. An ethyl acetate extract of the JM3 cell-free supernatant (CFS) showed concentration-dependent antibacterial activity, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 1 mg/mL. The acid-treated cell-free supernatant (AT-CFS), following acid treatment of the JM3 CFS and removal of the resulting precipitate, showed markedly reduced antibacterial activity, with an MIC of 8 mg/mL. At 0.5 mg/mL (1/16 MIC), AT-CFS did not markedly affect PCC21 growth but reduced N-acyl homoserine lactone associated signals, swarming motility, and extracellular protease, pectate lyase, and cellulase activities. RT-qPCR analysis revealed reduced expression of QS-related genes (expI and expR), extracellular enzyme genes (pelB, pehA, celA, and prt1), and motilityassociated genes (motA and flhC). These findings suggest that JM3 antagonizes PCC21 through both direct growth inhibition and extracellular activities affecting QS and virulence-associated traits under growth-noninhibitory conditions. The results provide a basis for further characterization of JM3 derived extracellular metabolites involved in interactions with the soft-rot pathogen.
records.authors: Lee D, Seo H, Kang M, Jeong T, Seo G, Jung Y, Seo YS.

records.title: A timeline for evolution of metabolism in early microbes
records.abstract: The metabolism of early microbes shaped our planet's chemistry and enabled more life to evolve. However, it remains uncertain when many forms of metabolism arose and which organisms carried them out. Here we combine machine learning, metabolic networks, and phylogenomics of microbes to date 14 forms of metabolism and 6 other traits. We find that metabolism evolved in three waves, starting >3.4 billion years ago (Ga) with fermentation and sulfur compound respiration. A second wave began ~3.2 Ga with aerobic respiration and growth, while a third began ~1.4 Ga with further specialization. We compared these predictions with independent dates from the geochemical record, and agreement with conservative dates was good (CCC = 0.81 to 0.89). Several forms of metabolism are invisible in the geochemical record, and our approach dates these forms, too. Our results reconcile different lines of evidence for microbial evolution and provide a fuller picture of early Earth.
records.authors: Hackmann T.

records.title: RNA-triggered Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and resistance plasmid degradation
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates programmable antibacterial strategies with novel mechanisms. Here, we evaluated an inducible intracellular CRISPR/Cas12a2 system in engineered  Escherichia coli targeting a chloramphenicol-resistance (Chl) transcript. Cas12a2 activation significantly delayed bacterial growth and reduced recoverable colony-forming units (CFU) by 3-log  10 in vitro , and reduced bacterial burdens in a mouse skin wound model. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of  recA , a key mediator of the SOS response. We therefore designed a Chl-  recA dual-targeting construct, which produced a greater growth delay than either single-targeting counterpart. The optimized dual-targeting system led to an approximately 4-log  10 reduction in bacterial burden  in vivo . Furthermore, exploratory qPCR of culture supernatants suggested a treatment-associated decrease in amplifiable plasmid DNA. Overall, this study provides proof-of-concept for resistance-transcript-guided Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and highlights the potential of co-targeting stress-associated transcripts to enhance programmable antimicrobials.
records.authors: Bai Y, Song Y, Gu W, Wu H, Liu Y.

records.title: The  Pseudomonas protegens  PBL3 secretome exerts antimicrobial activity against  Burkholderia glumae  by disrupting cell envelope homeostasis and impairing bacterial replication
records.abstract: The effectiveness of antimicrobials used to manage bacterial infections is increasingly threatened by the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. Many conventional antimicrobials act on a single defined target that pathogens can circumvent through target modification or pathway adaptation. In contrast, antimicrobials that disrupt multiple cellular processes may impose greater fitness costs and reduce the likelihood of resistance development, making their discovery a priority for pharmaceutical and agricultural applications. We previously demonstrated that the environmental bacterium  Pseudomonas protegens PBL3 secretes a complex mixture of molecules (secretome) with antimicrobial activity against several plants and human pathogens. However, the mechanism underlying this activity remained unknown. Here, we used the plant pathogen  Burkholderia glumae to investigate the mode of action of the  P. protegens PBL3 secretome. We showed that the  P. protegens PLB3 secretome causes extensive cell envelope damage that results in cell death and interferes with bacterial multiplication. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed broad disruption of processes associated with cell-envelope biogenesis and homeostasis and bacterial replication. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the  P. protegens PBL3 secretome acts as a multi-target antimicrobial that could be harnessed in the development of therapeutics to control bacterial infections of agricultural and medical importance.
records.authors: Ojha B, Anderson D, Altartouri B, Husein G, Rojas CM.
