records.title: Synergistic antibiotic activity and integrated genomic-metabolomic profiling of patch- and plaque-derived Staphylococcus aureus in mycosis fungoides.
records.abstract: Mycosis fungoides (MF), the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, is frequently associated with skin dysbiosis, and advanced lesions are often dominated by multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. To characterize microbiologically relevant properties of MF-associated S. aureus, we evaluated synergistic antibiotic combinations and performed integrated phenotypic, genomic, and metabolomic profiling. Several antibiotic combinations, most notably carbenicillin combined with either gentamicin or levofloxacin, exhibited pronounced synergistic activity and restored in vitro antimicrobial activity against highly resistant isolates. Comparative genomic analyses revealed substantial variability between isolates in resistomes and virulence repertoires, including enterotoxins, immune-evasion, and stress-response factors. Metabolomic profiling further revealed isolate-specific extracellular signatures, including putrescine and urocanic acid. In summary, this study identifies promising antibiotic combinations against multidrug-resistant S. aureus strains. Furthermore, this exploratory investigation demonstrates phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity among MF-associated S. aureus isolates, warranting further evaluation in larger longitudinal studies.ImportanceDespite its predominance in advanced mycosis fungoides (MF) lesions, the role of multidrug‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus in adverse clinical outcomes remains poorly understood. Bridging the gap between clinical observations and microbiological mechanisms is essential to clarify how S. aureus persists in MF skin and to identify therapeutic alternatives for S. aureus‑positive patients, for whom treatment options remain limited. This study addresses two major clinical needs: the lack of effective antibiotic strategies and the limited understanding of bacterial factors that may contribute to worsened clinical outcomes. By integrating synergistic antibiotic testing with genomic, phenotypic, and metabolomic profiling, our work highlights clinically relevant heterogeneity among MF-associated S. aureus isolates. These findings identify promising therapeutic directions and establish a framework for future large-scale longitudinal studies to better understand the role of diverse S. aureus strains in MF pathogenesis.
records.authors: Straub FA, Serbin LK, Barkani IE, Grünewald C, Mailänder V, Dominelli N.

records.title: Development of a TaqMan probe-based PCR for the detection of porcine bocavirus group 3 and identification of a novel genotype strain.
records.abstract: For specific detection of porcine bocavirus (PBoV) group 3 (G3), we developed a TaqMan probe-based real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the NS1 gene. The correlation coefficient and amplification efficiency of the PCR were 0.994 and 102.9%, respectively. There were no cross-reactions of the PCR with the genomes of classical swine fever virus, porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus, porcine parvovirus, porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV), transmissible gastroenteritis virus (TGEV), and porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV), and the detection limit of the PCR was 100 copies per reaction. The coefficients of variation of the inter-assay and intra-assay of the PCR were 1.38-2.71% and 0.23-0.67%, respectively. A total of 719 field samples collected from Xinjiang, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, and Shaanxi Provinces were detected via the developed PCR, and the positive rates were 80.82%, 44.51%, 97.50%, 98.94%, and 93.60%, respectively. In addition, coinfections of PBoV G3 with PEDV/TGEV/PDCoV/PCV2 were determined, and dual infections, triple infections, quadruple infections, and quintuple infections were observed. Furthermore, the complete genome sequences of 10 positive samples (two per province) randomly selected from five provinces were determined, and phylogenetic analysis placed all 10 within PBoV G3, but one strain formed a distinct branch, indicating it was a novel strain in PBoV G3. The established PCR provides a reliable tool for PBoV G3 detection and facilitates the understanding of its distribution and prevalence.ImportancePorcine bocavirus (PBoV) poses a threat to swine health and has potential public health significance. Owing to the high nucleotide diversity of PBoV, existing detection methods may yield false-negative results. A reliable detection method is needed to monitor its prevalence. Given that porcine bocavirus group 3 (PBoV G3) is the predominant group circulating in Chinese pig populations, we established a rapid and sensitive TaqMan probe-based polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for detection of PBoV G3. We detected 719 field samples collected from northwest China by the PCR and analyzed coinfections of PBoV G3 with porcine epidemic diarrhea virus/transmissible gastroenteritis virus/porcine deltacoronavirus PCV2. The results showed that the positive rate of PBoV G3 was high, and dual infections, triple infections, quadruple infections, and quintuple infections were present. Furthermore, a novel genotype was identified in PBoV G3. Taken together, the developed PCR facilitates the prevalence investigation of PBoV G3. The results enrich the data on the distribution and prevalence of PBoV G3 in China.
records.authors: Gong C, Zhong Q, Lu Y, Li B, Yang B, Yang J, Liu G, Fu Y.

records.title: Identification and characterization of a periplasmic phosphate-binding protein in phosphorus-starved Pyropia yezoensis.
records.abstract: The synthesis of several polypeptides (145, 76, 66, 52, 42, 32, and 16 kDa) in Pyropia yezoensis was markedly induced under phosphorus-starved conditions. The most abundant 32-kDa polypeptide was purified and characterized. Comparison of the genomic and cDNA sequences revealed an intronless gene encoding a 323-amino-acid precursor protein with a 24-amino-acid signal peptide and a 299-amino-acid mature protein. The mature 32-kDa polypeptide showed high sequence similarity to periplasmic phosphate-binding proteins (PBPs) from Escherichia coli and marine cyanobacteria. Both the native and recombinant proteins exhibited phosphate-binding ability in equilibrium dialysis assays. Immunological analyses indicated that the phosphorus-starvation-induced 32-kDa PBP is localized to the periplasmic space. Northern blot and quantitative real-time PCR analyses demonstrated that PBP gene expression was strongly induced by phosphorus starvation. These findings support a model of phosphate acquisition in P. yezoensis under phosphorus-starved conditions involving a periplasmic PBP and alkaline phosphatase.
records.authors: Miwa Y, Yano Y, Kono T, Yoshimizu M, Yamagishi Y.

records.title: Nuclear cGAS governs transcription to control lipid metabolism, tumor growth, and therapy response.
records.abstract: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) is a cytosolic DNA sensor critical for host defense against microbial infections. To prevent aberrant activation, nuclear cGAS is restrained by nucleosome tethering or by barrier-to-autointegration factor-mediated restriction of its access to DNA. However, its physiological roles beyond enzymatic suppression in the nucleus remain poorly understood. Here, we present a genome-wide map of cGAS chromatin localization in human cells and unexpectedly find its binding beyond nucleosome tethering, where cGAS is recruited to chromatin by AP-1 transcription factors via a potentially previously uncharacterized transactivation domain. Integrated CUT&RUN, RNA-seq, and metabolomics analyses reveal that cGAS transcriptionally regulates cholesterol homeostasis. Mechanistically, cGAS promotes LGALS3 transcription, which inhibits ACAA2 activity to suppress fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-CoA production, thereby lowering intracellular cholesterol levels. Reduced cholesterol lowers plasma membrane phosphatidylinositol [3,4,5] triphosphate [PI(3,4,5)P3] levels and decreases mTOR complex 2 (mTORC2) activation. In contrast, cGAS depletion results in cholesterol accumulation and elevated PI(3,4,5)P3, driving mTORC2/Akt signaling, promoting xenografted tumor growth, and conferring resistance to DNA-damaging agents. In vivo, the elevated hepatic cholesterol levels observed in cGas-/- mice were largely reversed by inhibition of Akt but not STING, whereas cGAS deficiency had minimal effects on lung physiology. Collectively, our findings uncover an unexpected role for nuclear cGAS in orchestrating a transcriptional program that links lipid metabolism to cell proliferation, stress response, and cholesterol homeostasis in liver.

records.title: High-efficiency antimony biomineralization by Serratia nematodiphila: process optimization and integrated genomic-transcriptomic-proteomic analysis.
records.abstract: This study aims to elucidate the transcriptional, protein expression and mineral crystallization response mechanisms of the Serratia nematodiphila strain during the process of converting Sb3+ into Sb2O3 through integrating multi-omics methods and various mineral analysis techniques. The isolate Serratia nematodiphila (MIC > 250 mM) achieved 96.18% Sb3+ removal under Box-Behnken-optimized conditions (27.7 ℃, pH 4.67, 205.6 rpm). Time-resolved SEM-EDS, Raman, XRD, and XPS revealed a non-classical mineralization pathway from an amorphous precursor to crystalline Sb2O3 within 36 h. Integrated genomic-transcriptomic-proteomic analyses resolved a coordinated physiological response: (1) energy metabolic remodeling via upregulated TCA cycle and fatty acid β-oxidation and suppressed anaerobic respiration, may help sustain NAD(P)H and proton motive force that could support ArsB-mediated efflux; (2) Fe-S cluster repair and metal sequestration through Suf assembly, iron/siderophore uptake, and molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis; (3) multi-level antioxidant defense via glutathione, catalase/peroxidase, and SoxR/OxyR systems; and (4) motility suppression, conserving energy and protons while enhanced capsule/EPS functions promote Sb adsorption and mineral nucleation. Together, these processes may promote the hydrolysis and precipitation of aqueous Sb3+ species, leading to the formation of crystalline Sb2O3. Serratia nematodiphila orchestrates a coordinated metabolic reprogramming that enhances energy generation, metal sequestration, and oxidative defense while suppressing motility, effectively transforming toxic aqueous Sb3+ into valuable crystalline Sb2O3. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for engineering microbial-based bioremediation and resource recovery from antimony-polluted environments.

records.title: An integrative single-cell epigenomic atlas annotates the regulatory genome of the adult mouse brain.
records.abstract: Histone modifications underpin the cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs that drive the remarkable cellular diversity of the mammalian brain. Here, we jointly profiled four histone modifications and the transcriptome in 2.5 million nuclei from the adult mouse brain. By integrating these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and three-dimensional genome organization, we constructed a unified epigenomic atlas spanning over 100 brain cell subclasses and assigned active, primed, and repressive chromatin states across 81% of the genome. Active chromatin states marked by combinatorial histone modifications better nominate candidate enhancers with functional support than chromatin accessibility alone, while H3K27me3- and H3K9me3-marked chromatin states delineate distinct modes of cell-type-specific gene repression. Finally, this multimodal resource enables the development of deep learning models that predict cell-type-specific epigenomic features and gene expression from DNA sequence, providing a comprehensive framework for annotating the brain regulatory genome and interpreting non-coding disease risk variants.

records.title: Single-cell multimodal atlas reveals regulatory programs in the human brain.
records.abstract: Direct measurement of chromatin states together with transcription is essential for understanding how cell-type-specific regulatory programs are established and maintained in the adult human brain. Here, we present a large-scale single-cell multimodal atlas by jointly profiling the transcriptome with active (H3K27ac) or repressive (H3K27me3) histone modifications across 18 adult brain regions. We targeted over 750,000 nuclei spanning 160 cell types and integrated these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, 3D genome architecture, and spatial transcriptomes. This framework resolved chromatin states for over 500,000 candidate regulatory elements, identified enhancer-gene links and regulatory programs, revealed Polycomb-associated ultra-long-range contacts, and uncovered brainwide epigenomic heterogeneity. We further developed a sequence-to-function model to predict cell-type-specific effects of candidate neurological disease variants. Finally, comparative analyses across species reveal conservation in active regulatory programs but divergence in repressive programs. Together, this study provides a comprehensive epigenomic reference for interpreting regulatory principles and epigenetic memory underlying human brain organization and disease.

records.title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia.
records.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet cell-type-resolved epigenomic and 3D genome maps of the human BG remain limited. Here, we present a multimodal single-cell atlas of DNA methylation (261,331 nuclei) and 3D chromatin conformation (229,286 nuclei) from eight subregions, harmonized under the BG consensus taxonomy and integrated with matched data across multiple regulatory layers. We identify millions of differentially methylated regions across cell types, enriched for distinct transcription factor motifs, and link them to disease-associated heritability. We characterize the POU6F2+ STR D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neuron (SPN) subtype, with concordant signatures across multiple modalities, and reveal region-specific methylation and contact gradients. Integrative gene regulatory networks (GRNs) predict cell-type-resolved enhancer-promoter interactions, nominating candidate regulatory mechanisms for Parkinson's disease (PD) risk variants at SNCA. Finally, multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) profiling combined with cross-species Patch-seq identifies a neuronal subtype, STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA, with electrophysiological differences across the striatal matrix-striosome (MS) boundary.

records.title: Taxonomic descriptions of Tessaracoccus zhenghani sp. nov., Tessaracoccus pujii sp. nov., Tessaracoccus luoxuelianae sp. nov. and Tessaracoccus yangjingae sp. nov.
records.abstract: Eight Gram-stain-positive, non-spore-forming, non-motile, oxidase-negative novel bacterial strains with oval- to rod-shaped morphology designated Y36ᵀ, Y1639, Z1128ᵀ, Y1544, Y1736ᵀ, W1776, G1721ᵀ and Y1940 were isolated from the in situ coal and coal mine dust matrices in Shanxi Province, PR China. Phylogenetic analysis of the 16S rRNA gene and 813 core genes revealed that these 8 strains belong to the genus Tessaracoccus. 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis revealed that strain Y36T exhibited the highest similarity to Tessaracoccus lubricantis KSS-17SeT (98.42%), while strains Z1128T, Y1736T and G1721T showed the highest similarities to Tessaracoccus aquimaris NSG39T (98.61%, 98.47% and 97.64%, respectively). Average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) values between these four novel species and all members of the genus Tessaracoccus were below species thresholds (95-96% for ANI and 70% for dDDH). Anteiso-C15:0 was the predominant cellular fatty acid in all eight isolates. Summed feature 3 (C16:1ω7c/C16:1ω6c) was also a major component in strains Z1128ᵀ, Y1544, Y1736ᵀ, W1776, G1721ᵀ and Y1940. Strain Y1736ᵀ additionally contained anteiso-C17:1ω9c as a major fatty acid. All novel type strains had MK-9 (H4) as the sole respiratory quinone. The major polar lipids of strains Y36ᵀ and Y1736ᵀ were diphosphatidylglycerol and phosphatidylglycerol. Strains Z1128ᵀ and G1721ᵀ contained diphosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylinositol mannoside as their major polar lipids. Strains Y36ᵀ and G1721ᵀ contained ribose as the sole cell-wall sugar. Strain Z1128ᵀ had ribose and glucose, while strain Y1736ᵀ harboured rhamnose, ribose and glucose as the major cell-wall sugars. The cell-wall peptidoglycan contained ʟʟ-diaminopimelic acid as the diagnostic diamino acid. Based on genotypic, phenotypic, phylogenetic and biochemical properties, the eight uncharacterized strains represent four novel species in the genus Tessaracoccus, for which the names Tessaracoccus zhenghani sp. nov. (type Y36T=GDMCC 1.5638T=KCTC 59558T), Tessaracoccus pujii sp. nov. (type strain Z1128T=GDMCC 1.5727T=KCTC 59595T), Tessaracoccus luoxuelianae sp. nov. (type strain Y1736T=GDMCC 1.5728T=KCTC 59596T) and Tessaracoccus yangjingae sp. nov. (type strain G1721T=GDMCC 1.5729T=KCTC 59594T) are proposed, respectively.
records.journal: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology
records.authors: Gao F, Chen Y, He Y, Zhao L, Xie J, Du X, Yang Q, Liu T, Yang C, Kang Z, Du X, Pu J, Zheng H, Xu J, Dong K.

records.title: Immobilized Epiphytic Bacteria Enhance Macrophyte Suppression of a Bloom-Forming Cyanobacterium.
records.abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms are an increasing threat to freshwater ecosystems and water security worldwide. Biological control using macrophytes or algicidal bacteria is often studied separately despite natural co-occurrence. Here we show that the epiphytic bacterium Priestia megaterium strain BW, isolated from submerged macrophytes, exhibits strong algicidal activity and forms an enhanced suppression system with its host plant Vallisneria natans. Pre-colonization of BW on V. natans leaves achieves > 80% inhibition of Microcystis aeruginosa biomass within 5 days. When immobilized on a ceramic material carrier, BW rapidly suppresses algal photosynthetic efficiency within 48 h. Mechanistically, the algicidal effect follows a multi-pathway process involving early photosynthetic impairment, oxidative stress and subsequent cellular disintegration. Notably, the combined application of immobilized BW with V. natans produces stronger and faster suppression than either the bacterium or the plant alone. Our findings demonstrate that an epiphytic bacterium can retain potent algicidal activity outside its native biofilm and that its efficacy is markedly enhanced when re-integrated with the plant, providing direct evidence for plant-microbe synergistic control of cyanobacterial blooms.
records.authors: Zheng Y, Zhang K, Lei S, Jeppesen E, Iversen LL, Wang L, Zhang W.

records.title: Beyond who is there: Industrialization shifts gut microbial ecology and evolution.
records.abstract: The relationship between industrialization and the gut microbiome remains incompletely understood due to limitations in cohort design involving host physiology and bacterial isolates. Two recent studies from the Global Microbiome Conservancy link industrialization to lower microbiome diversity and stability, altered host immune markers, and gene gain in gut bacteria.

records.title: Brassinosteroid and Light Quality Synergistically Regulate Aroma Biosynthesis via the CmBES1-4-CmDof13 Module in Postharvest Oriental Melon (Cucumis melo).
records.abstract: Brassinosteroids and light quality regulate secondary metabolism in fruits, yet the synergistic control of volatile aroma biosynthesis in oriental melon (Cucumis melo var. makuwa) remains unclear. In this study, we used volatile metabolomics, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and DNA Affinity Purification Sequencing (DAP-seq) methods to show that red light combined with brassinosteroids effectively increased total volatiles, particularly esters, at day 6 after harvest. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a module strongly associated with ester content, in which the brassinosteroid-responsive transcription factor CmBES1-4 co-occurred with CmDof13 and the downstream target genes CmLOX18 and CmAAT1. DAP-seq analysis revealed that CmBES1-4 bound E-box and BRRE motifs genome-wide, thereby directly targeting CmDof13. Dual-luciferase, yeast one-hybrid, and EMSA assays confirmed that CmBES1-4 activated CmDof13 expression via E-box binding. These findings identified a novel light/BR-CmBES1-4-CmDof13-ester biosynthesis regulatory module, which provided theoretical insights for improving postharvest aroma quality in oriental melon.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Zhang C, Ju M, Wang Z, Pang H, Zhang Y, Chen Q, Wu X.

records.title: l-Arginine Ameliorates IBS-D by Modulating the Ligilactobacillus murinus-LCA-FXR/eNOS Signaling Axis.
records.abstract: l-Arginine is a semiessential amino acid with diverse metabolic functions and has been implicated in gastrointestinal health through interactions with the gut microbiota; however, its therapeutic potential in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) remains unclear. Here, an IBS-D mouse model was established in C57BL/6J mice, and multiomics analyses combined with in vivo and in vitro validation were performed to investigate the mechanisms underlying l-arginine-mediated protection. l-Arginine supplementation significantly alleviated IBS-D-like symptoms and improved intestinal barrier function. Transcriptomic analysis revealed the activation of the FXR/PI3K/AKT/eNOS signaling pathway, which was associated with enhanced nitric oxide production. Integrated metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses identified Ligilactobacillus murinus (L. murinus) as a key microbiota component associated with bile acid metabolism and eNOS expression. Furthermore, L. murinus transplantation reproduced the beneficial effects of l-arginine, and metabolomic analysis identified lithocholic acid (LCA) as a microbiota-derived metabolite involved in this process. In vitro experiments demonstrated that LCA alleviated lipopolysaccharide-induced epithelial inflammation and barrier dysfunction via FXR/eNOS activation. Collectively, these findings reveal that l-arginine ameliorates IBS-D through microbiota remodeling, LCA-mediated bile acid regulation, and activation of the colonic FXR/PI3K/AKT/eNOS axis, highlighting its potential as a microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategy.

records.title: Synbiotic of 2'-FL and B. longum subsp. infantis BXY2 Alleviates Colitis in Toddler Microbiota-Associated Mice: Potential Involvement of Gut Microbial Arachidonic Acid Metabolism.
records.abstract: Increasing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence in toddlers requires safe interventions. We developed a synbiotic combining 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) with Bifidobacterium strain and evaluated its protective efficacy against DSS-induced colitis in toddler microbiota-associated (TMA) mice. Among 30 Bifidobacterium strains, Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis BXY2 and Bifidobacterium. breve BG4 utilized 2'-FL in vitro. However, only the 2'-FL and BXY2 synbiotic significantly alleviated colitis. The 400 mg/kg 2'-FL and BXY2 synbiotic showed the greatest protective effect, restoring body weight and colon length, reducing disease activity and histological scores, improving barrier function, attenuating inflammation. Compared with 2'-FL or BXY2 alone, the synbiotic enhanced goblet cells and barrier proteins. Metagenomics revealed enrichment of B. longum subsp. infantis and Phascolarctobacterium faecium. Metabolomics showed reduced fecal arachidonic acid (AA). These results indicated that gut microbial AA metabolism might be involved in alleviating colitis in TMA mice. Thus, this synbiotic is a promising preventive strategy for toddler IBD.

records.title: The balance between R-loops and RNAPII occupancy determines the outcome of transcription-replication conflicts.
records.abstract: Maintaining genome integrity requires the precise coordination of replication and transcription. While R-loops are known to cause transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs), the precise nature of the barrier, whether it is the RNA:DNA hybrid itself, the stalled RNA Polymerase II (RNAPII), or a combination of both, remains elusive. Using live-cell imaging in yeast to monitor a single R-loop prone locus in real time, we demonstrate that wild-type replisomes traverse R-loop enriched transcription units with high efficiency. We find that while R-loops initially repress transcription, replisome passage prompts a robust recovery of transcription activity. Indeed, we discover that R-loops serve a critical regulatory function by suppressing excessive RNAPII occupancy. In an RNAPII mutant with high DNA affinity, the enzymatic removal of R-loops leads to a pile-up of RNAPII molecules, creating a barrier to replication, more severe than the R-loops themselves. Thus, our findings reveal a dual nature of R-loops: while they can be obstacles and repress transcription, they can also serve as a physiological buffer that prevents the formation of high-density RNAPII 'trains'. These findings establish that the precise regulation of both R-loop levels and RNAPII density is critical for preventing harmful TRCs and maintaining genome stability.

records.title: [The impact of Cirbp knockout on the expression of immune-related genes in the cortex of developing mice].
records.abstract: Objective To investigate how cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (Cirbp) knockout affects the expression of immune-related genes in the cerebral cortex during postnatal development. Methods Wild-type (WT) and Cirbp knockout (Cirbp-) C57BL/6 mice were euthanized at postnatal day 21 (P21), and cortical tissues were collected. Western blot was used to detect CIRBP protein expression in cortical tissues. Transcriptome sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), thereby facilitating the identification of key immune-related genes. Candidate genes were validated using real-time quantitative PCR. Results Western blot confirmed the absence of CIRBP protein expression in the cortex of Cirbp- mice. Compared with the WT group, transcriptomic analysis identified 268 DEGs in the cortex of Cirbp- mice, of which 118 were upregulated and 150 were downregulated. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis showed that the DEGs were mainly enriched in biological processes including signal transduction, transmembrane transport, and positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis indicated that the DEGs were predominantly enriched in the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway, and Toll-like receptor signaling pathway. REACTOME pathway enrichment revealed that the DEGs were mainly enriched in signal transduction, peptide ligand-binding receptors, and downstream signaling pathways of G protein-coupled receptors. In the protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, the identified immune-related genes in the cortex included interleukin 6 (IL-6), C-C motif chemokine ligand 4 (CCL4), CCL5, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10), cellular communication network factor 1(CCN1), and cluster of Differentiation 274 (CD274). Real-time quantitative PCR validation showed that the mRNA expression levels of these key immune-related genes were consistent with the RNA sequencing results. Conclusion Cirbp knockout significantly alters the expression of immune-related genes in the cortex of developing mice, providing candidate targets for subsequent investigations into the protein-level underlying CIRBP-mediated neuroimmune regulation.

records.title: Lipophilic Redox Mediators Reprogram Intracellular Electron Flow to Promote Arsenic Methylation in Soil Fermentative Bacteria.
records.abstract: Anaerobic arsenic (As) methylation by fermentative microorganisms, particularly Clostridium-related populations, controls As speciation, mobility, and volatilization in flooded paddy soils, yet the mechanisms promoting this process remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that phenazine- and phenoxazine-like redox mediators can enhance anaerobic As methylation via reshaping the intracellular electron allocation in a representative As-methylating fermentative bacterium. We integrated As speciation analysis, metabolite profiling, proteomics, and metabolic-flux modeling to determine how resazurin, as a represenative lipophilic redox mediator, reshapes fermentative metabolism and methylated As (MeAs) formation. The membrane-permeable redox mediator resazurin increased the apparent rate constant of MeAs formation by up to fourfold relative to the hydrophilic mediator anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid (AQDS). Unlike AQDS, resazurin enhanced dimethylarsine formation while establishing a more reducing intracellular environment by diverting electrons from hydrogen evolution, indicating altered intracellular electron disposal. At the proteomic level, resazurin induced coordinated increases in As(III) methyltransferase (ArsM) and proteins involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) biosynthesis, representing the primary molecular responses associated with enhanced As methylation. Proteins involved in amino-acid-fueled energy conservation and redox homeostasis were also enriched, potentially creating favorable cellular conditions for SAM-dependent As methylation. In a paddy-soil-derived fermentative consortium, resazurin likewise enhanced MeAs production and increased transcript levels of Clostridium-associated arsM and the SAM synthetase gene (metK). These findings identify lipophilicity-dependent, redox-compound-mediated intracellular electron flow reprogramming as a previously underappreciated control on anaerobic As methylation and provide a mechanistic basis for predicting MeAs formation in flooded soil environments.

records.title: Electron Transfer at Microbe-Mineral Interfaces: From Molecular Mechanisms to Ecosystem-Scale Biogeochemical Cycling and Remediation.
records.abstract: Microbe-mineral electron transfer (MMET) drives key microbial processes and biogeochemical cycling, but linking these microscopic interactions to ecosystem-scale dynamics remains a major challenge. MMET couples intracellular metabolism to extracellular mineral transformations. The resulting changes in mineral redox state and reactivity can, in turn, influence microbial energy conservation and metabolism. MMET flux could therefore provide a quantitative link between nanometer-scale electron exchange and larger-scale biogeochemical processes. In energy-limited and contaminated environments, electroactive microorganisms may transfer electrons to or acquire electrons from redox-active minerals, depending on their metabolic capabilities and local redox conditions. These interactions can support energy conservation, mitigate toxic stress, and generate localized zones of high biogeochemical activity. As their effects accumulate across space and time, microscale electron transfer may influence ecosystem-scale elemental cycling, microbial community succession, organic carbon stabilization, and contaminant fate. Building on established modeling approaches, we suggest that integrating individual-based models (IBMs) with genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) could translate spatially heterogeneous, genome-informed microbial responses into collective MMET fluxes across scales while accounting for key thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. More broadly, progress requires characterizing electroactive microbial diversity and mechanisms, engineering microbe-mineral interfaces through computational design and synthetic biology, and translating MMET principles into scalable environmental applications.
records.authors: Liu J, Wu Z, Feng X, Shi L, Rosso KM.

records.title: Epigenome, Microbiome, and Metabolites: Unraveling the Complex Pathogenesis of Celiac Disease.
records.abstract: Celiac disease (CeD) is a chronic autoimmune disease triggered by gluten consumption in genetically susceptible individuals, primarily those with HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 haplotypes. Although these genetic factors are responsible for a substantial portion of disease risk, they do not fully explain disease heritability or the rising incidence observed worldwide. Recent clinical studies highlight epigenetic modifications-including DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNA regulation, and RNA methylation-as critical mediators bridging genetic susceptibility and environmental influences, such as gut microbiota dysbiosis, dietary patterns, early-life exposures, infections, and pharmaceutical interventions. These epigenetic mechanisms modulate immune responses, intestinal barrier function, and inflammatory pathways, contributing to the loss of gluten tolerance and perpetuation of mucosal damage. Key players, including tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), form amplifying feedback loops that exacerbate pathogenesis. Bacterial metabolites and lifestyle factors further influence epigenetic landscapes, offering reversible targets for intervention. This review synthesizes current evidence on epigenetic alterations in CeD, emphasizing their interplay with microbiota and metabolites, tissue-specific patterns, and potential as biomarkers. It also explores implications for novel therapeutic strategies beyond the gluten-free diet, including epigenetic modulators and microbiota-targeted approaches, to advance personalized prevention and management of CeD.
records.authors: Atoom AM, Allela OQB, Nayak PP, Arora V, Singla S, Athab ZH, Urazbaeva D, Usmanov R.

records.title: Long-Term Acclimation and Membrane Lipid Remodelling Enable Anaerobic Oxidation of Methane at Low-pH by 'Ca. Methanoperedens vercellensis'.
records.abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea are key members of the methane cycle, preventing emissions of the potent greenhouse gas into the atmosphere. Previous studies of freshwater anaerobic methanotrophs targeted their activity at circumneutral pH whereas molecular ecology studies detected anaerobic methane oxidizers in acidic environments such as peatlands. However, it remains unclear whether they can adapt to low pH and sustain an effective biological methane filter under acidic conditions. Here, we show that a granular enrichment culture of the freshwater methanotroph 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remains metabolically active down to pH 5.65 with appropriate acclimation time while it loses activity when experiencing immediate acid stress. Population-wide acclimation is required to support anaerobic methane oxidation at lower pH. Archaeal lipid analyses revealed an increased abundance of zwitterionic intact polar lipids over anionic lipids. This coincided with structural changes in biomass granules while methane oxidation rate and enrichment proportion of 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remained stable. These results demonstrate that 'Ca. M. vercellensis' remains metabolically active at lower pH values, despite increased maintenance energy requirements and the need for cytoplasmic pH homeostasis. Furthermore, they highlight that stress adaptations in slow-growing microorganisms requires long-term observation. Our findings provide new insights into methane cycling in acidic ecosystems.
records.authors: Tláskal V, Egas RA, Wang W, Zhao X, Wissink M, Echeveste Medrano MJ, Becker KW, Elling FJ, Welte CU.

records.title: A Bacterial Extracellular Matrix Protein Forms a Supramolecular Metallogel.
records.abstract: The microbial extracellular matrix (ECM) is a complex network of self-secreted biopolymers that unite cells in biofilms, providing them with structural integrity and protection from antimicrobials. Made of fibrillar proteins interspersed with polysaccharides, ECM material is often implicitly held responsible for biofilms' hydrogel-like mechanical signature; the exact molecular mechanisms of the ECM assembly and their link to hydrogel formation, however, remain enigmatic. Here, we discover that in the presence of zinc ions, TasA, the major ECM protein of Bacillus subtilis, forms hydrogels that recapitulate the mechanical properties of whole biofilms. Electron and atomic force microscopies as well as small-angle X-ray scattering showed that cross-linking with zinc ions induced a transition in the TasA architecture from one-dimensional fibers to two-dimensional nanosheets. Electron paramagnetic resonance and X-ray diffraction data link this dramatic morphological shift to molecular changes in the coordination environment of zinc ions and protein structure. This study provides the first example and a novel molecular mechanism of supramolecular metallogelation by a native bacterial protein. Bridging between molecular processes, mesoscopic structure, and macroscopic material properties, it not only advances the fundamental understanding of ECM assembly in situ but also establishes artificial ECM-based (metallo-)hydrogels as matrix mimics for bacterial infection studies.
records.authors: Ghrayeb M, Ashman A, Mukhopadhyay S, Fellig A, Jopp J, Levi-Kalisman Y, Raviv U, Bertinetti L, Politi Y, Zaburdaev V, Ruthstein S, Chai L.

records.title: Soil Microbes Mediate Contrasting Effects of Plant Diversity on Biotic Resistance and Invasional Meltdown.
records.abstract: Biological invasions are intensifying worldwide as a major component of global change, with soil microbes increasingly recognized as key regulators of invasion outcomes. Yet how soil microbes interact with biodiversity to determine whether communities resist or facilitate invasion, particularly through their effects on plant growth and species interactions, remains unclear. Here, we conducted a two-phase feedback experiment in which soils were conditioned across a diversity gradient of native or invasive plant communities. We characterized soil fungal communities and quantified microbial effects on plant growth and species interactions between phylogenetically paired native and invasive species. Biodiversity generated contrasting invasion outcomes depending on community origin, driven by distinct microbial pathways. In native-conditioned soils, increasing diversity reduced invader dominance (biotic resistance), primarily mediated by microbial effects on interspecific competition that enhanced native competition strength while reducing that of invaders. In contrast, in invasive-conditioned soils, increasing diversity facilitated invader dominance (invasional meltdown), primarily driven by enhanced invader growth and suppression of natives. These patterns were associated with shifts in key microbial groups. Putative pathogen richness increased with increasing plant diversity and was negatively associated with native growth, whereas AMF richness declined with increasing plant diversity in native communities but increased with increasing plant diversity in invasive communities, promoting invader growth and competition strength. By integrating biodiversity-ecosystem functioning, biotic resistance, invasional meltdown, and competitive interactions within a plant-soil feedback framework, our study advances invasion ecology. It identifies soil microbes as central mediators that link biodiversity to ecosystem invasibility through distinct pathways affecting plant growth and species interactions.
records.authors: Shen C, Tao Z, Wan J, Xu X, Siemann E, Huang W.

records.title: From mutations to mechanisms: using AlphaFold 2 to decode gentamicin resistance
records.abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance poses a major challenge to global health, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance often remain incompletely understood. In this webinar, I will present a case study from my PhD research investigating the genetic and structural basis of gentamicin resistance in experimentally evolved bacterial mutants. The project involved generating gentamicin-resistant mutants in the laboratory, performing whole-genome sequencing to identify resistance-associated mutations, and characterising the resulting protein variants. While mutations were identified across several proteins, the primary focus was on elongation factor G (EF-G), a key component of the bacterial translation machinery. To investigate the structural consequences of these mutations, AlphaFold2 was used to predict mutant protein structures and compare them with their wild-type counterparts. Structural alignments revealed that some mutations produced subtle conformational shifts in domain IV of EF-G, an extended region located near the gentamicin-binding site on the ribosome, while other mutations showed little or no detectable structural change. To place these findings into a functional context, experimental ribosome structures from the Protein Data Bank were integrated with AlphaFold predictions. By superimposing structures of EF-G-bound ribosomes and gentamicin-bound ribosomes, a composite structural model was generated, enabling the spatial relationship between resistance-associated mutations and the antibiotic-binding site to be examined. These analyses provided mechanistic insights into how specific mutations may reduce gentamicin binding through local structural and physicochemical effects. The webinar will discuss the opportunities and limitations of using AlphaFold to investigate the structural consequences of genomic variation, the challenges of interpreting subtle structural differences, and the importance of integrating AI-predicted models with experimental structural data to generate biologically meaningful hypotheses.

records.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Reveals Antibacterial Responses of Staphylococcus aureus to 60Co γ-Irradiation.
records.abstract: γ-Irradiation is a widely used nonthermal sterilization technology in food processing; however, the mechanisms underlying γ-irradiation-induced inactivation of Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of 60Co γ-irradiation on S. aureus and its molecular responses by integrating physiological assays with transcriptomic and proteomic analyses. γ-Irradiation produced a dose-dependent reduction in bacterial culturability from 0 to 2.0 kGy, with the greatest reduction observed at 2.0 kGy. Although no obvious surface morphological alterations were detected by scanning electron microscopy, γ-irradiation compromised membrane integrity, as evidenced by increased leakage of nucleic acids, proteins, and K+ and decreased ATPase-associated activities. Integrated omics analysis identified 486 differentially expressed genes and 178 differentially expressed proteins following 2.0 kGy irradiation. Functional enrichment analysis revealed alterations in pathways associated with cell envelope biosynthesis, amino acid metabolism, and energy metabolism. Notably, upregulation of MNH antiporters suggested a potential adaptive response to maintain cellular ion homeostasis under irradiation stress. Collectively, these findings indicate that γ-irradiation induces S. aureus inactivation through multiple cellular alterations, including membrane dysfunction, genomic damage, intracellular leakage, and metabolic disturbances.

records.title: Trophic highways and dead ends: Algal traits regulate nutrient flux and energy transfer in stream food webs.
records.abstract: Primary producers supply energy to ecosystems, but their traits determine whether fixed carbon (C) and nutrients are retained or transferred to consumers. In nitrogen (N)-limited rivers, N fixation can provide a critical nutrient input, yet its role in supporting food webs remains poorly constrained. We investigated how algal traits regulate the flux of newly fixed C and N to consumers in the South Fork Eel River, California, using stable isotope tracers to quantify nutrient flux and transfer to grazers (Gumaga nigricula). While several algal taxa exhibited high rates of nutrient fixation, trophic outcomes differed sharply. Assemblages dominated by Epithemia, a diatom genus with N-fixing cyanobacterial endosymbionts, supported disproportionately high trophic coupling. Conversely, cyanobacterial mats and mucilage-rich green algae were highly productive but little consumed. This decoupling is driven by nutrient packaging: Epithemia diatoms provide accessible nutrients and high-quality lipids, whereas cyanobacteria and filamentous green algae have traits that limit consumption. By quantifying variation in the flow of fixed nutrients into an algal-based food web, we show that transfer to primary consumers is governed by producer functional traits, and that shifts from diatom-dominated assemblages to cyanobacterial or green algal dominance will create trophic dead ends, limiting food supplies and top-down impacts of algivores.
records.authors: Zampini MC, Wulf MA, Sitati AN, Kariunga SH, Thomas SA, Power ME, Marks JC.

records.title: Family of β-Propeller Diels-Alderases Directs cis-Decalin Formation in Polyketide Biosynthesis.
records.abstract: Decalin-forming Diels-Alderases (pericyclases) exemplify how Nature repeatedly recruits unrelated protein folds to control [4 + 2] cycloadditions, yet exo-selective intramolecular Diels-Alder (IMDA) reactions that yield cis-fused decalins remain rare and poorly understood. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized bacterial pericyclase family that enforces an exo-IMDA trajectory in polyketide assembly. Using alchivemycin A, a macrocyclic antibacterial polyketide whose scaffold is defined by a highly functionalized cis-decalin core, we identify AvmG as the dedicated decalin-forming enzyme. Disruption of avmG diverts pathway flux to trans-decalin shunt isomers consistent with spontaneous, endo-biased cyclization that cannot be processed by the downstream macrocyclase, whereas AvmG enables formation of the authentic cis-decalin intermediate. AvmG is unrelated to known [4 + 2] cyclases and adopts an integrin α N-terminal domain-like β-propeller architecture, revealing an unexpected scaffold for pericyclic stereocontrol. Genome mining shows that AvmG-like proteins are widespread and enriched in actinomycete polyketide gene clusters; characterization of the lydicamycin homolog LymR establishes conserved exo-IMDA activity in a distinct pathway. Structural and mutational analyses implicate a loop-defined catalytic cavity in steering the kinetically demanding cis-decalin outcome. Together, these findings expand the fold and mechanistic diversity of Diels-Alderases, define an exo-selective β-propeller pericyclase superfamily, and provide a new handle for mining and bioengineering cis-decalin biosynthetic pathways.

records.title: Integrative transcriptomic profiling of the phosphatome identifies DUSP15 as a chromophobe renal cell carcinoma-selective epithelial biomarker associated with an immune-metabolic tumour state.
records.abstract: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) lacks robust molecular markers and well-defined therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, 265 protein-coding phosphatases were systematically interrogated using pan-cancer transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), cross-cohort evaluation in seven subtype-annotated Gene Expression Omnibus datasets drawn from a ten-dataset compilation, pathway and immune analyses, and two independent single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. DUSP15 emerged as the most chRCC-selective phosphatase (Tau = 0.977) and showed high retrospective discriminative performance both between chRCC and clear-cell and papillary RCC (AUC = 0.976) and between chRCC tumours and adjacent normal kidney tissue (AUC = 0.973) in TCGA. Subtype discrimination was independently reproduced across the GEO cohorts (AUC = 0.837). Transcriptome-wide analyses showed that DUSP15-high tumours were characterised by coordinated enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, MYC target and DNA repair programmes, together with reduced interferon and inflammatory signalling. Immune deconvolution revealed lower regulatory T-cell, dendritic-cell and overall immune enrichment scores, consistent with a relatively immune-poor transcriptional state. Single-cell analyses localised the bulk-tumour DUSP15 signal predominantly to tumour-associated epithelial populations in two independent datasets, with DUSP15 detected in 72.2-83.7% of tumour epithelial cells and pseudobulk abundance ranging from 144.9 to 204.3 counts per million. Expression was substantially lower in immune, stromal, normal renal epithelial and non-chRCC tumour populations. Collectively, these findings identify DUSP15 as a highly selective tumour-epithelial biomarker candidate for chRCC and establish the cellular context of a DUSP15-associated immune-metabolic state with potential diagnostic and biological relevance.
records.authors: Sarhan AR.

records.title: Acyldepsipeptide 1 and Furan Derivative from Pseudomonas chlororaphis Are Critical for Biocontrol of Tomato Bacterial Wilt Caused by Ralstonia solanacearum.
records.abstract: Tomato bacterial wilt, caused by Ralstonia solanacearum, is a destructive soil-borne disease that severely constrains tomato production. Here, we compared two rhizosphere bacterial strains Pseudomonas chlororaphis subsp. aurantiaca YS05 and YS21, with contrasting biocontrol efficiency. YS05 strongly suppressed disease, whereas YS21 showed substantially weaker efficacy. Comparative analyses indicated that both strains shared conserved genomic architecture and colonization-associated traits, but YS05 uniquely harbored secondary metabolite (SM) biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) associated with acyldepsipeptide 1 (ADEP1), furan derivative, and arylpolyene. Deletion of adeB or avrD reduced metabolite accumulation and biocontrol efficacy, whereas neither YS05 derivatives nor the corresponding metabolite standards directly inhibited R. solanacearum in vitro; instead, they activated tomato defense responses associated with salicylic acid, jasmonic acid, and reactive oxygen species homeostasis. These findings link ADEP1 and furan derivative to YS05-mediated bacterial wilt suppression and defense activation, and offer new insights into the development of environmentally friendly biocontrol agents.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Liu Y, Zhang S, Huang Y, Jiao Z, Xie X, Shi Y, Chai A, Zhang D, Li B, Li L.

records.title: Whole-Genome Sequences of Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV, Tobamovirus tabaci) Reveal Its Population Genetic Structure and Transmission Routes in China.
records.abstract: Viral diseases severely threaten agriculture, particularly in cigar tobacco. Here, we clarified the occurrence and distribution of viral diseases in cigar tobacco in Hainan, China, and identified TMV and CMV as the predominant viruses. Furthermore, we obtained the full-length genomes of two TMV isolates, analyzed their structures and variations, and validated their pathogenicity. Using whole-genome resequencing data from 79 TMV isolates collected over the past two decades─60 from five major tobacco-growing regions of China and 19 from other countries─we constructed a genome-wide SNP data set and analyzed the population genetics and transmission routes. Results indicated that TMV in China originated in northern China and spread via two independent routes: (i) progressive north-to-south spread to the middle and lower reaches of the Changjiang River basin and (ii) direct introduction to Hainan Island. Our study provides insights into viral disease management in the development of the cigar industry.
records.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
records.authors: Xia C, Xiang X, Li X, Lu H, Guo D, Yan T, Jiang L, Chen D, Yang Y.

records.title: Reprogramming Native Cryptic Plasmids Enables Antibiotic-Selection-Free Urate Degradation by Escherichia coli Nissle 1917.
records.abstract: Hyperuricemia is associated with renal injury and disturbances in gut microbial ecology. Intestinal urate clearance by engineered probiotics is limited by antibiotic-free functional maintenance and the oxygen requirement of urate oxidase (UOX). We reprogrammed the native cryptic plasmids of Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) to construct M12U, a marker-free dual-plasmid strain. pMUT2 carried an HucR-regulated urate-responsive UOX module, while pMUT1 encoded a low-oxygen-responsive UOX module and Tat-targeted Vitreoscilla haemoglobin (tat-VHB). M12U degraded urate in vitro and retained activity under low-oxygen conditions. In hyperuricemic mice (n = 5 per group), oral M12U reduced serum urate, creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, inflammatory cytokines and renal histopathological injury. 16S rRNA profiling showed increased microbial richness and a partial shift in community composition toward healthy controls. Shotgun metagenomics revealed enrichment of Lactobacillus johnsonii and Bacteroides acidifaciens, together with increased metabolic potential related to the pentose phosphate pathway and glutathione metabolism. Faecal metabolomics showed reduced uric acid abundance and increased thiamine monophosphate and argininosuccinic acid. These results support further evaluation of dual-native-plasmid architectures for gut-directed urate clearance.

records.title: Microbial Characteristics of Weissella cibaria HRL3 and Its Immunostimulatory Effects via TLR3/TLR9-Dependent IFN-α Production.
records.abstract: Rhinacanthus nasutus (L.) Kurz is a medicinal plant whose roots, stems, and leaves are commonly used in tea and traditional Chinese medicine; however, the beneficial effects of its flowers remain to be investigated. In this study, the lactic acid bacteria (LAB) found in the flowers of R. nasutus (L.) Kurz were isolated using a medium containing fructose, which is abundant in the flowers, and their microbial characteristics were subsequently analyzed. The isolated LAB strain was identified as Weissella cibaria based on whole-genome sequencing and was designated as HRL3. This strain was a facultative anaerobe whose growth was promoted under aerobic conditions, and it was classified as a heterofermentative LAB that produced lactate and ethanol via lactate fermentation. In addition, the HRL3 strain exhibited a unique carbohydrate utilization profile that differed from the type strain of W. cibaria. The immunostimulatory effects of the HRL3 strain were also investigated in this study. When added to mouse spleen cells, the HRL3 strain induced the production of IFN-α, which is a cytokine that plays a key role in enhancing antiviral immune responses. This induction could occur through recognition by endosomal Toll-like receptor (TLR) 3 and TLR9. Dectin-1 may also contribute to IFN-α production induced by the HRL3 strain. In an influenza A virus (IAV)-infected mouse model, oral administration of the HRL3 strain was associated with increased IFN-α mRNA expression, reduced IAV M mRNA expression, and attenuation of pulmonary histopathological changes. These findings provide new insights into the functional potential of R. nasutus (L.) Kurz flowers and the immunomodulatory activity of the HRL3 strain.
records.authors: Niitsuma F, Sasahara H, Masaki A, Toritani A, Tsukamoto M, Takahashi T, Tanaka S.

records.title: Toward a Universal Switch for Microbial Granulation: Photogranule Insights to Advance Granular Wastewater Treatment.
records.abstract: Microbial granulation─the assembly of self-immobilized, spheroidal aggregates─is a transformative approach for high-density, energy-efficient wastewater treatment. By concentrating biomass and enhancing resilience to influent fluctuations, granular systems significantly reduce infrastructure footprints. Current granular technologies primarily leverage upflow continuous reactors or sequencing-batch reactors, where specific external selection pressures are imposed to drive granulation. However, granulation remains neither spontaneous nor reliably predictable, and its fundamental biological drivers are poorly understood. Recent advances in photogranules challenge selection-pressure models. Photogranules form from activated-sludge inocula in hydrostatic and hydrodynamic batches and even in CSTRs where classical selection conditions are weak or absent. Moreover, the recurring emergence of compact spheroidal granules across diverse natural and laboratory systems suggests shared, intrinsic biological drivers rather than purely engineered causes. In this Perspective, we propose that the bacterial second messenger c-di-GMP functions as a conserved, Goldilocks-like molecular switch that integrates diverse environmental cues into a coordinated granulation program. We synthesize transcriptomic, biochemical, and genetic evidence and advance three hypotheses linking c-di-GMP signaling and community physiology to granulation. If validated, targeted modulation of c-di-GMP─by genetic or chemical means─could enable predictable, resilient granulation across a wider range of systems, including the continuous horizontal-flow basins that dominate wastewater infrastructure.
records.authors: Park C, Risser DD, Morita YS, Nüsslein K, Gikonyo JG.

records.title: Enzyme-Antibiotic Liquid Crystalline Nanoparticles for Enhanced Antibiofilm Activity, Bacterial Clearance, and Accelerated Healing of Infected Wounds.
records.abstract: Biofilm-associated wound infections remain difficult to treat because bacteria are protected within extracellular polymeric matrices that restrict antibiotic penetration, promote antimicrobial tolerance, and delay tissue repair. Here, we developed liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) for topical coformulation of gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), combining aminoglycoside therapy with an eDNA-targeting enzyme. GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs were successfully formulated as nanoscale particles with low polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency, and formulation-dependent in vitro release behavior. LCNP formulation preserved GEN antibacterial activity against planktonic Escherichia coli Xen14 and reduced the MBIC against established biofilms by approximately 4-fold. In a minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) model, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs achieved the greatest reduction in biofilm-associated viable bacteria, producing an approximately 6-log reduction compared with untreated biofilm controls and supporting the benefit of combining antibiotic delivery with rhDNase. Notably, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs markedly suppressed bacterial burden and reduced recoverable bacteria at day 9 to near the limit of detection in a bioluminescent E. coli Xen14 biofilm-associated excisional wound infection mouse model. This antibacterial effect translated into accelerated macroscopic wound closure and improved histological repair, including an approximately 80% reduction in wound gape compared with infected controls. Masson's trichrome staining further confirmed enhanced tissue remodeling, with the collagen-positive wound area increasing to approximately 88% following GEN + rhDNase-LCNP treatment, compared with approximately 21% in infected controls. In conclusion, LCNP-mediated codelivery of GEN and rhDNase improved bacterial clearance, re-epithelialization, and collagen deposition, supporting this platform as a promising topical antibiofilm strategy for infected wounds.
records.authors: Ahsan A, Nguyen HT, Wignall A, Kopecki Z, Barnes TJ, Thomas N, Ogunniyi AD, Prestidge CA.

records.title: Host Development and Environment Influence the Microbiomes of Aquatic Insects and Riparian Spiders.
records.abstract: Larval aquatic insects harbour diverse microbiomes critical for physiology and development, yet the effects of metamorphosis combined with environmental exposures on this community remain unknown. Herein we examined bacterial microbiome composition and predicted function across larval and adult stages of three families of aquatic insects and riparian spider predators, collected upstream and downstream of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) in Ontario, Canada. Insect host developmental stage was the primary driver of microbiome structure. Larval microbiomes were more diverse and showed higher abundances in pathways reflecting active feeding. Larval and adult populations of holometabolous insects shared few ASVs (3.8%-12.6% of the combined ASV pool), whereas a larger proportion was shared in hemimetabolous insects (23.4%). WWTP effluent exposures led to selective microbial filtering rather than broad community restructuring. Macroinvertebrate and spider microbiomes sampled downstream were characterized by higher abundances in bacterial taxa associated with wastewaters and increased xenobiotic degradation pathways. Such impacts on spider microbiomes provide evidence that ecological impacts of effluents cross the aquatic-terrestrial boundary. Lastly, a significant decrease of vertically transmitted endosymbionts (Rickettsiella, Wolbachia) was detected in aquatic insects, representing a pathway through which effluent pollution may affect host fitness without detectably altering overall microbiome diversity.

records.title: Spike gene evolution in HCoV-OC43: Evidence of post-pandemic selective expansion.
records.abstract: IntroductionThe aim is to characterise the evolution of the HCoV-OC43 spike from 2014 to 2024, spanning both the pre- and post-SARS-CoV-2 pandemic periods, in cases attended at a tertiary hospital in Catalonia.MethodsRespiratory specimens from patients with suspected acute respiratory infection were collected for laboratory-confirmation using a real-time PCR assay. A random selection of HCoV-OC43-positive specimens was performed per week. The whole spike gene was amplified by a nested RT-PCR using primers and protocol optimised from Gorse et al., 2017 and subsequently sequenced with the Illumina DNA Prep protocol. Further analyses were performed with MEGA and Nextclade softwares.ResultsThe overall prevalence of seasonal coronaviruses was 5.18%, with HCoV-OC43 accounting for 47.93%. Phylogenetic analysis of the S gene revealed the predominance of cluster C. Mutation analysis showed that the RBD accumulated the highest number of substitutions prior to the pandemic, followed by a reduction afterwards, suggesting shifts in selective pressures. Positive Tajima's D values in the pre-pandemic period were consistent with stable endemic circulation, whereas negative values in the post-pandemic period suggested population expansion following a bottleneck. Comparative analyses revealed that HCoV-OC43 also exhibited lower evolutionary rates than SARS-CoV-2, in the S1 and the RBD regions, underscoring differential immune pressures.ConclusionsThe present findings highlight the dynamic interplay between viral evolution and epidemiological changes associated with the pre- and post-pandemic periods in shaping the genetic landscape of endemic HCoVs.

records.title: Multi-locus genetic basis of stomatal density and size in maize revealed by integrated QTL and GWAS.
records.abstract: Stomatal patterning is a fundamental aspect of plant photosynthetic performance and water-use efficiency, yet its genetic basis in C4 grasses such as maize remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated linkage analysis across three recombinant inbred line populations and a genome-wide association study in a diverse maize panel to dissect the genetic architecture of six stomatal traits. This approach identified 33 quantitative trait loci and 51 association loci for 6 stomatal traits and revealed a significant negative genetic correlation between stomatal density (SD) and size, with multiple genomic intervals showing co-localization of effects on both trait categories. By integrating reported cell-type-specific transcriptomic data, we prioritized high-confidence candidate genes, including conserved stomatal regulators as well as previously uncharacterized candidates involved in processes such as cell wall biosynthesis. Functional analyses of EMS-induced mutants for candidates ZmbHLH140 and ZmCESA6 demonstrated that loss of ZmbHLH140 reduces SD, whereas mutation of ZmCESA6 has the opposite effect. In addition, the signature of selection at the ZmbHLH140 locus is consistent with a role for stomatal regulation during maize domestication. Together, our results establish a comprehensive genetic framework for stomatal development in maize, highlighting both conserved and grass-specific mechanisms that shape stomatal patterning and offering a foundation for future functional studies of stomatal development in cereals.
records.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology

records.title: Integrated Whole-Genome and RNA Sequencing Analysis of FFPE Lung Cancer Samples: Feasibility and Pathological Validation.
records.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) can be applied to formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens for genomic and transcriptomic analyses, including gene rearrangement detection. We tested whether PCR-free WGS and RNA-seq could detect driver alterations in FFPE lung adenocarcinoma samples prepared under standardized automated fixation and embedding conditions. Two adenocarcinoma cases were analyzed. Before this study, immunohistochemistry had suggested an EGFR alteration in one case and an ALK alteration in the other, although neither had been confirmed at the genomic or chromosomal level. In this analysis, PCR-free WGS yielded stable sequencing metrics and successfully detected small variants, including the canonical EGFR p.Leu858Arg mutation. By contrast, conventional structural variant calling failed to identify the EML4::ALK rearrangement. However, a custom algorithm based on supplementary alignment tags recovered the fusion candidate from WGS data despite support from only a single junction read, and RNA-seq independently confirmed expression of the EML4::ALK fusion transcript. Break-apart fluorescence in situ hybridization demonstrated tumor-wide clonal ALK rearrangement. These findings show that a single junction read can be biologically meaningful only when supported by orthogonal pathological validation and highlight the importance of integrating sequencing findings with pathological validation for the interpretation of gene rearrangements in FFPE specimens.
records.authors: Kiyose S, Yamada H, Miyazaki R, Yoshimura K, Takeuchi S, Takahashi S, Tanahashi M, Konno K, Hoshino H, Hoshi G, Ozawa H, Chiba H, Hattori N, Shinmura K.

records.title: Interpreting graph neural networks reveals microbial association patterns in inflammatory bowel diseases
records.abstract: Traditional machine learning models trained on gut microbiome abundance profiles can distinguish individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from non-IBD individuals. However, their interpretation typically considers taxa in isolation, making it difficult to understand how associations between taxa contribute to predictions. Here, we inferred individual-specific microbial association networks from longitudinal metagenomics data of 106 individuals in HMP2/iHMP and used them to train and interpret graph neural network (GNN) models, which we compared with abundance-based models such as Random Forest (RF). Although RF achieved higher predictive performance (AUPRC 0.59 vs 0.446), interpreting the GNNs revealed that their predictions relied on a densely connected module of co-abundant Bacteroidales species. Unlike the taxa prioritized by RF, these species were not differentially abundant between conditions. In an independent cohort, this module carried most of the predictive signal, and removing its associations reduced performance to near chance. These results show that coordinated association structure, rather than abundance shifts alone, is a feature of the IBD gut microbiome, and that interpreting GNNs can uncover such patterns that complement abundance-based analyses.
records.authors: Cunha AF, Vidal E, Barranco-Altirriba M, Amigó T, Assis JG, Nakaya HI, Santos A.

records.title: Development of Novel Furan-Chalcone Derivatives as Targeting Bacterial DNA Gyrase and Topoisomerase IV: Design, Synthesis, and In Silico Studies.
records.abstract: A series of novel furan-chalcone derivatives (Na1-Na8) were synthesized and evaluated for their antimicrobial, antioxidant, DNA gyrase inhibitory, and computational properties using integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. Among the synthesized compounds, Na5 exhibited the most potent antibacterial activity with low MIC values against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial strains. Antioxidant studies revealed significant free radical scavenging activity for Na3, Na4, and Na5. Molecular docking studies against DNA gyrase B demonstrated favorable binding interactions within the ATP-binding pocket. Enzyme inhibition studies against Escherichia coli DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV confirmed that Na5 showed the strongest inhibitory activity among the tested compounds. ADME predictions indicated acceptable drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties. Furthermore, DFT analysis of Na5 revealed a suitable HOMO-LUMO energy gap and favorable electronic properties supporting its biological activity. Overall, the results identify Na5 as a promising lead candidate for the development of novel antimicrobial agents targeting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
records.authors: Durgadasheemi NN, Cs V.

records.title: Lactobacillales-Enriched Oral Microbiome Profile as a Potential Link in the Tooth Loss-Cognition Association: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES 2011-2012.
records.abstract: AimThis study aimed to examine oral microbial features in the association between tooth loss and cognitive status in older adults from the US population and evaluate the role of oral microbiota in tooth loss and cognition.Methods and resultsEligible 568 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (Nhanes) 2011-2012 were recruited. Oral rinse sampleses were collected, and the 16S ribosomal RNA gene was sequenced. α-diversity and β-diversity was analyzed to depict microbiome profile. Mediation models were used to investigate the role of a-diversity in the association between tooth loss and cognitive function. The co-occurring group exhibited significantly reduced α-diversity and distinct β-diversity compared to CI (cognitive impairment) only group and the control group (p ConclusionThis pioneering study investigated the oral microbiota composition in relation to varying levels of tooth loss and cognitive status. It revealed the complex role of mucosal colonization in both dental and cognitive health, thereby underscoring the need to integrate the oral microbiome into cognitive research.

records.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Periodontal Disease: Rethinking Adjunctive Therapy in the Metagenomics Era, the Pressing Need for Precision Treatment and Periodontal Resistome Mapping.
records.abstract: Systemic antibiotics are effective when used as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of periodontitis; however, their use must be balanced against antimicrobial resistance, which is a major threat to global public health. This review provides an expert synthesis of the literature and a field-level overview of antimicrobial resistance in periodontal therapy, highlighting current knowledge and emerging directions, while examining how adjunctive antibiotic protocols may contribute to resistance within the periodontal microbiome through emerging metagenomic insights. To provide this synthesis, the PubMed database was searched for English-language publications using combinations of the terms periodontitis, systemic antibiotics, antimicrobials, resistance, resistome, therapeutic adjuncts, resistance genes, susceptibility, antibacterial and drug resistance, and the findings are presented as a narrative review. The evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of patients with periodontitis harbour subgingival microbiota that are non-susceptible to at least one antibiotic used in periodontal therapy. Across the included studies, antimicrobial resistance was most frequently reported in Prevotella and Porphyromonas species, while some studies also identified virulence-associated factors in Staphylococcus aureus, a non-classical periodontal organism detected within the subgingival microbiota. Overall, current evidence indicates a high prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes in the subgingival microbiota of patients with periodontitis and highlights the ecological consequences of adjunctive antibiotic use. These findings reinforce the need to optimize antibiotic prescribing protocols within an antibiotic stewardship framework and support further metagenomic investigations to refine understanding of resistance patterns, gene-transfer mechanisms and microbiome disruption, with the aim of advancing precision-based periodontal care.
records.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
records.authors: Alghafri M, Edwards L, Moyes D, Nibali L.

records.title: An integrated workflow for Mycoplasma detection and removal from cell cultures and viral stocks.
records.abstract: Contamination of cell cultures and viral stocks with Mycoplasma is one of the most frequent and underdiagnosed problems in laboratories working with these materials, severely affecting experimental reproducibility, data reliability, and biosafety. This article presents an integrated set of robust, sensitive, and broad applicable protocols for the detection, treatment, and mitigation of Mycoplasma contamination in cellular and viral systems. Basic Protocol 1 describes a sensitive qPCR-based method for Mycoplasma detection using DNA extracted from cell cultures and viral suspensions, including clear interpretation criteria based on amplification and melting curve analyses. Basic Protocol 2 outlines a sequential antibiotic treatment strategy for eliminating Mycoplasma from contaminated cell cultures, combining different antimicrobial classes and continuous monitoring of cell viability and morphology. Basic Protocol 3 presents a complementary approach to reduce Mycoplasma burden in viral stocks through serial dilution and controlled replication, aiming to preserve viral infectivity while minimizing bacterial contaminants. Together, these protocols provide a practical and reproducible workflow that enables rapid identification of contamination, implementation of effective corrective measures, and molecular validation of decontamination. The procedures are suitable for virology, cell biology, and experimental virus production laboratories, thereby improving experimental quality and data reliability. © 2026 The Author(s). records.title: Introduction and Spread of West Nile Virus in Lazio, Italy, 2025: Molecular Epidemiology and Genomic Characterization.
records.abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) is a flavivirus whose cycle involves mosquitoes and avian hosts that occasionally may infect horses and humans as "dead-end hosts." Human infection is mostly asymptomatic, sometimes leading to febrile or neuroinvasive disease. In 2025, Italy experienced its largest epidemic with an unprecedented geographic spread (79 provinces; 52% of cases in central Italy). Here we report whole‑genome sequencing and phylogeographic analysis of 39 WNV lineage 2 samples collected in Lazio and Campania regions between July and September 2025 from humans and animal samples. All 2025 strains belonged to a Southern Italian clade that diversified around 2020, with evidence of earlier circulation in 2024. All the 2025 genomes shared a substitution that lies in envelope protein domain III (K399R), potentially influencing interactions with the viral membrane. The same mutation was previously detected in Eastern European strains, leading to the hypothesis of introductions in Italy via migratory birds from these regions. Phylogeography identified strong viral dispersal routes within Central Italy supporting a pattern of short‑range spread and local overwintering. Overall, results highlight the roles of ecological conditions and cross‑border transmission dynamics in shaping the 2025 Italian epidemic, underscoring the need for integrated genomic/ecological surveillance.

records.title: Unilateral cross-feeding constrains adaptive evolution, even in the producer without direct fitness effects.
records.abstract: Cross-feeding interactions are pervasive in microbial communities and profoundly shape community structure, stability, and function. While previous studies have explored how cross-feeding affects evolvability, this work has predominantly focused on bidirectional mutualistic interactions in engineered auxotrophic systems where both partners reciprocally exchange essential metabolites. However, most metabolic interactions in natural microbial communities are unidirectional, with organisms feeding on the metabolic waste products of other species. Our study addresses this gap by examining how a unidirectional cross-feeding interaction affects the evolutionary dynamics of both the producer (Acinetobacter johnsonii) and consumer (Pseudomonas putida) over 800 generations of experimental evolution. We found that co-culture constrained adaptive evolution in both species. Co-cultures exhibited lower πN/πS ratios (0.75 for P. putida; 1.04 for A. johnsonii) than monocultures (1.44 and 2.02, respectively), indicating stronger purifying selection against nonsynonymous mutations in the community context. Lineage tracking through whole genome sequencing of populations and clones revealed greater lineage diversity and complexity in monocultures, with more mutations showing significant parallelism across replicate populations. Additionally, P. putida evolved increased dependence on its partner; co-culture-evolved P. putida grew significantly worse than its ancestor when A. johnsonii was removed. These findings indicate that ecological interactions can reshape fitness landscapes and constrain adaptive evolution even when fitness benefits are unidirectional, with implications for understanding microbial community stability and predicting evolutionary dynamics in complex communities.
