records.title: Model-based inference of gene expression noise from single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
records.abstract: The heterogeneity of expression levels among genetically identical cells, termed gene expression noise, is a property of the gene expression process whose importance in the biology of organisms and their evolution is increasingly recognized. Measuring gene expression noise requires single-cell expression data, as obtained from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNASeq). Its estimation, however, is challenging owing to (i) the presence of technical noise in addition to biological noise, and (ii) the heterogeneity of cell types in the sampled population. We propose a maximum-likelihood framework to infer biological noise from scRNASeq data, while accounting for technical noise, dropout probabilities, and distinct cell sequencing depths. We demonstrate the parameter identifiability using simulations and that the resulting noise estimates are uncorrelated from the mean gene expression, and therefore do not need extra correction in downstream analyses, easing intra- and inter- genome comparisons. Using two technical replicates of scRNASeq data from the wild yeast Saccharomyces paradoxus, we show that expression noise can be inferred in a reproducible manner.
records.authors: Giersdorf F, Rogers DW, Christensen S, Dutheil JY.

records.title: scMRdb: a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved Mendelian randomization of complex traits.
records.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) is a powerful analytical approach to infer putative causal links between gene expression and human disease, using genetic variants as instrumental variables to mitigate confounding and reverse causation. However, existing MR resources predominantly rely on bulk-tissue expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), which mask cell-type-specific transcriptional effects by averaging expression across cellular populations. Furthermore, cell-type-resolved causal evidence from single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) MR analyses remains fragmented across individual studies with inconsistent workflows, prohibiting standardized cross-cell-type comparisons. Here we present scMRdb (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/scmrdb), a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved MR of human complex traits and diseases. scMRdb harmonizes 5206 genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics of European and East Asian ancestry with 585 sc-eQTL datasets spanning 11 tissues and cell systems, including 110 cell types. A uniform pipeline evaluates all gene-trait pairs via MR followed by Steiger directionality testing. Significant associations are assessed by colocalization, and results are stratified into six confidence tiers with integrated drug-target annotation. scMRdb enables systematic recovery of candidate causal genes supported by cell-type-resolved regulatory evidence that is often diluted or obscured in bulk-tissue analyses. We expect scMRdb to serve as a user-friendly portal for generating cell-type-informed mechanistic hypotheses and prioritizing actionable therapeutic targets for complex human diseases.
records.authors: Pan S, Wang Z, Jia P.

records.title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
records.abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 weeks (BW3), and 6 weeks (BW6) of age in broiler chickens derived from reciprocal crosses between the commercial Arian line and native Urmia chicken. A total of 368 birds were genotyped using GBS, and 312 second-generation (F₂) birds with complete phenotypic records were utilized for genomic screening and machine learning analyses. The hyperparameters of both machine learning algorithms were optimized using a grid search with three-fold cross-validation. The combined application of RF and GBM identified several informative SNP markers located on chromosomes 1, 4, 13, 17, 19, 20, and 24. Positional candidate genes located within these genomic regions included platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD), KIRRE-like nephrin family adhesion molecule 3 (KIRREL3), ETS proto-oncogene 1, transcription factor (ETS1), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 1 (ACSL1), diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 2 (DGAT2), and selenophosphate synthetase 1 (SEPHS1). Gene Ontology enrichment analysis indicated that these genes are involved in biological processes related to the regulation of protein degradation, immune responses, and lipid metabolism. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating cost-effective GBS with machine learning approaches to identify genomic regions and informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens, providing valuable genomic resources for future breeding and genetic improvement programs.
records.authors: Bani Saadat H, Vaez Torshizi R, Masoudi AA.

records.title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing improves pathogen detection in culture-negative infections: a diagnostic performance study.
records.abstract: The conventional microbiological diagnosis is frequently insensitive, time consuming and targeted. Patients with underlying immune suppression and those who have recently been on antibiotics often have culture-negative infections. In recent years, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) has emerged as a novel, pathogen-agnostic diagnostic approach. A total of 136 clinical specimens were submitted for metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) between August 2022 and January 2024. Of these samples, 86 from 73 patients were included in this retrospective study. Thirteen patients had more than one specimen included in the study. All specimens were processed using conventional microbiological methods and analyzed using mNGS technology, either by using Illumina next-generation sequencing technology or Oxford Nanopore long-read technology. The diagnostic performance characteristics, including sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), were calculated for both methods. The agreement between the two methods was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficient. The paired comparisons were made using the McNemar test. The areas under the ROC curves for both methods were calculated, and the multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify the variables that were independently associated with mNGS positivity. Here, conventional microbiology identified pathogens in 16.3% of samples, whereas mNGS identified pathogens in 45.3% of samples. The sensitivity and specificity of mNGS were 57.1 and 84.2%, respectively. By McNemar testing, there was significant detection of pathogens by mNGS (p = 0.0015). The agreement between two methods was poor (kappa = 0.20). The ROC curve for mNGS results showed moderate diagnostic accuracy with an AUC of 0.71. By multivariable logistic regression, immunocompromised status (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.3-6.0, p = 0.018) and positive imaging findings (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.4-6.9, p = 0.010) were independently associated with mNGS positivity. mNGS is able to identify more pathogens in culture-negative cases than conventional methods. There is scope for mNGS to be used in a complementary fashion, whilst relying on conventional methods as the primary tool for diagnosis of infections. Notably, the greatest additional information will come from the use of mNGS in immunocompromised patients.
records.authors: Tayeb HT, Abouelhoda M, Alqasabi A, Magrashi A, Nafe G, Alzahrani T, Alzeer S, Bakheet R.

records.title: Integrating multi-marker phylogeny and morphology reveals hidden diversity and intraspecific morphological variation in the genus Pseudohydnum P. Karst. (Basidiomycota, Auriculariales) from China.
records.abstract: The toothed jelly genus Pseudohydnum P. Karst. (Basidiomycota, Auriculariales) has historically been treated under a broad morphological concept centered on P. gelatinosum, a view that has long masked substantial cryptic diversity worldwide. However, many Chinese collections remain taxonomically unresolved and species boundaries are poorly defined. Here, we reassess the species diversity of Chinese Pseudohydnum through an integrative approach combining detailed morphology with multi-marker phylogenetics (ITS, nrLSU, and rpb1). We formally describe three new species, P. ellipsosporum sp. nov., P. macroumbrosum sp. nov., and P. roseolostipitatum sp. nov. We also refine the circumscriptions of four previously described taxa and provide new insights into their intraspecific variation, geographic distribution, and ecology. Notably, we document a previously unknown host association: P. brunneiceps was consistently found on decayed bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis), a substrate never before recorded for any Pseudohydnum species. Critically, our results demonstrate that morphology alone is currently insufficient for species delimitation as convergent or plastic characters obscure diagnostic differences, reinforcing the necessity of molecular validation. These findings substantially expand the known taxonomic and ecological diversity of Pseudohydnum in Asia, suggesting that China, particularly the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, may be a global hotspot for the genus. Overall, this study underscores the essential role of phylogenetic inference in revising species boundaries and elucidating evolutionary patterns in morphologically plastic groups of fungi.
records.authors: Yu TJ, Zhang WH, Li XJ, Xiong YY, Gao YX, Li T, Xue R, Lu YT, Xu C, Li J, Tang LP.

records.title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
records.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.
records.authors: Kreimeyer H, Gonzalez C, Fondevila MF, AlcHepNet Investigators, Canbay A, Stärkel P, Gonzalez DJ, Schnabl B.

records.title: Immune Cell-Mediated Interactions Between the Gut Microbiome and Endometriosis: A Mendelian Randomization Investigation.
records.abstract: ObjectiveThe etiology of endometriosis (EM) remains unclear. Evidence indicates a correlation between intestinal microbial communities and immune homeostasis in the pathogenesis of EM. This investigation leverages Mendelian randomization (MR) to delineate causal links connecting gut microbiota composition, specific immune cell phenotypes, and endometriosis, aiming to identify novel therapeutic avenues.MethodsUsing publicly available genetic data from genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary datasets that encompass 473 microbial taxa, 731 immunological traits, and endometriosis cases, we executed bidirectional and two-step Mendelian randomization (MR) frameworks to assess causality and quantify mediation effects, aiming to evaluate the associations between intestinal microbial communities and immune homeostasis in the pathogenesis of endometriosis (EM). Utilizing single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) as instrumental variables (IVs), we ensured robustness through sensitivity assessments, specifically Cochran's Q statistic and MR-Egger regression, to mitigate concerns regarding horizontal pleiotropy and heterogeneity.ResultsOur analysis revealed that Actinobacteria exerted an influence on HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cells (total effect: -0.2736; mediated proportion: 6.45%), whereas Actinomycetales regulated DN (CD4-CD8-) NKT cell populations (total effect: -0.1961; mediated proportion: 5.77%). Furthermore, Aneurinibacillaceae demonstrated a 14.30% mediation effect operating through CD28 expression levels on resting regulatory T cells (Tregs) (total effect: 0.4053). Eisenbergiella sp900066775 displayed pleiotropic impacts on markers associated with both Tregs and B cells (total effect: -0.1447). Notably, protective correlations were identified for Actinobacteria (Odds Ratio [OR] = 0.76, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 0.65-0.89) and Bifidobacterium angulatum (OR = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.83-0.94). Conversely, Aneurinibacillaceae abundance was linked to elevated endometriosis susceptibility (OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.13-1.98).ConclusionDysbiosis within the gut microbiome fosters endometriosis development by modulating immune cell dynamics, predominantly via pathways involving Tregs and NKT cells. These results underscore the microbiota-immune axis as a promising target for intervention, warranting future clinical trials to evaluate probiotic or immunomodulatory strategies.
records.authors: Huang X, Zhong R, Pan L.

records.title: Transcriptome and DNA methylome profiling reveal molecular responses of bovine blastocysts to trophectoderm biopsy and post-biopsy vitrification.
records.abstract: Trophectoderm biopsy and post-biopsy vitrification are used in bovine embryo selection and cryopreservation, but their molecular effects remain incompletely understood. We investigated associated transcriptomic and DNA methylation changes in individual bovine blastocysts. Fifteen morphologically intact in vitro-produced blastocysts were allocated to non-biopsied fresh (NB), biopsied (B), and biopsied and vitrified (BV) groups (5 each). Cytoplasmic RNA and nuclear DNA from each blastocyst were profiled by Smart-seq2 and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, respectively. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs), differentially methylated regions (DMRs), and coordinated promoter methylation-expression changes were analyzed through pairwise comparisons and Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment. B vs NB yielded 822 DEGs (390 up/432 down), BV vs B 1295 (777/518), and BV vs NB 1494 (887/607). Biopsy-associated DEGs were enriched in glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, pyruvate metabolism, mitochondrial biogenesis, steroid biosynthesis, and peroxisome pathways. Vitrification was additionally associated with endocytosis, cell adhesion, and MAPK, TGF-β, FoxO, and estrogen signaling pathways; apoptosis and carbon metabolism featured in BV vs NB. B vs NB had the fewest DMRs, BV vs NB the most hypermethylated, and BV vs B the most hypomethylated. Genes with concurrent hypermethylation and downregulation were enriched in the tricarboxylic acid cycle and fatty-acid, amino-acid, sulfur, and glycerophospholipid metabolism, whereas those with hypomethylation and upregulation were associated with cytoskeleton remodeling, focal adhesion, and PI3K-Akt, Ras, MAPK, and calcium signaling. Biopsy was associated with transcriptional and epigenetic remodeling, and vitrification with broader metabolic, intercellular-signaling, and cellular-stress alterations. These candidate responses need functional validation and may help refine embryo biopsy and cryopreservation protocols.
records.authors: Feng X, Dong J, Ayantoye JO, Kolachi HA, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Wan P, Wang C, Zhao X.

records.title: Antimicrobial resistance detection technologies and the role of healthcare workforce: A scoping review of recent research.
records.abstract: BackgroundReliable determination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is fundamental to healthcare research and practice. High-quality research evidence is essential for guiding accurate AMR detection which, in turn, informs antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) decision-making. This scoping review is directed at a critical evaluation of the recent strategies in AMR detection across the globe.MethodsPertinent primary studies on AMR-associated strategies were identified by a comprehensive literature search on scholarly databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, and EMBASE) in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The final set of pertinent studies published during the last 5 years (2021-2026) included 58 studies. Subsequent analysis critically evaluated the evidence of integration of advanced technologies into AMR detection and prediction programs.ResultsWhole-genome sequencing (WGS; n = 37 articles) was the primary method for AMR screening across the included studies. Metagenomic sequencing (MGS) data was used for AMR characterization in 6 studies, while PCR/multiplex PCR was used in 10 articles. An interesting trend was the use of machine learning (ML) models for predicting AMR. Almost all studies which developed, validated and/or employed ML models (n = 21 studies) reported excellent time- and cost-efficiency, high accuracy and precision, and good concordance with conventional methods for AMR screening. Building on this synthesis, we propose the Integrated Diagnostic-Stewardship-Workforce (IDSW) model, a hypothesis-generating, five layered conceptual framework linking diagnostic innovations, workforce-mediated decision making, AMS intervention, contextual modifiers, and outcome feedback loop.ConclusionThe reviewed evidence supports the adaptation of AMR detection practices for clinical decision support systems, with potential downstream implications for technology-enhanced stewardship programs. Further, the proposed IDSW model offers a framework for guiding future research, policy making, and implementation efforts that integrate diagnostics and workforce roles, with AMS as a key downstream application.
records.journal: Journal of infection and public health
records.authors: Bantun F, Jalal NA, Faidah H, Babalghith AO, Johargy AK, Ahmad F, Mathkor DM, Haque S, Srivastava V.

records.title: Distribution patterns of PFASs in intertidal sediments and the effects on reductive dehalogenating bacteria: A nationwide study in China.
records.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are of great concern because of their environmental persistence. The intertidal zone sequesters various halogenated organic pollutants (HOPs) in sediments. Microbial reductive dehalogenation is crucial for HOPs detoxification. However, the nationwide distribution characteristics of PFASs in intertidal sediments and their impact on reductive dehalogenators (RDGs) remain poorly understood. We investigated PFAS distribution profiles in 128 intertidal sediments across China and analyzed their impact on potential RDGs. Sedimentary PFAS concentrations ranged 0.049-2.58 ng/g, with legacy PFASs being dominant. Amplicon sequencing and Spearman rank correlation analysis revealed positive correlation between total organic halogens and relative abundance and/or α-diversity of Anaerolineae and Desulfobacterota (p < 0.05), whereas no correlation was observed for Dehalococcoidia. Despite low ecological risks, Cl-PFESAs showed significant negative correlations with their relative abundance and α-diversity. Cl-PFESAs negatively correlated with abundance of the module associated with elemental cycles (p < 0.05), rather than those linked to organohalide utilization in the co-occurrence network. Microbial cultivation and metagenomic analysis reinforced the crucial role of Desulfobacterota and Anaerolineae in intertidal microbial dehalogenation and the negligible effect of 6:2 Cl-PFESA (0.1 mg/L) on reductive dehalogenating activity. This study provides critical insights into bioremediation strategies for HOPs in intertidal zones co-contaminated with PFASs.
records.authors: Zhu X, Wang H, Li S, Ni L, Li Y, Zhang D.

records.title: Genome-guided development of a halotolerant endophytic consortium-based biofertilizer enhances rice plant growth and salinity tolerance with reduced chemical fertilizer inputs.
records.abstract: Soil salinity is a major abiotic stress limiting rice productivity worldwide and necessitates sustainable alternatives to intensive chemical fertilizer use. We developed a genome-guided halotolerant endophytic bacterial consortium to enhance rice growth and resilience in salt-affected agroecosystems. A total of 101 endophytic bacteria were screened using a multi-phase strategy based on salt tolerance, plant growth-promoting (PGP) traits, retention of PGP functions under saline stress, and enhancement of rice seed germination under increasing salinity. Seven compatible strains were selected and identified as Phytobacter diazotrophicus, Mangrovibacter phragmitis (two strains), Brachybacterium paraconglomeratum, Priestia flexa, Micrococcus luteus, and Staphylococcus haemolyticus, for formulation into a talc-based biofertilizer. Whole-genome sequencing revealed genetic determinants linked to plant growth promotion and salinity adaptation, including genes associated with indole-3-acetic acid biosynthesis, phosphate solubilisation, nitrogen fixation, siderophore production, exopolysaccharide synthesis, osmoprotection, ion homeostasis, antioxidant defence, and plant colonisation. In vitro assays showed that the biofertilizer significantly enhanced rice seedling growth and biomass under saline conditions compared with individual strains and liquid consortium inoculation. Pot experiments showed that combining biofertilizer with a 75% reduced chemical fertilizer dose significantly improved plant growth, physiological performance, nutrient uptake, and stress tolerance under both 4 and 6 dS m⁻¹ salinity. Moreover, biofertilizer application improved soil nutrient status while reducing sodium accumulation and oxidative stress, with the magnitude of these benefits greater under salinity stress. These findings demonstrate the potential of genome-enabled microbial biofertilizers for sustainable rice cultivation in saline environments with reduced chemical fertiliser inputs.

records.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
records.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in-silico functional annotations against this experimental ground truth revealed poor predictive performance (cross-validated ROC-AUC = 0.55-0.59), demonstrating that computational predictions cannot reliably substitute for measured allelic activity. We therefore treated the ovarian analysis as hypothesis-generating. Convergent annotation evidence prioritised 44 of 176 ovarian cancer GWAS leads (31 independent loci); a core of 21 SNPs (17 loci) was stable under alternative weights, leave-one-feature-out scoring and threshold changes, and candidates were enriched in ovarian and fallopian-tube regulatory chromatin (OR = 7.9, FDR = 5 × 10⁻5). Copy-number recurrence at candidate genes agreed between two tumour cohorts (Spearman ρ = 0.75, 95% CI 0.46-0.88) but no more than for chromosome-arm-matched control genes, so this observation is exploratory. Formal colocalisation with full summary statistics supported a shared causal variant for prostate cancer risk and TLCD3A expression at 17p13.3 (PP.H4 = 0.92), whereas the ovarian 17q21.31 signal could not be resolved to a single gene. Transcription-factor motifs disrupted in both cancers were over-represented for the interferon-regulatory factor (IRF) and STAT families (FDR = 3 × 10⁻6), a motif-level hypothesis. In an independent MPRA in primary ovarian epithelial cells, variants disrupting interferon-stimulated response elements (ISREs) were depleted, not enriched, for allele-specific activity (4.6% vs 9.2%; OR = 0.47, nominal p = 0.06, FDR = 0.10), so the IRF/STAT hypothesis was not supported; the same assay confirmed allele-specific activity at one prioritised ovarian candidate, rs2976384 (skew = - 0.67, FDR = 3 × 10⁻5). These results provide an audited prostate regulatory-SNP catalogue, quantify the limits of annotation-based fine-mapping, and offer testable cross-cancer hypotheses.
records.authors: Al-Amili WA, Ayyed Najm M, Jumaah SS, Suleiman AA.

records.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis of Polygonatum odoratum Polysaccharide in D-Galactose-Treated Mice Reveals Changes in Oxidative Stress Markers and Gut Microbiota.
records.abstract: Age-related changes are associated with oxidative stress, metabolic dysregulation, and alterations in the gut microbiota. Although Polygonatum odoratum polysaccharide (POP) has shown antioxidant and neuroprotective effects, its associations with gut bacterial composition, circulating metabolites, and tissue gene expression remain unclear. Using a D-galactose-treated mouse model, we assessed hippocampal histology and oxidative stress markers and performed bacterial 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted serum metabolomics, and hippocampal and colonic transcriptomic analyses. POP treatment was associated with improved hippocampal histology, reduced malondialdehyde levels, and increased glutathione levels and superoxide dismutase activity. It was also associated with changes in selected gut bacterial taxa and serum lipid metabolites, lower expression of NF-κB-related genes (Btk, Lat, and Tnfrsf13c) in the colon, and lower Ninj2 expression in the hippocampus. Cross-omics analysis identified correlations among these bacterial, metabolite, and gene-expression features. These findings identify candidate gut-serum-tissue associations accompanying the effects of POP in D-galactose-treated mice. Functional studies are needed to determine whether any of these changes mediate its effects.

records.title: Human Saliva Induces Acetoin-Dependent Metabolic Adaptation that Promotes Stress Tolerance in  Streptococcus mutans
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Oral microbes are continually exposed to host-derived saliva, yet its effects on bacterial metabolism and stress adaptation remain incompletely defined. We investigated how saliva supplementation alters the physiology of the caries-associated bacterium  Streptococcus mutans using transcriptomics (RNA-Seq), targeted metabolite measurements, specific gene deletions, and transposon sequencing (Tn-Seq). Growth in a chemically defined medium supplemented with pooled saliva altered expression of genes involved in carbohydrate transport, purine biosynthesis, and pyruvate-associated metabolism, including induction of the acetoin dehydrogenase operon. Saliva significantly increased extracellular acetoin accumulation across all  S. mutans isolates tested, whereas little accumulation occurred in two commensal streptococcal species examined. Deletion of acetolactate synthase/decarboxylase (  alsSaldB ) abolished the saliva-associated increase, while deletion of individual acetoin dehydrogenase components (  adhC /  lplA ) enhanced accumulation, supporting the predicted roles of genes in acetoin synthesis and catabolism. Increasing the available carbohydrate concentrations within the media further increased acetoin accumulation, alongside declining terminal culture pH that was significantly lower in cultures supplemented with saliva. Following growth with saliva,  S. mutans exhibited approximately 10,000-fold greater survival during a hydrogen peroxide challenge than cells grown without saliva. Mutants within the acetoin pathway retained saliva-associated protection but showed approximately 100-fold lower survival than the wild type. Serial passage of a pooled transposon library identified previously unrecognized saliva-associated fitness determinants, including depletion of mutants carrying insertions in the acetoin dehydrogenase operon. Together, these findings identify acetoin metabolism as a contributor to saliva-associated metabolic remodeling and oxidative stress tolerance in  S. mutans and establish saliva as a critical modulator of  S. mutans physiology.
records.authors: Harris JS, Deever AN, Lee K, Kaspar JR.

records.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
records.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

records.title: Bacteriophages versus priority pathogens: resistance mechanisms, therapeutic challenges, and opportunities for novel combinations.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a critical global health threat, and renewed interest in bacteriophage (phage) therapy highlights its potential as a targeted alternative to antibiotic monotherapy. However, phage resistance in bacteria remains a key limiting factor in phage therapy, driven by evolutionary adaptations to phage exposure. Antibacterial modalities (antibiotics, adjuvants, antimicrobial peptides, and RNA-based therapeutics) could help overcome these barriers and represent untapped potential for synergistic, precision antimicrobial interventions when combined with phage therapy. Importantly, bacterial physiology and environmental context could strongly influence treatment outcomes, underscoring the need for clinically relevant models for testing combinations. Integration of multi-omics and artificial intelligence-driven approaches could help predict patterns for the development of precision therapies and support the development of novel antimicrobial interventions.
records.authors: Byrne S, Collins ACZ, Nolan AC, Wigneshweraraj S, Zeden MS.

records.title: Multi-omics insights into rare earth element recovery by microalgae under salinity gradients.
records.abstract: Conventional rare earth element (REE) extraction methods are resource-intensive and generate secondary pollutants, whereas biomining using microorganisms such as microalgae offers a more sustainable alternative. Microalgal growth and metal recovery are strongly influenced by environmental factors, especially salinity; however, the molecular mechanisms driving REE recovery in microalgae exposed to saline conditions remain largely unexplored. The overarching aim of this study is to elucidate the effects of salinity on REE recovery by microalgae using a multi-omics framework. Specifically, nine microalgal strains were screened across salinities of 0-5 %, followed by integrated metabolomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic characterization of Limnospira maxima under control, REE-only, 3.5 % salinity, and combined REE-salinity conditions. Among the tested species, L. maxima exhibited the highest REE recovery efficiency, outperforming other microalgae by a factor of 2-10. In L. maxima, heavy REE (Sc, Y, Tb, and Dy) were recovered 10-15 % more efficiently than light REE (La, Pr, Nd), particularly under salinities between 0.5 % and 5 %. The selective recovery of REE by L. maxima was most pronounced at elevated salinities. Global metabolomic profiles of the combined treatment were primarily associated with salinity, suggesting that salinity establishes the dominant physiological state within which REE-associated responses occur. Multi-omics analysis showed distinct responses to REE and salinity stress, including changes in carbon fixation, photosynthesis, and amino acid and lipid metabolism, with both transcript-protein convergence and pathway-level discordance indicating complex cross-layer regulation. Overall, the results identify L. maxima as a promising candidate for REE recovery under saline conditions while defining molecular responses and knowledge gaps relevant to future development of microalgae-based REE separation.
records.authors: Vo PHN, Songsomboon K, Kim M, Strezov V, Clark S, Kuzhiumparambil U, Pernice M, Ralph PJ.

records.title: Adaptive evolution identifies candidate genetic routes associated with oxalate utilization in probiotic and gut-derived E.coli.
records.abstract: Functional probiotics offer a therapeutic modality for degrading disease-associated compounds in the gut. In hyperoxaluria, therapeutic strategies based on natural oxalate degraders such as Oxalobacter formigenes have shown variable efficacy, motivating methods to expand the repertoire of oxalate-utilizing bacterial chassis and explore native genetic routes by which this function can evolve. Here, we used adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under microaerobic conditions to enable oxalate utilization in probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 and three gut-derived E. coli isolates. Within ∼400 generations, all lines evolved robust growth on minimal medium with oxalate as the sole carbon and energy source. Recurrent mutations identify native aldehyde-dehydrogenase-associated modules, including AdhE and the Eut system, as candidate genetic routes associated with evolved oxalate utilization. We propose ALE as a scalable framework to uncover latent metabolic potential in probiotic and gut-associated bacteria and generate mechanistically tractable candidates for downstream functional validation.
records.authors: Yona AH, Joshua Liu CW, Ben-Moshe Z, Nichols TM, Bodhankar GA, Key FM, Rao CV, Lieberman T, Tullman-Ercek D, Gore J.

records.title: TEDEdb: A multicohort analysis and resource for transposable element differential expression in cancer.
records.abstract: The human genome consists of nearly 50% repetitive DNA, referred to for decades as "junk DNA." These repetitive sequences, usually under the strict control of epigenetic silencing, can become aberrantly expressed in cancer. Some of these expressed sequences, e.g., transposable elements (TEs), can induce innate immune responses when derepressed following treatment with epigenetic therapies. As a result, epigenetic therapy has been suggested to augment cancer therapies. TEs are traditionally ignored in most RNA-seq studies and their expression is often excluded from publicly available data sources. Thus, the vast amount of publicly available RNA-seq data is an untapped resource for exploring the role of TE expression in cancer and cancer treatment. Here, we present a uniform reanalysis of over 7,000 RNA-seq samples, encompassing more than 2,000 differential expression experiments across 220 cancer cell lines and 700 drug treatments. We observed that TE expression is more prone to batch effects than gene expression alone, necessitating the use of meta-analysis techniques to probe the dataset for global trends. We confirm that DNMTi and HDACis are powerful inducers of TE expression. We also show that nonepigenetic compounds such as cyclin-dependent kinase and topoisomerase inhibitors can also induce robust up-regulation of TE-derived repetitive DNA elements and confirm that this induction is consistent with transcriptional signatures of viral mimicry response. We made all data available through a publicly available database called the Transposable Element Differential Expression Database, or TEDEdb, and created an interactive web application for its exploration located at https://dataexplorer.coriell.org/TEDEdb/.

records.title: Evolutionarily diverged on-switch for actin assembly in fungal endocytosis.
records.abstract: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is a conserved eukaryotic trafficking process where an Arp2/3 complex-nucleated branched actin network provides force for vesicle formation. The mechanisms that initiate endocytic actin assembly are incompletely understood. In the fission yeast, Schizosaccharomyces pombe, actin assembly is initiated by Dip1, an Arp2/3 complex activator. In the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the initiation of actin assembly has remained a mystery. Here, we show that S. cerevisiae Ldb17, the homolog of Dip1, functions as an on-switch for endocytic actin assembly. Unexpectedly, the regulation of Ldb17 is more complicated than that of constitutively active Dip1. Ldb17 is controlled by a coat protein, Sla1, via separate recruitment and activation steps. This regulation was likely lost in the S. pombe lineage, and this simplification may be related to other changes in actin assembly between these species. Our findings add a key missing piece in the understanding of endocytosis in S. cerevisiae and reveal an intriguing evolutionary tinkering of the actin on-switch.
records.authors: Sebellin J, Kandiyoth FB, Bagyashree VT, Picco A, Carvalho N, Hakala M, Rivier-Cordey AS, Michelot A, Toret CP, Kaksonen M.

records.title: Temporal phosphoproteomic programmes set a redox-gated rheostat on neutrophil phagocytosis
records.abstract: Neutrophils are essential frontline immune cells in the defence against bacterial pathogens such as  Staphylococcus aureus , but their killing machinery also causes host tissue damage. How neutrophils regulate these processes remains incompletely understood. Here, we profiled the proteome and phosphoproteome of human neutrophils across a two-hour exposure to  S. aureus , alongside five simultaneous functional readouts, before investigating how an initial encounter modulates the response to a second. The phosphoproteomic response resolved into qualitatively distinct early and late windows: the early landscape drives particle uptake, while by the late window this machinery is deactivated, with a broadly supressed kinome, and cells geared towards inflammatory output. Correlating protein phosphorylation and functional kinetics — an approach we term KINETIC — implicates putative mediators of key neutrophil antimicrobial functions. A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in neutrophil-like PLB-985 cells, sorted on phagocytic load, recovered canonical engulfment machinery among the strongest facilitators of phagocytosis, additionally identifying the lysosomal Ragulator-mTORC1 nutrient sensing pathway and HOPS complex corresponding to the KINETIC-identified pathways. Conversely, the NRF2 repressor KEAP1 was the strongest phagocytic brake, positioning oxidative burden as a regulator of phagocytic appetite. Neutrophils in the late window exhibited impaired phagocytosis and phagosomal acidification on  S.aureus re-challenge. Underlying these functional deficits, cells in the late window were refractory across multiomic layers: a second  S. aureus meal altered no phosphoprotein, protein, or transcript, whereas the chemoattractants PAF and fMLP evoked a largely consistent phosphoproteomic programme, delineating the phenotype as receptor-specific rather than a global loss of signalling capacity. Consistent with de-repressing the antioxidant response via genetic loss of KEAP1 increasing phagocytosis, reducing ROS production via inhibition of the NADPH oxidase resulted in a partial rescue of phagocytosis of the re-exposed  S.aureus . Together, these findings describe a ROS-gated phagocytic rheostat, enabling neutrophils to meter their phagocytic appetite according to their exposure history, likely limiting uptake of pathogens they lack the capacity to effectively digest. Inappropriate activation of this rheostat under conditions of physiological stress or severe illness may underpin the defects in phagocytosis identified in such patients.

records.title: A novel lineage of  Chilomastix mesnili  in wild Moroccan Barbary macaques (  Macaca sylvanus  )
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Chilomastix spp. are flagellated protists found in the intestines of a broad range of hosts. They are generally non-pathogenic and have been little studied, especially using molecular techniques, and significant taxonomic uncertainty regarding the host specificity of lineages remains. As part of a study of intestinal microbial communities of wild Barbary macaques (  Macaca sylvanus ) from Morocco, we mined 50 faecal metagenomic sequence libraries and found 11 rRNA sequences matching  Chilomastix . Compared to published 18S rRNA sequences, the Barbary macaque  Chilomastix sequences formed a well-supported clade distinct from human-derived  C. mesnili ST1 from Indonesia. The macaque  Chilomastix sequences cluster with a single pig-derived isolate and two sequences from Japanese macaques (  Macaca fuscata ). This indicates that  M. sylvanus harbours a lineage of  Chilomastix distinct from the common human strain of  C. mesnili and geographically widespread. We were also able to reconstruct the complete rDNA operon from this lineage.

records.title: Sequence-structured fitness landscapes predict influenza evolution
records.abstract: Seasonal influenza viruses continually evolve to evade host immunity. Vaccines must be regularly updated to protect against new circulating strains, motivating efforts to forecast viral evolution. Recent experimental and computational methods have made progress on this problem, but learning the fitness landscape driving viral evolution remains challenging because genomic surveillance samples only a small fraction of the possible sequence space. Here, we developed a generative framework that shares information across genetically related variants, inferring effective mutation-level contributions to viral fitness from temporal sequence data. Applied to hemagglutinin and neuraminidase from A/H3N2 and A/H1N1 viruses, the inferred fitness landscapes recovers known determinants of antigenicity and reveals convergent spatial organization across subtypes consistent with common antibody-mediated selection. Forward simulations from these landscapes predicted both the fixation or loss of circulating mutations and the future composition of viral populations, outperforming models based on neutral evolution or multinomial-logistic growth. Collectively, our results show that interpretable representations of pathogen fitness landscapes can reveal biologically important features and improve prospective evolutionary forecasting.
records.authors: Rodríguez-Horta E, Barton JP.

records.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling reveals early responses of tomato plants elicited by compost-derived bacteria
records.abstract: Compost produced from biowaste has a defined microbiota, and some bacterial species may represent promising resources for low-input crop systems. However, their effects on plant physiology are poorly investigated and remain difficult to predict from standard bacterial traits alone. We isolated several bacterial strains (  Bacillus sonorensis, Glutamicibacter arilaitensis, and  Kocuria rhizophila ) from biowaste compost and examined their early effects on tomato seedlings under controlled in vitro conditions. Responses were assessed by root phenotyping, root and shoot transcriptomics, and mass spectrometry-based profiling of primary metabolites in plant tissues, root exudates and bacterial culture filtrates.  B. sonorensis induces the broadest response, reducing primary root length and lateral root number and density and triggering broad transcriptional changes related to metabolism, redox balance, hormone signalling and defence-associated pathways.  G. arilaitensis elicits a more selective, tissue-dependent response, whereas  K. rhizophila has limited phenotypic and transcriptional effects at this stage. All isolates reshape primary metabolism, with recurrent effects on amino acid-, carbohydrate- and lipid-related pathways, together with isolate-specific changes in root exudate composition. This study characterises the early molecular and metabolic responses of tomato to compost-derived bacteria and identifies common and strain-specific physiological signatures that provide a foundation for future studies under biotic and abiotic stress.
records.authors: Ghirardello G, Araniti F, Cipriani R, Zanardi W, Bonato T, Baldan B, Nigris S.

records.title: Infection-Induced SRSF2 Downregulation Drives VEGF-A Isoform Switching to Impair Angiogenesis in Diabetic Foot Ulcers
records.abstract: Abstract    Background:  Impaired vascular repair and infection contribute to delayed healing in diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). Whether infection-associated inflammatory stress affects endothelial function through altered RNA processing remains incompletely understood. We investigated SRSF2 and VEGFA isoform regulation in this setting. Human DFU tissues and microbiota were assessed across Wagner grades, and bacterial inoculation was examined in a diabetic mouse wound model. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were exposed to high glucose (HG) with or without lipopolysaccharide (LPS). SRSF2 was manipulated to assess scratch closure, EdU incorporation, and tube formation. Knockdown RNA sequencing was performed separately in HMEC-1 cells. Isoform-directed RT-qPCR, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP)-qPCR, and a dual-fluorescence VEGFA minigene reporter were used to examine RNA regulation in HUVECs.  Results:  Higher Wagner grades were associated with lower granulation tissue and CD31-positive areas and differences in microbial composition. In diabetic mice, bacterial inoculation delayed wound closure and was accompanied by reduced vascularization and endothelial SRSF2 staining. HG+LPS reduced SRSF2 expression and impaired endothelial functional readouts. SRSF2 knockdown reproduced these defects, whereas overexpression partially improved them under HG+LPS. Transcriptomic analysis identified widespread splicing changes after SRSF2 depletion. Under HG+LPS, RT-qPCR showed lower VEGFA-165a and higher VEGFA-165b signals; SRSF2 overexpression partially reversed these changes. The minigene reporter shifted toward VEGF-A165b-associated output under HG+LPS or SRSF2 knockdown and toward VEGF-A165a-associated output following SRSF2 overexpression. VEGFA pre-mRNA was enriched in SRSF2 immunoprecipitates.  Conclusions:  SRSF2 contributes to endothelial angiogenic function under hyperglycemic and LPS stress, and its manipulation alters VEGFA isoform-associated readouts. These findings support a potential role for SRSF2-associated RNA processing in diabetic wound vascular dysfunction. They do not establish that VEGFA isoform switching mediates the functional effects of SRSF2 or that the same mechanism operates in human DFUs.

records.title: Rhizobacterial genetic diversity associated with Paspalum atratum and Paspalum notatum by metagenomic analysis
records.abstract: Abstract    The genus  Paspalum  belongs to the Poaceae family and encompasses several species native to South America. The  Paspalum  Germplasm Bank of Embrapa Pecuária Sudeste has about 450 accessions of 50 species. Among the conserved accessions,  Paspalum notatum  BGP 26 and  Paspalum atratum  BGP 308 were selected for their importance as turfgrass and forage, respectively. The rhizospheric bacterial community of  P. atratum  and  P. notatum  was analyzed via 16S (V3-V4 region) metabarcoding sequencing. The statistical difference found for the Chao ecological index indicates that the bacterial composition and diversity were associated with each species. Thirty-one operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified with a predominance higher than 1% from 9 phyla (Proteobacteria n = 11, Acidobacteria n = 8, Actinobacteria n = 3, Planctomycetes n = 2, Nitrospirae n = 2, Verrucomicrobia n = 2, Chloroflexi n = 1, Gemmatimonadetes n = 1, and Bacteroidetes n = 1). Among these, 19 OTUs significantly differed between the species studied. Soil hydrogen-ionic potential (pH) was one of the most important factors influencing the species-specific difference of bacterial populations among accessions. Acidobacteriaceae (Subgroup 1), from the phylum Acidobacteria, was the most abundant family in  P. atratum  . The main group found in  P. notatum  was related to the family Nitrosomonadaceae from the phylum Proteobacteria. Our findings highlight a significant distinction in the rhizospheric bacterial community among the examined  Paspalum  accessions and underscore the existence of a species-specific association. These results can aid soil management practices, particularly in relation to vital economic aspects. Further research could help optimize agricultural strategies and promote sustainable soil health.
